knowledge_statements.title: Complicating-Variable Partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the variable partition that exposes conditionally independent logic-based Benders subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider an optimization problem 
\[\min\{f(x,y): (x,y)\in F\},\]
with variables partitioned as master variables \(x\in X\) and residual variables \(y\in Y\). The set \(x\) is a complicating-variable set if fixing any \(\bar x\in X\) reduces the residual problem to 
\[Q(\bar x)=\inf\{f(\bar x,y):(\bar x,y)\in F\},\]
which belongs to a designated tractable class or decomposes into mutually independent subproblems. The associated complicating-variable partition places \(x\) in the master problem and represents the effect of the residual value function \(Q\) through valid logic-based Benders cuts or bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complicating-variable partition assigns variables to the master when fixing them makes the remaining optimization tractable or separable, with residual costs represented by Benders cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\times Y\) is the feasible set.
\(Q(x)\) is well-defined in the extended reals for every master-feasible \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) forms a valid complicating-variable master interface whenever fixing \(x\) yields the prescribed tractable or separable residual problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Assignment–Recourse Partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite assignment decisions form the master; operational recourse is evaluated after assignments are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a\in A\subseteq\{0,1\}^{I\times J}\) encode assignments and let \(y\) denote recourse decisions. An assignment–recourse partition represents the problem as 
\[\min_{a\in A}\left\{c(a)+Q(a)\right\},\qquad Q(a)=\inf_{y}\{q(a,y):(a,y)\in F\}.\]
The master contains \(a\), the assignment constraints defining \(A\), and a variable \(\theta\) estimating \(Q(a)\). For a fixed assignment \(\bar a\), the subproblem optimizes \(y\); its infeasibility or optimal value supplies a valid feasibility or optimality cut in \((a,\theta)\)-space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary assignments are chosen in the master, while a conditional operational problem evaluates feasibility and recourse cost and returns cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(A\subseteq\{0,1\}^{I\times J}\) contains all master-feasible assignments.
\(Q(a)\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) for each \(a\in A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{a\in A}\{c(a)+Q(a)\}\) is represented by an assignment master coupled to conditional recourse subproblems.

notation.meaning: indicator that item i is assigned to option j

knowledge_statements.title: Planning–Scheduling Partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strategic or tactical plans are master decisions; detailed scheduling is the conditional subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\in P\) describe aggregate planning decisions and let \(s\in S(p)\) describe a detailed schedule compatible with \(p\). A planning–scheduling partition has the value-function form 
\[\min_{p\in P}\left\{C(p)+Q(p)\right\},\qquad Q(p)=\inf_{s\in S(p)}D(p,s).\]
The master enforces planning constraints and carries an estimate \(\theta\) of \(Q(p)\). After fixing \(\bar p\), the scheduling subproblem either constructs a feasible schedule and evaluates \(Q(\bar p)\), or establishes that \(S(\bar p)=\varnothing\); the resulting inference is expressed as an optimality or feasibility cut on master plans.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master chooses aggregate plans; a detailed scheduling subproblem tests implementability and cost, returning cuts that exclude or price plans.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the set of master-feasible plans.
\(S(p)\) contains exactly the schedules compatible with plan \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The integrated planning–scheduling optimum equals \(\inf_{p\in P}\{C(p)+Q(p)\}\), with scheduling information communicated through valid master cuts.

notation.meaning: optimal scheduling value, with infeasibility represented by positive infinity

children.title: Scenario-Indexed Partitions
children.top_down_role: Partition structures organized by scenario-indexed uncertainty or recourse components.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Indexed Partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A shared master decision induces one conditionally independent recourse problem per scenario.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite scenario set \(\Omega\), probabilities \(\pi_\omega>0\), and shared decision \(x\in X\), a scenario-indexed partition represents 
\[\min_{x\in X}\left\{c(x)+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}\pi_\omega Q_\omega(x)\right\},\qquad Q_\omega(x)=\inf_{y_\omega\in Y_\omega(x)}q_\omega(x,y_\omega).\]
Fixing \(x=\bar x\) leaves separate subproblems indexed by \(\omega\), because neither the feasible set nor objective of one scenario contains another scenario's recourse variables. Each scenario may therefore return its own feasibility or value cut, or their valid weighted aggregate may be added to the master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common decision is fixed in the master, producing independent recourse subproblems for scenarios whose weighted values determine total recourse.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) is finite and \(\pi_\omega>0\) with \(\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}\pi_\omega=1\).
Conditional on \(x\), recourse variables and constraints are scenario-separable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recourse value is \(Q(x)=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}\pi_\omega Q_\omega(x)\), and all scenario subproblems can be solved independently for fixed \(x\).

notation.meaning: probability or normalized weight of scenario omega

children.title: Block-Structured Partitions
children.top_down_role: Partition structures organized by separable model blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Structured Partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixing linking variables separates the residual model into independently optimized blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in X\) be linking variables and let \(y_b\in Y_b(x)\) be variables of blocks \(b\in B\). A block-structured partition has the form 
\[\min_{x\in X}\left\{c(x)+\sum_{b\in B}Q_b(x)\right\},\qquad Q_b(x)=\inf_{y_b\in Y_b(x)}q_b(x,y_b).\]
For fixed \(\bar x\), no constraint or objective term couples \(y_b\) with \(y_{b'}\) when \(b\ne b'\). Consequently, each \(Q_b(\bar x)\) is computed independently, while the master contains \(x\), its linking constraints, and epigraph variables or cuts representing the block values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linking variables remain in the master; after they are fixed, disjoint variable blocks yield independent value functions and cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a finite block index set.
All cross-block interactions are represented through \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed \(x\), the residual value separates as \(Q(x)=\sum_{b\in B}Q_b(x)\).

notation.meaning: conditional optimal value of block b

children.title: Scenario–Block Coupling Patterns
children.top_down_role: Coupling regimes linking scenario indices to block boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario–Block Coupling Patterns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when scenario and block indexing yields full, partial, or no conditional separability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let residual components be indexed by vertices \(V\subseteq\Omega\times B\), and form a coupling graph \(G_x=(V,E_x)\) after fixing master variables \(x\). Join two vertices when their residual variables occur together in a constraint or nonseparable objective term. The residual problem decomposes exactly over the connected components \(C\) of \(G_x\): 
\[Q(x)=\sum_{C\in\mathcal C(G_x)}Q_C(x).\]
Thus an edgeless graph gives independent scenario–block subproblems, edges only within scenarios give scenario-indexed subproblems, edges only within blocks give block-indexed subproblems, and general edges produce larger coupled components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional coupling graph determines decomposition granularity: each connected component is one subproblem, while its edge pattern distinguishes scenario and block separability.
assumptions_latex: The residual objective is additive across uncoupled components.
Every residual cross-component constraint or nonseparable term induces an edge in \(G_x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maximal conditionally independent subproblems are indexed by \(\mathcal C(G_x)\), the connected components of the coupling graph.

notation.meaning: residual coupling graph after fixing master variables
connected components of the coupling graph

children.title: Assignment Master Representations
children.top_down_role: Master representations centered on assignment decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Assignment Master Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary assignment variables and recourse-value surrogates constitute the logic-based Benders master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate assignment of item \(i\in I\) to option \(j\in J\), and let \(A\) encode admissible assignments. An assignment master is represented by 
\[\min\left\{\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J}c_{ij}a_{ij}+\theta:a\in A,\ \theta\ge L,\ (a,\theta)\in\bigcap_{k\in K}\mathcal B_k\right\}.\]
Here each \(\mathcal B_k\) is a valid logic-based Benders feasibility or optimality restriction derived from a previously evaluated assignment. Initially \(K\) may be empty; subsequent cuts tighten the master without removing any assignment whose true recourse value is finite and correctly represented.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The assignment master optimizes binary assignment costs plus a recourse estimate, subject to assignment rules and accumulated valid Benders cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(J\) are finite.
\(L\) is a valid lower bound on recourse cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed model is a valid relaxation of the assignment–recourse problem whenever every \(\mathcal B_k\) is valid for the recourse epigraph.

notation.meaning: valid Benders restriction generated at iteration k

children.title: Selection Master Representations
children.top_down_role: Master representations centered on selection decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection Master Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary activation choices form the master interface to conditional operational subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_j\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether option \(j\in J\) is selected, and let \(Z\) contain the admissible selections. A selection master has the representation 
\[\min\left\{\sum_{j\in J}f_jz_j+\theta:z\in Z,\ \theta\ge L,\ (z,\theta)\in\bigcap_{k\in K}\mathcal B_k\right\}.\]
The subproblem is conditioned on a selected set \(\{j:z_j=1\}\). Each \(\mathcal B_k\) is a valid feasibility restriction on selections or an optimality restriction lower-bounding their recourse value. The master is a relaxation when its accumulated restrictions contain the epigraph of the true selection-dependent value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The selection master chooses activated options and a recourse estimate, then accumulates valid cuts obtained from operational subproblems.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite and \(Z\subseteq\{0,1\}^{J}\).
\(L\) is a valid global lower bound on recourse value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The master feasible region contains \(\{(z,\theta):z\in Z,\ \theta\ge Q(z)\}\) whenever all accumulated restrictions are valid.

children.title: Coupled Assignment–Selection Masters
children.top_down_role: Master structures coupling assignment choices with selection choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Assignment–Selection Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection activates admissible assignment columns, coupling both decision families in one master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_j\in\{0,1\}\) select option \(j\), and let \(a_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) assign item \(i\) to option \(j\). A coupled assignment–selection master is 
\[\min\left\{\sum_j f_jz_j+\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}a_{ij}+\theta:(a,z)\in M,\ \theta\ge L,\ (a,z,\theta)\in\bigcap_{k\in K}\mathcal B_k\right\},\]
where \(M\) includes linking conditions such as \(a_{ij}\le z_j\) and assignment requirements such as \(\sum_j a_{ij}=1\). Each \(\mathcal B_k\) is valid for the epigraph or effective domain of the recourse value \(Q(a,z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled master jointly selects options and assigns items, enforces activation links, and represents conditional recourse through a surrogate and valid cuts.
assumptions_latex: The index sets are finite.
\(M\) contains all required assignment, selection, and linking constraints.
\(L\le Q(a,z)\) for every master-feasible \((a,z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation is a valid master relaxation of \(\min_{(a,z)\in M}\{f^\top z+c^\top a+Q(a,z)\}\).

notation.meaning: recourse value conditional on assignments and selections

children.title: Planning Master Representations
children.top_down_role: Master representations for planning-level decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Planning Master Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate planning variables and recourse surrogates define the master passed to detailed operational subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\in P\) denote aggregate capacity, quantity, timing, or resource-allocation decisions, and let \(Q(p)\) be the optimal value of the detailed problem conditioned on \(p\). A planning master is represented as 
\[\min\left\{C(p)+\theta:p\in P,\ \theta\ge L,\ (p,\theta)\in\bigcap_{k\in K}\mathcal B_k\right\}.\]
Each \(\mathcal B_k\) is a valid feasibility or optimality restriction inferred from evaluating a prior plan. The formulation remains a relaxation provided every feasible epigraph point \((p,\theta)\), with \(\theta\ge Q(p)\), satisfies all accumulated restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The planning master chooses aggregate resource and timing decisions while cuts progressively represent feasibility and value of detailed operations.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) contains exactly the aggregate master-feasible plans.
\(L\le Q(p)\) for every \(p\in P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed master is a valid relaxation of \(\min_{p\in P}\{C(p)+Q(p)\}\) under valid accumulated cuts.

children.title: Design Master Representations
children.top_down_role: Master representations for design-level decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Design Master Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete or strategic design choices form the master interface to conditional operation models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d\in D\) denote design decisions, such as capacities, configurations, or facility activations, and let \(Q(d)\) be the optimal conditional operating value. A design master has the form 
\[\min\left\{F(d)+\theta:d\in D,\ \theta\ge L,\ (d,\theta)\in\bigcap_{k\in K}\mathcal B_k\right\}.\]
The set \(D\) enforces design-only restrictions. Every \(\mathcal B_k\) must be valid for the effective domain or epigraph of \(Q\), so infeasible designs may be removed and feasible designs may receive progressively stronger operating-cost lower bounds without excluding any true epigraph point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The design master chooses capacities or configurations and uses valid cuts to represent whether each design can operate and at what cost.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is the master-feasible design set.
\(Q(d)\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(L\le Q(d)\) for all \(d\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation is a valid relaxation of \(\min_{d\in D}\{F(d)+Q(d)\}\) whenever all \(\mathcal B_k\) are valid.

children.title: Planning–Design Coupling
children.top_down_role: Structural links between planning choices and design choices in the master.

knowledge_statements.title: Planning–Design Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the master-level compatibility condition linking plans to installed or selected designs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\in P\) be planning decisions and \(d\in D\) be design decisions. A planning–design master coupling is a relation \(R\subseteq P\times D\) such that 
\[(p,d)\in R\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad H(p,d)\le 0,\quad E(p,d)=0,\]
for specified master-checkable compatibility maps \(H\) and \(E\). The coupled master domain is \(M=(P\times D)\cap R\), and its conditional value formulation is 
\[\min_{(p,d)\in M}\{C(p)+F(d)+Q(p,d)\}.\]
All compatibility restrictions needed before solving the operational subproblem must be included in \(R\); remaining operational dependence is represented by \(Q(p,d)\) and valid Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plans and designs are jointly master-feasible exactly when they satisfy explicit compatibility constraints; operational consequences remain in a conditional value function.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and \(D\) are the uncoupled planning and design domains.
\(H\) and \(E\) are evaluable using master variables alone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The valid coupled master domain is \(M=\{(p,d)\in P\times D:H(p,d)\le0,\ E(p,d)=0\}\).

notation.meaning: operational value conditional on plan and design

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a master domain, let \(c:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and define the subordinate value function by \(Q(x)=\inf\{f(x,y):y\in Y(x)\}\), using \(Q(x)=+\infty\) when \(Y(x)=\varnothing\). An exact value-function master is \[\inf\{c(x)+\eta:x\in X,\ \eta\ge Q(x)\}.\] Its feasible set is precisely \(\operatorname{epi}_X Q=\{(x,\eta)\in X\times\mathbb{R}:\eta\ge Q(x)\}\). Consequently, whenever the infimum is attained, its optimal master assignments and objective value equal those of \(\inf_{x\in X}\{c(x)+Q(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact master uses the true subordinate value function as an epigraph constraint, giving the same optimal assignments and value as the undecomposed minimization problem.

children.title: Surrogate-Value Masters
children.top_down_role: Master representations using proxy subproblem values.

knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate-Value Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-surrogate representation for minimization masters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a master domain, let \(c:X\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(Q:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the exact subordinate value function, and let \(S:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfy \(S(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). The surrogate-value master is \[\inf\{c(x)+\eta:x\in X,\ \eta\ge S(x)\}.\] It is a relaxation of the exact value-function master and therefore supplies a valid lower bound for minimization. If a surrogate-optimal assignment \(x^*\in X\) exists and satisfies \(S(x^*)=Q(x^*)<+\infty\), then \(x^*\) is optimal for the exact master and the two optimal values coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surrogate master replaces the exact subordinate value by a pointwise lower estimator. It gives a lower bound and is exact when the estimator equals the true value at a surrogate-optimal assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the master domain and \(c:X\to\mathbb{R}\).
\(Q:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is the exact subordinate value function.
\(S:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfies \(S(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf_{x\in X}\{c(x)+S(x)\}\le \inf_{x\in X}\{c(x)+Q(x)\}.\]

notation.meaning: Surrogate subordinate-value function used by the master.
Epigraph variable for the surrogate value.

children.title: Surrogate Fidelity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes distinguished by the accuracy and conservatism of surrogate values.

knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Fidelity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three fidelity predicates for minimization surrogates: lower-valid, incumbent-exact, and globally exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a master domain, let \(c:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(Q,S:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the exact and surrogate value functions. Define \(v_Q=\inf_{x\in X}\{c(x)+Q(x)\}\) and \(v_S=\inf_{x\in X}\{c(x)+S(x)\}\). Lower-valid fidelity means \(S(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), and it implies \(v_S\le v_Q\). Incumbent fidelity at \(\bar x\in X\) means \(S(\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\). If \(S\) is lower-valid, \(\bar x\) is surrogate-optimal, and \(S(\bar x)=Q(\bar x)<+\infty\), then \(\bar x\) is exact-master optimal and \(v_S=v_Q\). Global exact fidelity means \(S(x)=Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), in which case the surrogate and exact epigraph masters are identical.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise lower surrogate gives a lower bound. Equality with the true value at a surrogate optimum certifies exact optimality, while equality everywhere makes the surrogate and exact masters identical.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the master domain and \(c:X\to\mathbb{R}\).
\(Q,S:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) are respectively the exact and surrogate value functions.
The formulation is in minimization form.

knowledge_statements.title: Initial Master Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initial lower-bounding master before oracle-generated cuts are added.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a master domain, let \(c:X\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(Q:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the subordinate value function, and set \(D=\{x\in X:Q(x)<+\infty\}\). Choose \(X_0\) with \(D\subseteq X_0\subseteq X\) and \(L:X_0\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\) satisfying \(L(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). The initial master relaxation is \[\inf\{c(x)+\eta:x\in X_0,\ \eta\ge L(x)\}.\] Its value is a lower bound on \(\inf_{x\in D}\{c(x)+Q(x)\}\). Valid feasibility cuts may subsequently shrink the permitted master set, while valid optimality cuts may raise the enforced lower estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An initial master uses an outer approximation of feasible assignments and a lower estimate of subordinate cost, producing a lower bound that valid cuts can tighten.

\(D=\{x\in X:Q(x)<+\infty\}\) is the projected feasible master set.
\(D\subseteq X_0\subseteq X\) and \(L(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in D\).

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Subproblem Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite additive decomposition into conditionally independent subordinate blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a nonempty finite index set and \(X\) a master domain. For each \(x\in X\), suppose the subordinate feasible region is \(\prod_{i\in I}Y_i(x)\) and the objective is \(\sum_{i\in I}f_i(x,y_i)\). Define \(Q_i(x)=\inf\{f_i(x,y_i):y_i\in Y_i(x)\}\), using \(+\infty\) when \(Y_i(x)=\varnothing\), and assume \(Q_i(x)>-\infty\) for every \(i\in I\). Then \[Q(x)=\inf_{y_i\in Y_i(x),\ i\in I}\sum_{i\in I}f_i(x,y_i)=\sum_{i\in I}Q_i(x).\] Thus the blocks may be evaluated independently, and valid blockwise lower bounds aggregate by summation into a valid lower bound on \(Q(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many conditionally independent blocks with an additive objective and no value equal to negative infinity, the total subordinate value is the sum of the independently computed block values.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a nonempty finite index set.
For each \(x\in X\), the subordinate feasible set is \(\prod_{i\in I}Y_i(x)\) and its objective is additive across \(I\).
Each block value \(Q_i(x)\) belongs to \(\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Q(x)=\sum_{i\in I}Q_i(x).\]

notation.meaning: Nonempty finite index set of subordinate blocks.

children.title: Hierarchical Subproblem Decompositions
children.top_down_role: Subproblem organizations with explicit levels of authority or resolution.

assumptions_latex: The hierarchy is a finite rooted tree \(T=(V,E)\).
Each node communicates with its parent only through a declared interface state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Q_r(z_r)=\inf_{y_r\in Y_r(z_r)}\left\{f_r(z_r,y_r)+\sum_{u\in\operatorname{ch}(r)}Q_u(T_{ru}(z_r,y_r))\right\}.\]

notation.meaning: Finite rooted hierarchy with root node \(r\).
Optimal downstream value rooted at node \(v\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive value representation over a finite rooted subproblem tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=(V,E)\) be a finite rooted tree. For every node \(v\), let \(z_v\) be its incoming interface state, \(y_v\in Y_v(z_v)\) its local decision, and \(T_{vu}(z_v,y_v)\) the state passed to child \(u\in\operatorname{ch}(v)\). Define recursively \[Q_v(z_v)=\inf_{y_v\in Y_v(z_v)}\left\{f_v(z_v,y_v)+\sum_{u\in\operatorname{ch}(v)}Q_u(T_{vu}(z_v,y_v))\right\}.\] For leaves the sum is zero. The root value \(Q_r(z_r)\) equals the hierarchical subordinate value when the declared interfaces preserve every cross-level dependency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hierarchical decomposition recursively combines each node's local cost with child value functions. It is exact when interface states retain every dependency crossing a hierarchy edge.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive tree formulation is plausible, but no source or locator supports its exactness condition or its placement specifically within logic-based Benders decomposition.

children.title: Nested Subproblem Chains
children.top_down_role: Subproblem organizations embedded recursively across decomposition levels.

assumptions_latex: There are finitely many levels \(1,\ldots,L\).
Each level passes a state to the next level through \(T_\ell\).

notation.meaning: Number of levels in the nested chain.
Value function for the suffix beginning at level \(\ell\).
State transition from level \(\ell\) to level \(\ell+1\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path-shaped specialization of a hierarchical subordinate decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For levels \(\ell=1,\ldots,L\), let \(z_\ell\) be the incoming state and \(y_\ell\in Y_\ell(z_\ell)\) the local decision. Set \(Q_{L+1}\equiv0\) and recursively define \[Q_\ell(z_\ell)=\inf_{y_\ell\in Y_\ell(z_\ell)}\{f_\ell(z_\ell,y_\ell)+Q_{\ell+1}(T_\ell(z_\ell,y_\ell))\}.\] This is a nested subproblem chain: each level has at most one subordinate child. The representation is exact when all effects of earlier levels on the remaining suffix are mediated by the transmitted state \(z_{\ell+1}=T_\ell(z_\ell,y_\ell)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested chain recursively passes one interface state from each level to the next and adds the current cost to the downstream optimal value.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Subproblem Chains

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The path-shaped recursion is mathematically plausible, but the record has no cited evidence for the nested formulation or the asserted interface-mediated exactness condition.

children.title: Cross-Level Coordination Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Information interfaces connecting adjacent subproblem levels.

assumptions_latex: A decomposition edge separates upstream data \(u\) from downstream decisions \(w\).
The transmitted interface is \(z=T(u)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[T(u)=T(u')\Longrightarrow\bigl(Y_{\mathrm{down}}(u)=Y_{\mathrm{down}}(u')\ \land\ f_{\mathrm{down}}(u,w)=f_{\mathrm{down}}(u',w)\bigr).\]

notation.meaning: Upstream state and decisions relevant at a hierarchy edge.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficiency condition for an exact interface across one hierarchy edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an edge separating upstream information \(u\) from a downstream subproblem with feasible set \(Y_{\mathrm{down}}(u)\) and objective \(f_{\mathrm{down}}(u,w)\). A map \(T\) is an exact cross-level coordination interface if, whenever \(T(u)=T(u')\), \[Y_{\mathrm{down}}(u)=Y_{\mathrm{down}}(u')\quad\text{and}\quad f_{\mathrm{down}}(u,w)=f_{\mathrm{down}}(u',w)\ \text{for every feasible }w.\] Under this condition the downstream value depends on upstream information only through \(z=T(u)\), so cuts, bounds, and feasibility messages indexed by \(z\) remain valid across that edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interface is exact when equal transmitted states induce identical downstream feasible sets and costs, making the downstream value independent of all omitted upstream information.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Level Coordination Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed interface condition is a strong sufficient condition, but no source is supplied to establish this as the intended cross-level coordination notion or to support the claims about reusable cuts and messages.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Indexed Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite expected-value decomposition with scenario independence conditional on the master assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a master domain and let \(\Omega\) be a nonempty finite scenario set with \(p_\omega>0\) and \(\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega=1\). For fixed \(x\in X\), define \(Q_\omega(x)=\inf\{f_\omega(x,y_\omega):y_\omega\in Y_\omega(x)\}\), using \(+\infty\) for an empty feasible set, and assume \(Q_\omega(x)>-\infty\) for every \(\omega\in\Omega\). If scenario decisions and constraints are conditionally independent given \(x\), then the expected subordinate value is \[Q(x)=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q_\omega(x).\] The scenarios may therefore be evaluated separately. If any positive-probability scenario is infeasible, then \(Q(x)=+\infty\); otherwise weighted scenario lower bounds aggregate into a valid lower bound on \(Q(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many conditionally independent scenarios whose values are not negative infinity, the expected subordinate value is the probability-weighted sum of the independently evaluated scenario values.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the master domain.
\(\Omega\) is a nonempty finite scenario set with \(p_\omega>0\) and \(\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega=1\).
Scenario decisions and constraints are conditionally independent given \(x\), and \(Q_\omega(x)\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) for every \(\omega\in\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Q(x)=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega Q_\omega(x).\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty master-assignment domain. For each \(x\in X\), let \(F(x)\) be the feasible set of a minimization subproblem with objective \(f_x\), and define \(v(x)=\inf\{f_x(y):y\in F(x)\}\), using \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Let \(\widehat F(x)\supseteq F(x)\) and let \(\widehat f_x\) satisfy \(\widehat f_x(y)\le f_x(y)\) for every \(y\in F(x)\). If the relaxed infimum is not \(-\infty\), the relaxation oracle returns \(\mathcal R(x)=\inf\{\widehat f_x(y):y\in\widehat F(x)\}\). Then \(\mathcal R(x)\le v(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). If \(\widehat F(x)=\varnothing\), then \(F(x)=\varnothing\), so \(\mathcal R(x)=v(x)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation oracle minimizes a relaxed objective over a feasible-set relaxation and returns a lower bound on the original minimization value. If the relaxed feasible set is empty, the original subproblem is also infeasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a certified lower-bound oracle for LBBD minimization subproblems, independently of how the bound is computed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the value function of a minimization subproblem. A bound oracle returns, for a queried \(x\in X\), a value \(L(x)\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) together with a validity assertion satisfying \(L(x)\le v(x)\). If it additionally returns a function \(\ell_x:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) such that \(\ell_x(z)\le v(z)\) for every \(z\in X\), then the master inequality \(\theta\ge\ell_x(z)\) is globally valid. Equality at the query, \(\ell_x(x)=v(x)\), makes the generated bound supporting at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound oracle certifies a lower bound at a query and may export a globally valid lower-bounding function as an LBBD master cut.
assumptions_latex: The subproblem is minimized.
\(\theta\) represents a master lower approximation to the subproblem value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle response satisfies \(L(x)\le v(x)\), and any exported \(\ell_x\) yields the valid inequality \(\theta\ge\ell_x(z)\).

notation.meaning: Globally valid lower-bounding function generated at x.

children.title: Oracle Tightness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Interface regimes distinguished by bound strength and relaxation fidelity.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Tightness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies lower-bound oracles by exact, additive, or multiplicative approximation guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a value function \(v:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) and a lower-bound oracle \(L\le v\), define three tightness regimes on \(D\subseteq X\). The oracle is exact on \(D\) when \(L(x)=v(x)\) for all \(x\in D\). It is additively \(\varepsilon\)-tight when \(0\le v(x)-L(x)\le\varepsilon\) for all \(x\in D\). If \(v(x)\ge0\) on \(D\), it is multiplicatively \(\rho\)-tight, for \(\rho\in(0,1]\), when \(\rho v(x)\le L(x)\le v(x)\) for all \(x\in D\). Exactness is the special case \(\varepsilon=0\) or \(\rho=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle tightness may be exact, uniformly additive, or—when values are nonnegative—multiplicative over a specified master domain.
assumptions_latex: \(L(x)\le v(x)\) for every \(x\in D\).
For the multiplicative regime, \(v(x)\ge0\) on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact, additive, and multiplicative tightness are characterized respectively by \(L=v\), \(v-L\le\varepsilon\), and \(L\ge\rho v\) on \(D\).

notation.meaning: Domain on which tightness is assessed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally coherent and fits the tightness-regime leaf, including the nonnegativity condition for the stated multiplicative convention. No citation is supplied, however, and the normalization and parameter convention for multiplicative tightness require an inspectable source.

children.title: Explanation Oracles
children.top_down_role: Oracle interfaces returning concise reasons for subproblem outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines explanations of infeasibility or lower bounds in terms of queried master literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(x)\) be the finite set of master literals asserted by an assignment \(x\), and let \(P(B)\) denote the subproblem restricted by assumptions \(B\subseteq A(x)\). An infeasibility explanation oracle returns \(E\subseteq A(x)\) such that \(P(E)\) is infeasible. A bound explanation oracle for a reported value \(b\) returns \(E\subseteq A(x)\) such that every master assignment \(z\) satisfying all literals in \(E\) has \(v(z)\ge b\). The explanation is inclusion-minimal when no proper subset of \(E\) retains the corresponding validity property; minimality is optional, but validity is mandatory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explanation oracle identifies master assumptions sufficient to justify subproblem infeasibility or a lower bound, optionally removing redundant assumptions.
assumptions_latex: Master assignments admit finite literal descriptions.
The subproblem restriction induced by any returned explanation is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned \(E\) logically entails the reported infeasibility or lower-bound conclusion.

notation.meaning: Master literals asserted at assignment x.
Subproblem restricted by explanation literals E.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Explanation Oracles leaf and distinguishes validity from optional inclusion minimality. An authoritative source is needed to support the chosen LBBD explanation semantics and the relationship between restricted subproblems and assignments satisfying the returned literals.

children.title: Proof-Certificate Oracles
children.top_down_role: Oracle interfaces returning transferable proof artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Proof-Certificate Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies machine-checkable certificates supporting oracle claims used by the LBBD master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proof-certificate oracle for a subproblem instance \(P(x)\) returns a claim \(q\), a finite certificate \(c\), and a deterministic checker \(V\). Soundness requires \(V(P(x),q,c)=1\) only if \(q\) is true. For an infeasibility claim, truth means that \(P(x)\) has no feasible solution; for a lower-bound claim \(q=(v(x)\ge b)\), truth means every feasible subproblem solution has objective at least \(b\). Completeness relative to a certificate class means that every true supported claim admits some \(c\) accepted by \(V\). Only accepted claims may generate master constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proof-certificate oracle accompanies each subproblem claim with finite data accepted by a sound deterministic checker before master use.
assumptions_latex: Subproblem instances and claims have finite encodings.
The checker implements the declared certificate semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(P(x),q,c)=1\) certifies the truth of \(q\) under checker soundness.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate content kind fits the terminal container, and soundness is stated correctly. No source is provided for this proof-certificate oracle model or for its class-relative completeness convention.

children.title: Certificate Export Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Representational boundaries for exporting certificates to the master.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Export Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes semantics-preserving serialization of oracle certificates for an independent checker.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a certificate space, \(S\) a finite serialization space, and \(E:C\to S\) an exporter. A certificate export interface consists of \(E\), a decoder \(D:S\rightharpoonup C\), and a checker \(V\). It is semantics-preserving when \(D(E(c))=c\) for every supported \(c\in C\), and safe when malformed \(s\in S\) is rejected whenever \(D(s)\) is undefined. For an instance \(P\) and claim \(q\), exported acceptance is defined by \(V(P,q,D(s))=1\). Soundness requires that exported acceptance imply the truth of \(q\), independently of the producing oracle's internal state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate export interface serializes proofs so an independent decoder and checker preserve valid certificates, reject malformed data, and soundly verify claims.
assumptions_latex: Supported certificates and serialized objects have finite representations.
The checker is independent of unexported oracle state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every supported \(c\), exported verification of \(E(c)\) is equivalent to verification of \(c\), and acceptance implies the claim.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind fits an export-interface leaf, and decoder round-tripping supports the stated verification equivalence. The locally selected serialization, malformed-input, and independent-checker model has no cited specification or authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Dual Inference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States LP-dual inference of globally valid Benders lower-bound cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in X\), consider \(v(x)=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge0\}\). Its dual is \(\max\{\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx):W^{\mathsf T}\pi\le c,\ \pi\ge0\}\). Every dual-feasible \(\pi\) satisfies \(v(x)\ge\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\) by weak duality, so \(\theta\ge\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\) is a globally valid master inequality. If the primal is feasible with finite optimum and the dual is feasible, linear-programming strong duality gives an optimal \(\pi^*\) with \(v(x)=\pi^{*\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\), making the cut exact at the generating assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible LP dual solution yields a valid Benders lower-bound cut; strong duality makes an optimal dual cut exact at its generating assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(W,T,h,c\) are finite-dimensional real data of compatible dimensions.
For exactness, the primal has a finite optimum and the dual is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual feasibility implies \(\theta\ge\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\); under strong-duality hypotheses, equality holds at the generating \(x\) for \(\pi=\pi^*\).

otin D_i\) only when \(P\land A\models z_i
e z\). If propagation detects failure, an explanation is a subset \(E\subseteq A\) satisfying \(P\land E\models ot\). Consequently the master may add the nogood \( igvee_{a\in E}
eg a\). This nogood is valid for every master assignment because no assignment satisfying every literal of \(E\) can extend to a feasible solution of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound CP propagation removes only impossible values; a failure explanation produces a valid master nogood excluding all assignments containing the explaining literals.
assumptions_latex: Master decisions are represented by literals whose conjunction restricts the CP domain store.
Every propagator and explanation procedure is logically sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(P\land E\models\bot\), then \(P\models\bigvee_{a\in E}\neg a\), yielding a valid LBBD nogood.

notation.meaning: Master literals active in the subproblem.

source_refs.source_title: Model Building in Mathematical Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Model Building in Mathematical Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited introductory CP section is not reliably sufficient for explanation-based propagation and LBBD nogood export. In addition, the propagation formula uses \(D_i\) and \(z_i\) without introducing the variable index or its domain. A source covering sound explanations and nogoods is needed before choosing a corrected formalization.

children.title: Satisfiability-Based Inference
children.top_down_role: Inference interfaces grounded in satisfiability reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Satisfiability-Based Inference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses unsatisfiable assumption cores to derive clause-form LBBD feasibility cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a propositional encoding of the subproblem and let \(A(x)\) be the assumption literals supplied by master assignment \(x\). If a SAT oracle establishes that \(F\land\bigwedge_{a\in A(x)}a\) is unsatisfiable and returns an unsatisfiable core \(U\subseteq A(x)\), then \(F\land\bigwedge_{a\in U}a\models\bot\). Equivalently, \(F\models\bigvee_{a\in U}\neg a\). The clause \(\bigvee_{a\in U}\neg a\) is therefore a valid LBBD feasibility cut: it excludes the queried assignment and every other master assignment containing all assumptions in \(U\), while preserving every assignment extendable to a model of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unsatisfiable SAT assumption core yields a valid clause excluding every master assignment that contains all literals in the core.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) soundly represents subproblem feasibility.
Master restrictions are supplied as propositional assumption literals.
The returned core is genuinely unsatisfiable with \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\models\bigvee_{a\in U}\neg a\), so the core clause is a valid LBBD feasibility cut.

notation.meaning: Assumptions induced by master assignment x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unsatisfiable-core implication is mathematically standard, but the record states an inference principle rather than specifying a certificate or checker, so the selected certificate kind does not fit the statement. No authoritative SAT-core or LBBD-interface source is supplied to support a reliable replacement.

children.title: Conflict-Driven Inference
children.top_down_role: Inference interfaces centered on conflicts discovered during search.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Driven Inference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies conflict analysis that learns an entailed clause for the LBBD master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a CNF subproblem \(F\), master assumptions \(A\), and a sound implication graph produced by unit propagation. Initialize the conflict clause \(C\) from a falsified constraint. While \(C\) contains more than one literal assigned at the current decision level, resolve \(C\) with the reason clause of a latest such literal. Stop at an asserting clause or earlier according to a declared resolution policy. Output \(C\), backtrack to the highest remaining assignment level, and retain \(C\). Every resolution step preserves entailment, hence \(F\models C\); if the queried assumptions falsify \(C\), the clause is a valid conflict cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflict analysis resolves reason clauses until obtaining an entailed learned clause, then backtracks and retains that clause as a valid cut.
assumptions_latex: All reason and conflict clauses are entailed by \(F\).
The implication graph records sound unit-propagation reasons.
Resolution is applied only to complementary literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The learned clause \(C\) satisfies \(F\models C\) and excludes the conflicting assumption assignment.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits the leaf, and resolution preserves clause entailment. The instruction to backtrack to the highest remaining assignment level is not a precise CDCL backjump rule and may be incorrect; the asserting level is normally determined from the learned clause. A CDCL source and an LBBD export specification are required before correction.

children.title: Clause-Level Explanation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces transferring clause-level reasons into decomposition information.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause-Level Explanation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the validity and relevance conditions for exporting a clause explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a subproblem formula \(F\), a current master assignment \(x\), and an exported clause \(C= igvee_{i=1}^{k}\ell_i\), a clause-level explanation interface is valid exactly when \(F\models C\). It explains the current failure when additionally \(x\models
eg\ell_i\) for every \(i\), equivalently \(x\models
eg C\). An optional antecedent representation \(E=\{
eg\ell_1,\ldots,
eg\ell_k\}\) must satisfy \(F\land igwedge_{e\in E}e\models ot\). The interface may minimize \(C\), but it must preserve entailment and current-assignment falsification after every deletion or transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exported explanation clause must be entailed by the subproblem and falsified by the current master assignment; optional minimization must preserve both properties.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(C\) use a shared interpretation for exported master literals.
Entailment and assignment evaluation are computed under the same encoding semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exportability requires \(F\models C\); explanation of \(x\) additionally requires \(x\models\neg C\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind fits the interface leaf, and entailment plus falsification are the relevant validity and current-failure conditions. No source specifies the shared interpretation between subproblem and master literals or supports the proposed export and minimization contract.

children.title: Combinatorial Inference
children.top_down_role: Inference based on discrete structure independent of a single application domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Inference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States validity requirements for LBBD bounds derived from problem-specific combinatorial arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a minimization subproblem value function. A combinatorial inference procedure associates with a query \(\bar x\in X\) a tractable function \(L_{\bar x}:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), derived from discrete structure rather than an LP dual, and must certify \(L_{\bar x}(x)\le v(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). The inequality \(\theta\ge L_{\bar x}(x)\) is then a valid master cut. If \(L_{\bar x}(\bar x)=v(\bar x)\), the inference is exact at the query; otherwise it remains valid but may provide only partial separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A combinatorial inference derives a globally valid structural lower bound; equality at the queried assignment makes its master cut locally exact.
assumptions_latex: The original subproblem is minimized.
The structural argument certifies the lower bound over the entire stated master domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\bar x}(x)\le v(x)\) for all \(x\in X\), hence \(\theta\ge L_{\bar x}(x)\) is valid.

notation.meaning: Combinatorial lower-bounding function generated at the query.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle content kind fits the Combinatorial Inference leaf, and a globally certified lower-bounding function would yield the stated master cut. No LBBD source is supplied, and the domain-specific mechanism by which global validity is certified remains unspecified.

children.title: Domain-Specific Inference
children.top_down_role: Inference exploiting specialized knowledge from a problem domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Specific Inference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound inference specialized to an LBBD subproblem domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) be a subproblem domain with admissible models \(\mathcal M_D\), and let \(\Gamma(y)\) denote the facts induced by master assignment \(y\). A domain-specific inference system \(\vdash_D\) is sound when
\[\Gamma\vdash_D\varphi\;\Longrightarrow\;(M\models\Gamma\Rightarrow M\models\varphi)\quad\text{for every }M\in\mathcal M_D.\]
An inferred formula \(\varphi\) is an admissible LBBD consequence only when its master-variable projection is valid for every assignment whose induced facts satisfy \(\Gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Domain-specific inference derives master-valid consequences from subproblem facts using rules sound for every admissible model of that domain.
assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma(y)\) correctly represents the subproblem facts induced by \(y\).
Every rule of \(\vdash_D\) is sound over \(\mathcal M_D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Gamma(y)\vdash_D\varphi\) yields a valid projected LBBD consequence.

notation.meaning: Admissible semantic models of domain D.
Facts induced by master assignment y.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semantic soundness condition is standard and the definition role fits the leaf, but no source is supplied for the LBBD-specific projection claim. The target language and the meaning of a master-variable projection must also be specified before the conclusion can be evaluated reliably.

children.title: Cross-Domain Transfer Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on reusing specialized inference outside its originating problem class.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Domain Transfer Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary for transferring specialized inference rules between domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r:(\Gamma\Rightarrow\varphi)\) be sound over domain models \(\mathcal M_D\), and let \(T\) translate formulas into a second domain \(D'\). The transferred rule is sound over \(\mathcal M_{D'}\) only if
\[M'\models T(\Gamma)\;\Longrightarrow\;M'\models T(\varphi)\quad\text{for every }M'\in\mathcal M_{D'}.\]
Transfer fails whenever a countermodel \(M'\in\mathcal M_{D'}\) satisfies \(T(\Gamma)\) but not \(T(\varphi)\), even though \(r\) is sound in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A specialized rule transfers only when translated premises entail the translated conclusion in every target-domain model; one target countermodel marks the boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(r\) is sound over \(\mathcal M_D\).
\(T\) specifies the intended translation of premises and conclusions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists M'\in\mathcal M_{D'}:M'\models T(\Gamma)\land M'\not\models T(\varphi)\) invalidates the transfer.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The countermodel criterion is mathematically coherent and failure_boundary is appropriate for this leaf, but the record has no citation supporting its use as an LBBD cross-domain transfer boundary.

children.title: Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Representations certifying that a subproblem outcome is infeasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable subproblem certificate supporting an LBBD feasibility cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For master assignment \(y\), let \(F(y)\) be the subproblem constraint set. An infeasibility certificate is a finite object \(\pi\) accepted by a sound verifier \(V_{\mathrm{inf}}\) such that
\[V_{\mathrm{inf}}(F(y),\pi)=1\;\Longrightarrow\;\{z:z\models F(y)\}=\varnothing.\]
If \(A(\pi)\) is the set of master conditions on which the verified derivation depends, then the associated LBBD feasibility cut may exclude every \(y'\) satisfying all conditions in \(A(\pi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite, checkable derivation certifies subproblem infeasibility and identifies master conditions whose simultaneous activation can be excluded.
assumptions_latex: \(V_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is sound for the subproblem inference system.
\(A(\pi)\) contains every master-dependent premise used by \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_{\mathrm{inf}}(F(y),\pi)=1\Rightarrow F(y)\text{ is infeasible}.\)

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the container, but the cited generic Benders section does not directly support the finite-verifier formulation or the certificate-to-cut assertion. Completeness of A(pi) alone does not ensure that every assignment satisfying A(pi) recreates the certificate premises; premise activation and derivation invariance are required.

children.title: Infeasibility Explanations
children.top_down_role: Representations identifying master-relevant causes of infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master-level explanation of a subproblem contradiction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y\) be the master domain and let \(F(y)\) be the subproblem induced by \(y\in Y\). An infeasibility explanation is a finite set \(E\) of master literals or conditions satisfying
\[\forall y'\in Y,\quad y'\models E\;\Longrightarrow\;\{z:z\models F(y')\}=\varnothing.\]
It is minimal when no proper subset \(E'\subsetneq E\) has this property. The clause \(\neg\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\) is then a valid feasibility cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasibility explanation is a set of master conditions whose joint satisfaction makes every corresponding subproblem infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(F(y')\) is defined for every \(y'\in Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\neg\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\) is valid for every master assignment admitting a feasible subproblem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is precise, and its universal condition does imply the stated feasibility cut. However, no source is supplied for this notion as an LBBD infeasibility explanation, so it cannot be accepted as sourced candidate-review knowledge.

children.title: Certificate-to-Explanation Mapping
children.top_down_role: Structural mappings from infeasibility certificates to transferable explanations.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-to-Explanation Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection of a verified infeasibility derivation onto master conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\pi\) be an accepted infeasibility certificate and let \(a(p)\) map each master-dependent premise \(p\) of \(\pi\) to a master condition activating that premise. Define
\[E(\pi)=\{a(p):p\text{ is a master-dependent premise used by }\pi\}.\]
If every \(y'\models E(\pi)\) activates all premises used by \(\pi\), and the certificate rules remain sound for \(F(y')\), then \(E(\pi)\) is an infeasibility explanation and \(\neg\bigwedge_{e\in E(\pi)}e\) is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map each certificate premise to its activating master condition; their collection explains infeasibility when the derivation remains sound under reactivation.
assumptions_latex: The premise-activation map \(a\) is complete for \(\pi\).
Certificate rules are invariant over assignments activating the mapped premises.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E(\pi)\) is an infeasibility explanation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role and conditional mapping are coherent, with the needed activation and invariance assumptions stated. No source is provided for this certificate-to-explanation construction in LBBD.

children.title: Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Representations certifying an optimal subproblem outcome.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable matching-bound certificate for a minimization subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a minimization subproblem with feasible set \(Z(y)\) and objective \(f_y\), an optimality certificate is a triple \((\bar z,L,\pi)\) for which a sound verifier establishes
\[\bar z\in Z(y),\qquad L\le f_y(z)\ \text{for all }z\in Z(y),\qquad f_y(\bar z)=L.\]
Consequently, \(\bar z\) is optimal and the subproblem value is \(v(y)=L\). The derivation \(\pi\) must make both feasibility and the lower bound finitely checkable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible solution and a verified lower bound certify optimality when their objective values coincide.
assumptions_latex: The subproblem is a minimization problem.
The verifier for feasibility and the lower-bound derivation \(\pi\) is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(y)=f_y(\bar z)=L\) and \(\bar z\) is optimal.

source_refs.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming

children.title: Optimality Explanations
children.top_down_role: Representations exposing master-relevant reasons for an optimal value.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master conditions explaining a valid subproblem value bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v(y)\) be the value of a minimization subproblem for \(y\in Y\). An optimality explanation for a bound \(\beta\) is a finite set \(E\) of master conditions such that
\[\forall y'\in Y,\quad y'\models E\;\Longrightarrow\;v(y')\ge\beta.\]
If the current assignment \(\bar y\) satisfies \(E\) and has a feasible subproblem solution of value \(\beta\), then \(v(\bar y)=\beta\). The implication supplies a valid conditional LBBD optimality cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimality explanation lists master conditions under which every associated minimization subproblem has value at least a certified bound.
assumptions_latex: \(v(y')\) uses the extended value \(+\infty\) for infeasible subproblems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y'\models E\Rightarrow v(y')\ge\beta.\)

source_refs.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quantified lower-bound condition is mathematically coherent and definition is an appropriate content kind. The cited section supports optimality via bounds in general, but it does not directly support the master-condition explanation concept or the conditional LBBD cut specialization.

children.title: Certificate-to-Explanation Mapping
children.top_down_role: Structural mappings from optimality certificates to transferable explanations.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-to-Explanation Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection of a bound derivation onto its master-dependent premises.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\pi\) certify the subproblem lower bound \(v(\bar y)\ge\beta\). Map every master-dependent premise \(p\) used by \(\pi\) to an activating master condition \(a(p)\), and set
\[E_\beta(\pi)=\{a(p):p\text{ is used by }\pi\}.\]
If the same verified derivation remains valid for every \(y'\models E_\beta(\pi)\), then \(v(y')\ge\beta\) for all such \(y'\); hence \(E_\beta(\pi)\) is an optimality explanation for \(\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project a bound certificate onto its master-dependent premises; invariant revalidation turns those conditions into an optimality explanation.
assumptions_latex: The activation map \(a\) includes every master-dependent premise of \(\pi\).
The bound derivation is sound whenever all mapped premises are activated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y'\models E_\beta(\pi)\Rightarrow v(y')\ge\beta.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the mapping leaf, and the invariance hypothesis is sufficient for the stated implication. No source is supplied for projecting a lower-bound derivation into an LBBD optimality explanation.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite witness validating a lower or upper optimization bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a minimization problem with value \(v=\inf_{z\in Z}f(z)\), a lower-bound certificate is a finite object \(\pi\) accepted by a sound verifier \(V_B\) such that
\[V_B(Z,f,\beta,\pi)=1\;\Longrightarrow\;\beta\le f(z)\quad\text{for every }z\in Z,\]
and therefore \(\beta\le v\). An upper-bound certificate is a feasible \(\bar z\in Z\), which certifies \(v\le f(\bar z)\). Equality of certified lower and upper bounds certifies optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verified derivation supplies a global lower bound, while a feasible solution supplies an upper bound; equality certifies optimality.
assumptions_latex: The verifier \(V_B\) is sound.
The optimization convention is minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_B(Z,f,\beta,\pi)=1\Rightarrow\beta\le v\), and \(\bar z\in Z\Rightarrow v\le f(\bar z)\).

children.title: Propagation Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanations supporting deductions made during subproblem propagation.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reason set certifying a propagated search literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a search state with active literals \(S\), a propagation explanation for a derived literal \(\ell\) is a finite set \(E\subseteq S\) satisfying
\[F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models\ell,\]
where \(F\) is the invariant constraint theory. Equivalently, \(F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\land\neg\ell\) is infeasible. A sound inference derivation of this infeasibility is a checkable certificate for the propagation and yields the valid clause \(\bigvee_{e\in E}\neg e\lor\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagation explanation is a subset of active search literals that, with the invariant constraints, logically entails the propagated literal.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is unchanged over the search states where the explanation is used.
\(E\subseteq S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\models\bigl(\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\bigr)\Rightarrow\ell.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The entailment and resulting clause are mathematically correct, but the selected content_kind is mismatched: the record defines a propagation explanation E, while only an optional derivation of infeasibility is described as its certificate. The exact leaf is better represented as a definition once an authoritative constraint-programming explanation source is supplied.

children.title: Conflict Explanations
children.top_down_role: Explanations supporting conflicts detected during subproblem search.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reason set certifying inconsistency of a search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be the invariant constraint theory and \(S\) the active literals at a conflicting search state. A conflict explanation is a finite set \(E\subseteq S\) for which a sound certificate establishes
\[F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models\bot.\]
Therefore the learned clause \(\bigvee_{e\in E}\neg e\) is entailed by \(F\) and excludes every future state containing all literals of \(E\). The explanation is subset-minimal if no proper subset of \(E\) still entails \(\bot\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conflict explanation is a subset of active literals jointly inconsistent with the invariant constraints and therefore supports a learned clause.
assumptions_latex: \(E\subseteq S\).
The inconsistency certificate is sound for \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\models\bigvee_{e\in E}\neg e.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inconsistency condition and learned clause are correct, but the primary object being specified is a conflict explanation, not the sound certificate mentioned as establishing it. The content kind should be definition, and an authoritative source for conflict explanations is required.

children.title: Explanation Reuse Across Search States
children.top_down_role: Transfer scope for explanations across related search states.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation Reuse Across Search States
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone reuse criterion for previously derived explanations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an explanation establishes \(F\land\bigwedge_{e\in E}e\models\ell\), where \(F\) is invariant. At any later search state \(S'\) with \(E\subseteq S'\), the same consequence remains valid:
\[F\land\bigwedge_{s\in S'}s\models\ell.\]
For a conflict explanation, take \(\ell=\bot\). Reuse is not justified if the invariant theory, literal semantics, or premise-activation mapping changes; in that case the explanation must be revalidated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explanation remains reusable in any state containing its premises, provided the constraint theory and premise meanings have not changed.
assumptions_latex: \(E\subseteq S'\).
\(F\) and the meanings of literals in \(E\) are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\land\bigwedge_{s\in S'}s\models\ell.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits the leaf, and monotonicity of entailment justifies reuse when the invariant theory and literal meanings remain unchanged. No citation is supplied for this search-state reuse criterion.

children.title: Classical Benders as an Inference Specialization

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Optimality-Certificate Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous linear subproblem with a finite incumbent optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in X\), let \(Q(x)=\min\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge0\}\), with dual feasible region \(D=\{\pi\ge0:W^{\mathsf T}\pi\le q\}\). If the subproblem at \(\bar x\in X\) has a finite optimum, linear-programming strong duality holds, and \(\bar\pi\in D\) is dual-optimal at \(\bar x\), then \(Q(x)\ge\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\) for every \(x\in X\), and \(Q(\bar x)=\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)\). Thus the linear optimality certificate yields the globally valid Benders cut \[\theta\ge\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx).\] Its affine lower bound is exact for the value function at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal dual solution of a feasible linear subproblem certifies a globally valid affine lower bound on the subproblem value, and that bound equals the value at the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: For each master vector \(x\in X\), \(Q(x)=\min\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge0\}\).
The subproblem at \(\bar x\in X\) is feasible with a finite optimum, and linear-programming strong duality holds.
The vector \(\bar\pi\ge0\) satisfies \(W^{\mathsf T}\bar\pi\le q\) and is dual-optimal at \(\bar x\).
The variable \(\theta\) is the master variable representing the subproblem value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in X\), \(Q(x)\ge\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\), with equality at \(\bar x\); hence \(\theta\ge\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\) is a valid Benders optimality cut.

notation.meaning: Subproblem value at master assignment x
Master variable representing the subproblem value

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Infeasibility-Certificate Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-certificate specialization for a continuous linear feasibility subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the parameterized system \(Wy\ge h-Tx\), \(y\ge0\), for \(x\in X\). If \(\bar\pi\ge0\), \(W^{\mathsf T}\bar\pi\le0\), and \(\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)>0\), then \(\bar\pi\) is a linear infeasibility certificate at \(\bar x\). The associated Benders feasibility cut is \[\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0.\] Every \(x\in X\) whose subproblem is feasible satisfies this inequality, while \(\bar x\) violates it strictly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Farkas multiplier certifying incumbent subproblem infeasibility yields a linear feasibility cut satisfied by every assignment whose subproblem is feasible and violated by the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The master domain is \(X\), and the subproblem at \(x\in X\) is the system \(Wy\ge h-Tx\), \(y\ge0\).
The vector \(\bar\pi\ge0\) satisfies \(W^{\mathsf T}\bar\pi\le0\).
At the incumbent \(\bar x\in X\), \(\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(x\in X\) whose subproblem is feasible satisfies \(\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0\), and \(\bar x\) violates this inequality strictly.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

assumptions_latex: Classical Benders uses a continuous linear subproblem for which strong duality and Farkas alternatives apply.
Logic-based Benders permits a sound inference system for a possibly discrete or nonlinear subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The classical multiplier construction is recovered in the linear case, but no finite linear-dual representation is guaranteed outside that case.

notation.meaning: A sound logical explanation or certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between LP-dual certificates and general sound subproblem inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a continuous linear subproblem, strong duality and the Farkas alternative represent optimality and infeasibility certificates by dual multipliers, so logic-based Benders reproduces classical Benders cuts. If the subproblem is discrete, nonconvex, or handled by a proof system not characterized by linear-programming duality, a sound certificate \(C\) may still imply a valid master constraint, but it need not admit a representation by a finite vector of LP dual multipliers. Thus the guaranteed equivalence ends at the linear-duality setting. This boundary asserts representational non-guarantee, not that every logical cut is stronger than every classical cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LP dual multipliers recover classical Benders, while general logical certificates may remain valid without any finite linear-dual representation or universal dominance relation.
knowledge_statements.title: Logical Generalization Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representational boundary is plausible and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but the claim that no finite LP-dual representation is guaranteed for the listed nonclassical settings requires an authoritative LBBD source with a specific locator.

assumptions_latex: A sound subproblem derivation at \(\bar x\) uses a finite set of master-dependent premises \(P_1(\bar x),\ldots,P_k(\bar x)\).
The same derivation remains sound whenever the corresponding premises hold at another master assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected implication \(\bigwedge_{i=1}^k P_i(x)\Rightarrow R(x)\) is valid on the master domain.

notation.meaning: Master-dependent premises used by the derivation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection of proof premises onto the master-variable language.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a sound subproblem derivation at \(\bar x\) establish a conclusion \(R(\bar x)\) using only master-dependent premises \(P_1(\bar x),\ldots,P_k(\bar x)\) and master-independent subproblem axioms. If replacing \(\bar x\) by any \(x\in X\) for which \(P_i(x)\) holds for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) preserves every inference step, then the derivation projects to the master-valid implication \[\bigwedge_{i=1}^k P_i(x)\;\Longrightarrow\;R(x).\] For an infeasibility conclusion, its contrapositive becomes a feasibility cut; for a lower-bound conclusion, it becomes a conditional optimality cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subproblem proof depending only on selected master premises projects to an implication valid for every assignment satisfying those same premises.
knowledge_statements.title: Premise Projection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional projection statement is internally coherent and principle fits the leaf, but both the named premise-projection construction and its asserted LBBD cut interpretations lack cited support.

assumptions_latex: An incumbent certificate proves \(A_{\bar x}\Rightarrow R\), where \(A_{\bar x}\) encodes the complete incumbent assignment.
A master formula \(E\) satisfies \(A_{\bar x}\Rightarrow E\) and independently admits a sound derivation \(E\Rightarrow R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(A_{\bar x}\) by \(E\) preserves validity and applies the conclusion to every assignment satisfying \(E\).

notation.meaning: Formula encoding the full incumbent assignment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound weakening of an assignment-specific explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an incumbent-specific explanation proves \(A_{\bar x}\Rightarrow R\), where \(A_{\bar x}\) is the conjunction encoding the complete master assignment. An explanation generalization is a master formula \(E\) such that \(A_{\bar x}\Rightarrow E\) and there is a sound derivation of \(E\Rightarrow R\) from the subproblem theory. The replacement \[A_{\bar x}\Rightarrow R\quad\leadsto\quad E\Rightarrow R\] is valid and covers every \(x\in X\) satisfying \(E(x)\). The implication \(A_{\bar x}\Rightarrow E\) alone is insufficient: soundness requires the generalized premise itself to entail \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incumbent explanation may be weakened to a broader master formula only when that weaker formula still soundly entails the certified conclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Explanation Generalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement correctly requires the generalized explanation itself to entail the conclusion, but no source supports this terminology or its role in LBBD proof generalization.

assumptions_latex: A certificate \(c\) proves a subproblem assertion at \(\bar x\).
A master condition \(E(x)\) and a transformation \(L_x\) are specified.
For every \(x\in X\) with \(E(x)\), \(L_x(c)\) is accepted by the same sound verifier for the corresponding assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The implication \(E(x)\Rightarrow R(x)\) is a valid lifted certificate over the master domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifier-preserving transport of a certificate between parameterized subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V(x,d,R)\) be a sound verifier whose acceptance means that certificate \(d\) establishes assertion \(R(x)\) for the subproblem parameterized by \(x\). Given an incumbent certificate \(c\), a certificate lift over condition \(E\) is a family of transformations \(L_x\) satisfying \[E(x)\;\Longrightarrow\;V\bigl(x,L_x(c),R\bigr)=1\qquad\text{for every }x\in X.\] Soundness of \(V\) then yields \(E(x)\Rightarrow R(x)\). The lift may alter certificate data; merely reusing the unmodified incumbent certificate without verifying acceptance at \(x\) does not establish validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate is lifted when a verifier-preserving transformation makes it certify the corresponding assertion for every assignment in a stated master region.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Lifting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The verifier-preserving formulation is mathematically sound as an abstract definition and certificate is a plausible kind, but the proposed certificate-lifting model is uncited and may be author-created rather than established LBBD terminology.

assumptions_latex: A sound verifier accepts certificate \(c\) for assertion \(R(x)\) on every \(x\) in a characterized set \(U_c\subseteq X\).
The master solver encounters an assignment \(x'\in U_c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stored certificate can derive \(R(x')\) without resolving the subproblem, subject to successful verification.

notation.meaning: Certified reuse region in the master domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound certificate caching over an explicitly verified master region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c\) be a stored certificate and define its verified reuse region by \[U_c=\{x\in X:V(x,c,R)=1\},\] where \(V\) is a sound certificate verifier. Whenever a later master assignment \(x'\) belongs to \(U_c\), the same certificate establishes \(R(x')\), so the associated infeasibility conclusion or value bound may be reused without resolving the subproblem. Reuse based only on similarity between \(x'\) and the original incumbent is not valid; membership in \(U_c\), or an equivalent sufficient condition implying verifier acceptance, is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stored certificate is reusable at a new master assignment exactly when a sound verifier, or a sufficient reuse condition, accepts it there.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Reuse Across Master Assignments

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reuse condition is sound but largely definitional because the region is defined by verifier acceptance. A source is required for the claimed LBBD certificate-caching interpretation and any operational reuse result.
