assumptions_latex: The master variables are binary: \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\).
The subproblem is infeasible at the incumbent \(\bar x\in\{0,1\}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cut \(\sum_{i:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)+\sum_{i:\bar x_i=0}x_i\ge1\) excludes exactly \(\bar x\) among binary assignments.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-assignment nogood for a binary master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an infeasible binary incumbent \(\bar x\in\{0,1\}^n\), the elementary nogood cut is \[\sum_{i:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)+\sum_{i:\bar x_i=0}x_i\ge1.\] Each summand is zero precisely when the corresponding component of \(x\) equals that of \(\bar x\). Consequently, the left-hand side is zero at \(x=\bar x\) and is at least one at every other binary assignment. The cut therefore removes the incumbent and no other binary master point; its validity requires only the certified infeasibility of the subproblem at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The binary nogood cut requires at least one master bit to differ from an infeasible incumbent, thereby excluding that assignment and no other binary point.
knowledge_statements.title: Nogood Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary exact-assignment nogood formula is precise, and representation fits the cut-form leaf, but the record provides no citation. A specific authoritative locator is required.

children.title: Generalized Nogood Cuts
children.top_down_role: Nogood cuts extended beyond the originating master assignment.

assumptions_latex: The binary master domain is \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\).
A conjunction \(E(x)=\bigwedge_{j\in C}\ell_j(x)\) of binary literals soundly implies subproblem infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\sum_{j\in C}(1-\ell_j(x))\ge1\) is valid for every master assignment with a feasible subproblem.

notation.meaning: Binary literal, equal to either x_j or 1-x_j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Literal-based nogood excluding a certified family of infeasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each \(\ell_j(x)\) be either \(x_j\) or \(1-x_j\), and suppose the subproblem theory proves that \(E(x)=\bigwedge_{j\in C}\ell_j(x)\) implies infeasibility. A generalized nogood is \[\sum_{j\in C}\bigl(1-\ell_j(x)\bigr)\ge1.\] It excludes every assignment satisfying all literals in \(E\), not merely the incumbent from which the explanation was obtained. The inequality is valid because any master assignment having a feasible subproblem must falsify at least one explaining literal. Taking \(C\) to encode every component of one incumbent recovers the elementary nogood cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized nogood negates a certified infeasible conjunction of master literals, excluding every assignment that satisfies the conjunction.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Nogood Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The literal-based inequality correctly negates a conjunction sufficient for infeasibility, but the generalized-nogood terminology and its LBBD placement have no cited support.

children.title: Strengthened Nogood Cuts
children.top_down_role: Nogood cuts tightened through stronger exclusion information.

assumptions_latex: A full incumbent literal set \(C\) defines an elementary nogood.
A subset \(C'\subseteq C\) is independently certified to imply subproblem infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cut from \(C'\) dominates the full-assignment nogood on the binary master domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance obtained by deleting unnecessary literals from a binary nogood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) encode the complete infeasible incumbent and let \(C'\subseteq C\) be a certified infeasible explanation. The strengthened nogood is \[\sum_{j\in C'}\bigl(1-\ell_j(x)\bigr)\ge1.\] Any binary assignment violating the full nogood satisfies every literal indexed by \(C\), hence every literal indexed by \(C'\), and also violates the strengthened cut. Conversely, when \(C'\subsetneq C\), assignments may satisfy all literals in \(C'\) while differing on \(C\setminus C'\); these are removed only by the strengthened cut. Thus the shorter certified explanation yields a cut at least as strong as the full-assignment nogood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting unnecessary incumbent literals yields a stronger nogood when the remaining literals still certify infeasibility, because more assignments satisfy the smaller conjunction.
knowledge_statements.title: Strengthened Nogood Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Under the stated independent infeasibility certification, deleting literals produces a cut whose excluded set contains that of the full-assignment nogood. The property is mathematically plausible, but its dominance claim and strengthened-nogood terminology require a source.

children.title: Generalization–Strength Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between broader applicability and exclusion strength.

assumptions_latex: Two sound infeasibility explanations satisfy \(E_1(x)\Rightarrow E_2(x)\) on the master domain.
Each explanation is negated to form its feasibility cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cut \(\neg E_2(x)\) dominates \(\neg E_1(x)\); broader sufficient explanations yield stronger exclusion cuts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical dominance order for sound infeasibility explanations and their negations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) be sound sufficient conditions for subproblem infeasibility on \(X\), and suppose \(E_1(x)\Rightarrow E_2(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Because \(E_2\) holds on at least as many master assignments, its negation excludes at least as many points: \[\{x\in X:
eg E_2(x)\}\subseteq\{x\in X:
eg E_1(x)\}.\] Hence the feasibility cut \(
eg E_2(x)\) dominates \(
eg E_1(x)\). Generalization is beneficial only while sound entailment of infeasibility is retained; weakening beyond that boundary invalidates the cut, and finding a broader sound explanation may require greater inference effort.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among sound infeasibility explanations, the logically weaker condition covers more assignments and its negation gives the stronger cut, but may be harder to certify.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalization–Strength Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical dominance direction is correct when both explanations are sound, but the broader claim about inference effort and the named generalization–strength tradeoff are unsupported by any citation.

assumptions_latex: At an infeasible incumbent, a sound solver returns a conflict set \(C\) of master literals.
The conjunction of all literals in \(C\) is sufficient for subproblem infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Negating the conflict yields a valid Benders feasibility cut, and subset-minimal conflicts give irredundant literal explanations.

notation.meaning: Binary master literal in the conflict

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility cut obtained from a solver-generated logical conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose conflict analysis at an infeasible incumbent \(\bar x\) returns literals \(\{\ell_j:j\in C\}\) such that the subproblem theory entails \[\bigwedge_{j\in C}\ell_j(x)\;\Longrightarrow\;\text{infeasible}.\] The conflict-directed Benders cut is the negation of this explanation, represented for binary literals by \[\sum_{j\in C}\bigl(1-\ell_j(x)\bigr)\ge1.\] The conflict itself is a verifiable certificate of cut validity. If no proper subset of \(C\) still entails infeasibility, the conflict is subset-minimal and the cut contains no premise literal removable by that same explanation test, although subset-minimality does not imply maximum global cut strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflict analysis identifies master literals jointly causing infeasibility; negating their conjunction gives a valid Benders cut, with minimal conflicts removing locally unnecessary literals.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Directed Benders Cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Negating a sound conflict explanation gives the displayed binary cut, and the subset-minimality qualification is careful. An authoritative conflict-analysis or LBBD source is still required; that source should also establish whether this leaf is best treated as a certificate or as a cut representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Benders Feasibility Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary-master feasibility cut induced by an infeasible explanatory partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), let \(\bar x\in X\), and suppose the subproblem at \(\bar x\) is infeasible. If \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) satisfies \(x_i=\bar x_i\ (i\in S)\Rightarrow Y(x)=\varnothing\) for every \(x\in X\), then the combinatorial cut is \[\sum_{i\in S:\,\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i\in S:\,\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)\geq 1.\] It excludes every master assignment reproducing the infeasible explanation on \(S\), including \(\bar x\), and retains every assignment whose subproblem is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible partial binary assignment yields a cut requiring at least one explanatory master decision to change.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is the master domain.
The fixed-master subproblem has feasible set \(Y(x)\).
\(S\) is a valid infeasibility explanation for \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \sum_{i\in S:\,\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i\in S:\,\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)\geq1\) is valid for all \(x\in X\) with \(Y(x)\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of the subproblem fixed at master assignment x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct Boolean encoding of an infeasible partial assignment

knowledge_statements.title: Nogood Value Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent-specific value cut over a finite binary master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), let \(v:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the subproblem value function, and let \(v(\bar x)=q<+\infty\). Define the Hamming expression \(d_{\bar x}(x)=\sum_{i:\,\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i:\,\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)\). If \(M\geq0\) satisfies \(q-Md_{\bar x}(x)\leq v(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), then \[\theta\geq q-Md_{\bar x}(x)\] is a valid value cut. It is tight at \(\bar x\) and can be arbitrarily weak away from that assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A big-M Hamming-distance cut reproduces the incumbent value and becomes weaker whenever master decisions differ.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is finite.
\(v(\bar x)=q<+\infty\).
\(M\) satisfies the displayed global lower-bound condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\geq q-Md_{\bar x}(x)\) is valid for the epigraph condition \(\theta\geq v(x)\).

notation.meaning: master variable representing a lower bound on the subproblem value
Hamming distance from the incumbent assignment

knowledge_statements.title: Analytical Logic-Based Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting value cuts obtained by symbolic analysis of the fixed-master subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a master domain \(X\) and subproblem value function \(v:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), an analytical logic-based cut at \(\bar x\in X\) is an inequality \(\theta\geq L_{\bar x}(x)\) whose function \(L_{\bar x}:X\to\mathbb R\) is derived from a symbolic argument about the subproblem and satisfies \(L_{\bar x}(x)\leq v(x)\) for all \(x\in X\). It is supporting at \(\bar x\) when \(L_{\bar x}(\bar x)=v(\bar x)<+\infty\). The derivation may exploit logical implications, exchange arguments, or problem-specific inequalities without using linear-programming duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An analytical logic-based cut is any symbolically derived global underestimator of the subproblem value, preferably tight at the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the master domain.
\(v\) is the extended-real subproblem value function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every analytical underestimator \(L_{\bar x}\leq v\) yields the valid cut \(\theta\geq L_{\bar x}(x)\).

notation.meaning: analytically derived lower estimator anchored at the incumbent

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: validity follows from global value-function underestimation

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Derived Value Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value cuts generated from a parameterized lower-bounding relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(x)=\inf\{f(x,y):y\in Y(x)\}\) and let \(R(x)\supseteq Y(x)\) define a relaxation with value \(r(x)=\inf\{f(x,y):y\in R(x)\}\). Then \(r(x)\leq v(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), so \[\theta\geq r(x)\] is a valid value cut whenever its epigraph is representable in the master model. If \(r(\bar x)=v(\bar x)<+\infty\), the cut is supporting at \(\bar x\); otherwise it remains valid but need not reproduce the incumbent subproblem value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing a lower-bounding relaxation produces a valid value cut; equality at the incumbent makes it supporting.
assumptions_latex: \(Y(x)\subseteq R(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
Both value functions use the same minimization objective.
The epigraph of \(r\) is expressible or separable in the master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\geq r(x)\) is valid wherever \(\theta\geq v(x)\) is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Specific Value Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Problem-class-specific lower estimators used as logic-based optimality cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a master domain and \(v:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) its subproblem value function. A domain-specific value cut is an inequality \(\theta\geq\phi(x)\) in which \(\phi:X\to\mathbb R\) is obtained from structural properties of the modeled application and obeys \(\phi(x)\leq v(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Typical structural premises may concern resource consumption, precedence, setup, assignment, or scheduling. The cut is incumbent-supporting when \(\phi(\bar x)=v(\bar x)<+\infty\); validity depends on the stated domain inference, not merely on agreement at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A domain-specific cut converts an application-specific lower-bound argument into a globally valid subproblem-value inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(v\) is the minimization subproblem value function.
The domain inference establishes \(\phi(x)\leq v(x)\) on all of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\geq\phi(x)\) is a valid value cut over \(X\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a globally valid structural lower estimator induces an epigraph cut

assumptions_latex: The decomposition is a minimization problem.
Each generated estimator is globally valid on \(X\).
Master and subproblem bounds use a common stopping tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update adds the valid optimality cut \(\theta\geq L_{\bar x}(x)\), supporting at \(\bar x\) when equality holds.

notation.meaning: value underestimator generated at the incumbent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic construction of a supporting logic-based Benders optimality cut.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a master domain \(X\), value function \(v\), incumbent \(\bar x\in X\), and master value variable \(\theta\). Solve the fixed-master subproblem to obtain \(q=v(\bar x)<+\infty\). Derive a representable function \(L_{\bar x}:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(L_{\bar x}(x)\leq v(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and, when possible, \(L_{\bar x}(\bar x)=q\). Add \(\theta\geq L_{\bar x}(x)\) to the master. Repeat after each finite-valued incumbent; stop when the master lower bound meets the incumbent feasible objective within the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the incumbent subproblem, derive a global value underestimator, add its epigraph cut, and repeat until bounds meet.

children.title: Value-to-Optimality Cut Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships between value-cut representations and optimality-cut roles.

assumptions_latex: \(v\) is an extended-real minimization value function.
\(L\) is finite-valued on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\geq L(x)\) is valid for \(E\) if and only if \(L\leq v\) on \(X\).

notation.meaning: epigraph of the subproblem value over the master domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between value underestimators and valid epigraph inequalities.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a master domain, let \(v:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and define \(E=\{(x,\theta):x\in X,\ \theta\geq v(x)\}\). For any real-valued \(L:X\to\mathbb R\), the inequality \(\theta\geq L(x)\) is valid for \(E\) if and only if \[L(x)\leq v(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in X.\] Consequently, constructing a logic-based optimality cut is equivalent to constructing a representable lower estimator of the subproblem value function. The cut supports \(E\) at \((\bar x,v(\bar x))\) exactly when \(L(\bar x)=v(\bar x)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid optimality cuts correspond exactly to lower estimators of the subproblem value; equality gives incumbent support.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-to-Optimality Cut Correspondence

assumptions_latex: \(C\) contains only master-controlled literals true at \(\bar x\).
The subproblem proof certifies that \(C\) entails infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \bigvee_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell\) is valid for every master assignment with a feasible subproblem.

notation.meaning: master literals satisfied by the incumbent

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: logical negation of a sufficient infeasibility premise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility cuts extracted from a checkable subproblem contradiction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the master assignment \(x\) determine literals from a finite set \(\mathcal L\), and let \(Y(x)\) be the resulting subproblem feasible set. Suppose an infeasibility proof at \(\bar x\) identifies \(C\subseteq\mathcal L(\bar x)\) such that every \(x\in X\) satisfying all literals in \(C\) has \(Y(x)=\varnothing\). Then \[\bigvee_{\ell\in C}\neg\ell\] is a valid feasibility cut. The proof together with the entailment defining \(C\) is a certificate: checking it establishes that no feasible master assignment may satisfy the entire proof support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contradiction supported by master literals yields a cut requiring at least one supporting literal to be false.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility-Proof Cuts
Optimality-Proof Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value cuts justified by a checkable lower-bound proof from the subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v(x)\) be the subproblem value, and suppose a checkable proof object \(P\) establishes
\[
A_P(x)\Rightarrow v(x)\ge L_P(x)
\qquad(x\in X),
\]
where \(A_P\) is representable in the master problem. Then every point in the value epigraph \(\{(x,\theta):\theta\ge v(x)\}\) satisfies the optimality-proof cut
\[
A_P(x)\Rightarrow\theta\ge L_P(x).
\]
Any exact linear or logical encoding of this implication is therefore valid. If \(A_P(\bar x)\) holds and \(L_P(\bar x)=v(\bar x)<+\infty\), the cut supports the incumbent epigraph point \((\bar x,v(\bar x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A verifiable conditional lower-bound proof becomes an optimality cut after encoding its master-side premise.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) certifies \(A_P(x)\Rightarrow L_P(x)\leq v(x)\).
The implication has an exact master-model encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_P(x)\Rightarrow\theta\geq L_P(x)\) is valid for the value epigraph.

notation.meaning: master condition under which the proof applies
lower bound certified by the proof

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a certified conditional value lower bound defines a conditional epigraph cut

assumptions_latex: All explanation literals are controlled or representable in the master.
The propagation rule is sound for the original subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed clause or conditional value inequality is valid for every feasible decomposed solution.

notation.meaning: master-representable literal in a propagation explanation
objective lower bound inferred by propagation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: clausal encoding of a sound propagator implication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cuts obtained from explanations returned by constraint propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\{\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k\}\) be master literals used by sound propagation. If propagation certifies \(\ell_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\ell_k\Rightarrow
eg\ell_0\), then \[
eg\ell_1\vee\cdots\vee
eg\ell_k\vee
eg\ell_0\] is a valid explanation cut. If instead it certifies \(\ell_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\ell_k\Rightarrow v(x)\geq b\), the valid conditional value cut is \[(\ell_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\ell_k)\Rightarrow	heta\geq b.\] Soundness is checkable by replaying the propagator or validating its explanation against the subproblem constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sound propagation explanation becomes either a clause forbidding conflicting literals or a conditional lower-bound cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Explanation Cuts

assumptions_latex: The relaxed diagram has value \(r(x)\leq v(x)\).
The selected flow-dual solution is feasible for every \(x\in X\).
Strong duality holds for the diagram flow model at the incumbent when support is claimed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\geq\alpha+\beta^\top x\) is valid over \(X\).

affine bound induced by a flow-dual solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value cuts obtained from a relaxed decision diagram and its flow dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(x\in X\), let a layered acyclic relaxed decision diagram define a minimum-cost unit-flow problem with value \(r(x)\leq v(x)\). Suppose a feasible solution of its flow dual yields an affine bound \(L(x)=\alpha+\beta^\top x\) that remains dual-feasible for every \(x\in X\). Weak duality gives \(L(x)\leq r(x)\leq v(x)\), hence \[\theta\geq\alpha+\beta^\top x\] is a valid value cut. If the diagram is exact at \(\bar x\) and the dual solution is optimal there, the cut is supporting at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly feasible dual solution of a relaxed decision-diagram flow model yields an affine lower-value cut.

knowledge_statements.title: Irreducible-Explanation Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion filtering for an inclusion-minimal infeasibility or bound explanation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite explanation support \(C\) and a monotone predicate \(P(S)\) meaning that literals in \(S\subseteq C\) suffice to prove the target infeasibility or value bound. Require \(P(C)=\mathrm{true}\). Initialize \(S\leftarrow C\). Visit each \(e\in S\); if \(P(S\setminus\{e\})=\mathrm{true}\), set \(S\leftarrow S\setminus\{e\}\). After every surviving element has been tested against the current set, output \(S\). Then \(P(S)=\mathrm{true}\) and \(P(S\setminus\{e\})=\mathrm{false}\) for every \(e\in S\); thus \(S\) is inclusion-minimal, though not necessarily minimum-cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly delete dispensable premises to obtain an inclusion-minimal explanation, which need not have minimum size.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite and satisfies \(P(C)\).
\(P\) is monotone: \(P(S)\) and \(S\subseteq T\subseteq C\) imply \(P(T)\).
Each predicate evaluation is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(S\) is an inclusion-minimal subset of \(C\) satisfying \(P\).

notation.meaning: predicate that S suffices for the target inference

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: deletion filtering under a monotone sufficiency predicate

knowledge_statements.title: Deletion-Filter Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy reduction of a Boolean infeasibility explanation using a feasibility oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), let \(\bar y\notin Y\), and let \(S\subseteq[n]\) satisfy \(Y\cap F(S)=\varnothing\), where \(F(S)=\{y\in\{0,1\}^n:y_i=\bar y_i\text{ for all }i\in S\}\). Initialize \(T\leftarrow S\). Visit each \(i\in T\) once in a fixed order; if \(Y\cap F(T\setminus\{i\})=\varnothing\), set \(T\leftarrow T\setminus\{i\}\). Output \(T\) and the cut \[\sum_{i\in T:\bar y_i=0}y_i+\sum_{i\in T:\bar y_i=1}(1-y_i)\ge 1.\] The output cut is valid for \(Y\), and no retained index is deletable relative to the final support under the chosen pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly delete a fixed literal whenever the remaining fixings still admit no feasible completion; the final support yields a valid, deletion-minimal no-good cut.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\)
\(Y\cap F(S)=\varnothing\)
The feasibility oracle answers each restricted-feasibility query exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned support \(T\) defines a valid no-good cut and is deletion-minimal for the completed pass.

notation.meaning: feasible master assignments admitting acceptable subproblem completion
assignments agreeing with the rejected point on support S

knowledge_statements.title: Additive Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental construction of a sufficient Boolean explanation from candidate literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), \(\bar y\notin Y\), and let \((i_1,\ldots,i_m)\) order candidate indices. Initialize \(T\leftarrow\varnothing\). For \(k=1,\ldots,m\), set \(T\leftarrow T\cup\{i_k\}\) and query whether \(Y\cap F(T)=\varnothing\). Stop at the first such \(k\), optionally apply a deletion filter to \(T\), and return the no-good cut supported on \(T\). If no prefix is infeasible, report failure for this ordering. Whenever the procedure returns a support, its cut \[\sum_{i\in T:\bar y_i=0}y_i+\sum_{i\in T:\bar y_i=1}(1-y_i)\ge1\] is valid for \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add candidate fixings until they jointly preclude every feasible completion; the resulting support, optionally deletion-filtered, defines a valid no-good cut.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) and \(\bar y\notin Y\)
Candidate indices are ordered as \((i_1,\ldots,i_m)\)
Restricted feasibility is decided exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned support \(T\) satisfies \(Y\cap F(T)=\varnothing\) and therefore yields a valid no-good cut.

notation.meaning: assignments matching the rejected point on T

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction is valid when it returns, but no source establishes that this prefix-building procedure is the intended meaning of additive strengthening in logic-based Benders decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Based Support Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or bounded search for a smallest infeasible explanation contained in an initial support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Y\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), a rejected point \(\bar y\), and \(S\subseteq[n]\) with \(Y\cap F(S)=\varnothing\), solve \[\min\{|T|:T\subseteq S,\ Y\cap F(T)=\varnothing\}.\] A branch-and-bound search branches on retaining or deleting each index, prunes a node when its best possible cardinality is no better than the incumbent, and may prune any partial deletion whose maximal permitted completion cannot remain infeasible. Return an optimal support \(T^*\) when the search closes; if terminated early, return the incumbent with its bound. The no-good cut supported on any feasible incumbent is valid for \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search over subsets of an initial explanation to minimize support size, using exact restricted-feasibility tests and bounds; every feasible incumbent yields a valid cut.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\cap F(S)=\varnothing\)
The restricted-feasibility oracle is exact
Search bounds are valid for the cardinality objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A completed search returns a minimum-cardinality support \(T^*\subseteq S\); early termination returns a valid incumbent and bound.

notation.meaning: assignments agreeing with the rejected point on T

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subset-cardinality formulation is coherent, but the stated branch-and-bound and early-termination guarantees need a source and a more precise oracle/search model, particularly for the maximal-completion pruning rule and returned bound.

children.title: Cut-Dominance Relations
children.top_down_role: Comparison relations based on the relative exclusion strength of cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Dominance Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic dominance and its support-order specialization for Boolean no-good cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For cuts \(c_1\) and \(c_2\) over a common master domain \(D\), let \(V_D(c)=\{y\in D:y\text{ satisfies }c\}\). Define \(c_1\) to dominate \(c_2\) on \(D\) when \(V_D(c_1)\subseteq V_D(c_2)\); dominance is strict when the inclusion is proper. For a rejected Boolean point \(\bar y\), let \(c_T\) be its no-good cut supported on \(T\). If \(T_1\subseteq T_2\), then \(V_D(c_{T_1})\subseteq V_D(c_{T_2})\), so \(c_{T_1}\) dominates \(c_{T_2}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut dominates another when every master point satisfying the first also satisfies the second. For one rejected Boolean point, smaller no-good support means stronger dominance.
assumptions_latex: Both cuts are interpreted on the same master domain \(D\)
For the support-order claim, both no-good cuts refer to the same \(\bar y\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_1\subseteq T_2\) implies \(c_{T_1}\) dominates \(c_{T_2}\) on \(D\).

children.title: Minimal Cut Supports

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Cut Supports
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion-minimal support for a valid no-good explanation at a rejected Boolean point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), \(\bar y\notin Y\), and \(F(T)=\{y\in\{0,1\}^n:y_i=\bar y_i\text{ for every }i\in T\}\). A set \(T\subseteq[n]\) is a minimal cut support for \(\bar y\) relative to \(Y\) if \[Y\cap F(T)=\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad Y\cap F(T\setminus\{i\})\ne\varnothing\ \text{ for every }i\in T.\] Thus its no-good cut is valid, while deleting any one supported literal destroys the explanation property. Minimality is by inclusion and need not imply minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A support is minimal when its fixed literals forbid every feasible completion, but removing any one literal permits at least one feasible completion.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\)
\(\bar y\notin Y\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The support is inclusion-minimal exactly when it satisfies the displayed infeasibility and single-deletion conditions.

children.title: Dominance–Minimality Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where dominance comparisons and support minimality lead to different rankings.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance–Minimality Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of identifying minimal explanation supports with globally undominated cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(Y\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) and a rejected point \(\bar y\). Within the family of no-good cuts \(\{c_T:T\subseteq[n],\ Y\cap F(T)=\varnothing\}\) for this same point, \(T\) is inclusion-minimal if and only if no valid \(c_U\) with \(U\subsetneq T\) dominates \(c_T\) by support deletion. This equivalence does not establish global undominance: a cut of another algebraic form, or a cut derived from another inference region, may strictly dominate \(c_T\). Nor does inclusion-minimality imply that \(|T|\) is minimum among valid supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimal support excludes further deletion-based strengthening for the same no-good family, but it guarantees neither minimum cardinality nor global undominance among all valid cuts.
assumptions_latex: All support-order comparisons use the same rejected point \(\bar y\)
Dominance is evaluated on a common master domain
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Support minimality characterizes deletion-undominance only inside the fixed-reference no-good family.

notation.meaning: assignments agreeing with the rejected point on T

children.title: Cut-Lifting Mechanisms

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Lifting Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential lifting of a valid inequality after restoring fixed Boolean variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), let \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(a_j=0\), and suppose \(a^\top x\le b\) is valid for \(P\cap\{x:x_j=0\}\). Assume \(P\cap\{x:x_j=1\}\ne\varnothing\), and define \[\alpha_j=b-\max\{a^\top x:x\in P,\ x_j=1\}.\] Then \(a^\top x+\alpha_jx_j\le b\) is valid for \(P\). Sequential lifting restores several fixed variables one at a time, recomputing each coefficient over the set in which previously lifted variables are free and the remaining variables retain their prescribed fixings. Exact solutions of the lifting subproblems produce an inequality valid after all variables have been restored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restore fixed Boolean variables one at a time and compute each new coefficient by exact optimization so that the expanded inequality remains valid.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\)
\(a_j=0\) and \(a^\top x\le b\) is valid on the face \(x_j=0\)
\(P\cap\{x:x_j=1\}\ne\varnothing\)
The lifting maximization is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted inequality \(a^\top x+\alpha_jx_j\le b\) is valid for \(P\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Generalization Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalizing a point cut through a sufficient logical predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the master domain, \(Y\subseteq D\) the acceptable assignments, and \(\bar y\in D\setminus Y\). Suppose a predicate \(G:D\to\{0,1\}\) satisfies \(G(\bar y)=1\) and \[G(y)=1\ \Longrightarrow\ y\notin Y\qquad(y\in D).\] Then the generalized logical cut \(G(y)=0\) is valid for \(Y\) and excludes every assignment in the inference region \(R_G=\{y\in D:G(y)=1\}\), including \(\bar y\). A mechanism may obtain \(G\) by dropping irrelevant literals, replacing equalities by implied ranges, or projecting a verified subproblem explanation; validity depends only on the displayed implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace exclusion of one rejected point by exclusion of a logically certified region whose every assignment has an unacceptable subproblem completion.

\(G(y)=1\) implies \(y\notin Y\) throughout \(D\)

children.title: Lifted-Cut Validity Scope

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Cut Validity Scope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain condition required for a lifted or generalized cut to remain valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the master domain, \(Y\subseteq D\) its acceptable assignments, and let \(\ell(y)\le\beta\) be a lifted cut derived using an inference model valid on a region \(R\subseteq D\). Its certified validity scope is \(Y\cap R\) precisely when \[\ell(y)\le\beta\qquad\text{for every }y\in Y\cap R.\] It is globally valid on \(Y\) only if the inequality holds for every \(y\in Y\), which follows, for example, when \(Y\subseteq R\). Outside \(R\), validity requires a separate argument; coefficient correctness on the derivation region alone cannot justify global insertion into an unrestricted master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted cut is certified only where its inference assumptions hold; using it globally requires validity over every acceptable master assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq D\)
The lifting argument is certified on \(R\subseteq D\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global use is justified only when \(\ell(y)\le\beta\) holds for all \(y\in Y\).

children.title: Cut Aggregation

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative aggregation of valid inequalities over a common master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and suppose \(a_k^\top y\ge b_k\) is valid for \(Y\) for every \(k=1,\ldots,m\). For any multipliers \(\lambda_k\ge0\), the aggregate cut is \[\left(\sum_{k=1}^m\lambda_k a_k\right)^\top y\ge\sum_{k=1}^m\lambda_k b_k.\] It is valid for \(Y\). If all multipliers are positive, satisfaction of every component cut implies the aggregate, but the aggregate generally does not imply each component. Aggregation therefore replaces a family by a logically weaker single inequality unless additional structure makes the two descriptions equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative weighted sum of valid cuts is valid, but usually retains less separating information than enforcing every component cut individually.
assumptions_latex: \(a_k^\top y\ge b_k\) is valid for \(Y\) for each \(k\)
\(\lambda_k\ge0\) for each \(k\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed aggregate inequality is valid for \(Y\).

children.title: Cut Disaggregation

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Disaggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replacing an aggregate inequality by separately valid component cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_k^\top y\ge b_k\), \(k=1,\ldots,m\), be valid cuts for \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\lambda_k>0\). Disaggregation replaces their aggregate by the system \[a_k^\top y\ge b_k\qquad(k=1,\ldots,m).\] The system implies \(\left(\sum_k\lambda_k a_k\right)^\top y\ge\sum_k\lambda_k b_k\). The converse can fail: with \(y\in\mathbb R^2\), component cuts \(y_1\ge0\), \(y_2\ge0\), and unit multipliers, the aggregate \(y_1+y_2\ge0\) admits \((-1,1)\), which violates the first component. Thus disaggregation can strictly strengthen the master relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enforcing component cuts separately implies their positive aggregate and can be strictly stronger, because an aggregate permits violations offset by surplus in other components.
assumptions_latex: Every component inequality is valid for the same feasible set \(Y\)
\(\lambda_k>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The disaggregated system implies its aggregate, while the reverse implication need not hold.

children.title: Cut-Granularity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs involving cut count, strength, locality, and management cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Granularity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength-versus-size relation between aggregated and disaggregated cut systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a master relaxation, and let the valid component cuts be \(a_k^\top y\ge b_k\) for \(k=1,\ldots,m\), with aggregation weights \(\lambda_k>0\). Define \(R_D=R\cap\bigcap_{k=1}^m\{y:a_k^\top y\ge b_k\}\) and \(R_A=R\cap\{y:(\sum_{k=1}^m\lambda_k a_k)^\top y\ge\sum_{k=1}^m\lambda_k b_k\}\). Then \(R_D\subseteq R_A\). Consequently, for any common minimization objective \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), whenever both infima are well defined, \(\inf_{y\in R_D}f(y)\ge\inf_{y\in R_A}f(y)\). Aggregation reduces the number of stored inequalities from \(m\) to one, while strict containment—and hence a weaker relaxation—is possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregated cuts give an equal or tighter minimization relaxation, while one aggregate uses fewer constraints; aggregation can lose relaxation strength.
assumptions_latex: All component cuts are valid on a common feasible set
\(\lambda_k>0\) for \(k=1,\ldots,m\)
Both formulations use the same base relaxation \(R\)
The compared formulations use the same minimization objective \(f\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_D\subseteq R_A\), and therefore \(\inf_{y\in R_D}f(y)\ge\inf_{y\in R_A}f(y)\) whenever both infima are well defined.

knowledge_statements.title: Scope Promotion Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for promoting a locally justified cut to global use.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x,\theta)\leq0\) be known valid on \(S\subseteq X\), and let \(E(x,\theta)\) denote the epigraph-feasibility predicate of the original decomposed problem. \(E\) exactly characterizes feasible master epigraph points.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Cut LBBD
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative LBBD adding at most one aggregated inference cut per master solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a master relaxation \(M_0\), set \(k=0\). Solve \(M_k\) for \((x^k,\theta^k)\), then solve the logical subproblem fixed by \(x^k\). If the subproblem certifies feasibility and \(\theta^k\) is a valid lower representation of its value, return \(x^k\). Otherwise derive one globally valid feasibility or optimality cut \(c_k(x,\theta)\leq0\) violated by \((x^k,\theta^k)\), including any aggregation of several subproblem explanations, and set \(M_{k+1}=M_k\cap\{c_k\leq0\}\). Increment \(k\) and repeat; infeasibility of the strengthened master certifies infeasibility of the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single-cut LBBD solves a master and adds one aggregated valid inference cut after each failed subproblem check.
assumptions_latex: Each generated cut is valid for every feasible epigraph point.
Master and fixed-master subproblems are solved to the stated stopping tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{k+1}=M_k\cap\{(x,\theta):c_k(x,\theta)\leq0\}\), with at most one new cut per iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Cut LBBD
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative LBBD retaining separate cuts from decomposable logical subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose recourse decomposes into subproblems indexed by \(J\), with master variables \(\theta_j\). At iteration \(k\), solve the current master for \((x^k,\theta^k)\) and evaluate every selected subproblem \(j\in J\) at \(x^k\). For each subproblem whose feasibility or value is not represented correctly, derive a valid cut \(c_{jk}(x,\theta_j)\leq0\) violated by the current point. Add all such cuts separately and re-solve. Stop when every subproblem is feasible and no \(c_{jk}\) is violated; return the resulting master solution. Unlike single-cut LBBD, no aggregation across \(j\) is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multi-cut LBBD adds separate valid inference cuts for each violated recourse component at an iteration.
assumptions_latex: The recourse structure admits a finite index set \(J\).
Every component cut is valid for the original feasible epigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{k+1}=M_k\cap\bigcap_{j\in V_k}\{(x,\theta):c_{jk}(x,\theta_j)\leq0\}\).

notation.meaning: Components producing violated cuts at iteration k.
Cut from component j at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Enhanced LBBD
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LBBD strengthened by a tractable lower relaxation of logical recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x)\) be the logical recourse value and let \(R(x)\) satisfy \(R(x)\leq Q(x)\) on the master domain. Initialize the LBBD master with \(\theta\geq R(x)\), or add valid inequalities obtained from this relaxation during the search. At a master solution \((x^k,\theta^k)\), solve the exact logical subproblem, add a violated globally valid LBBD cut when necessary, and repeat. Terminate only when the exact subproblem is feasible and its value is represented within tolerance; satisfaction of the relaxation alone is not a stopping certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation-enhanced LBBD combines exact logical checks with a tractable global lower bound on recourse.
assumptions_latex: \(R(x)\leq Q(x)\) for every admissible master assignment.
Exact logical subproblems remain available for certification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\geq R(x)\) strengthens the master without replacing the exact LBBD termination check.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Started LBBD
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LBBD initialized with reusable valid cuts, bounds, or feasible incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an initial master \(M_0\) containing a collection \(C_0\) of cuts already certified valid for the current model, and optionally a feasible incumbent \((\bar x,\bar y)\) with objective value \(U\). Solve \(M_0\), perform the exact logical subproblem check, and add valid violated LBBD cuts as in the ordinary iterative method. Retain \(U\) as an upper cutoff when minimizing. Terminate under the usual exact feasibility and bound conditions. Any inherited cut whose validity depends on changed data must be revalidated or discarded before initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Warm-started LBBD begins with certified reusable cuts and optionally a feasible incumbent, then follows the ordinary exact LBBD loop.
assumptions_latex: Every cut in \(C_0\) is valid for the current model instance.
The incumbent is used only if its complete solution is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_0=M_{\mathrm{base}}\cap\bigcap_{c\in C_0}\{c\leq0\}\), with optional valid cutoff \(U\).

notation.meaning: Objective value of an initial feasible incumbent.
