children.title: Incumbent-Triggered Subproblem Checks
children.top_down_role: Subproblem invocation restricted to candidate incumbent solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Triggered Subproblem Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact logical checking only when the master search produces an integer incumbent candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: During branch-and-bound, invoke the logical subproblem oracle whenever the master solver proposes an integer incumbent candidate \((x^I,\theta^I)\). Fix the master decisions to \(x^I\) and solve the exact subproblem. Accept the candidate only if the subproblem is feasible and \(\theta^I\) represents its value within tolerance. Otherwise derive a globally valid cut violated by \((x^I,\theta^I)\), reject the candidate, and return the cut through the solver's incumbent callback. The procedure performs no logical check solely because a fractional node relaxation has been solved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each integer incumbent candidate is checked by the exact logical subproblem before acceptance; a failed candidate produces a valid rejecting cut.
assumptions_latex: The callback is invoked before an incumbent becomes final.
The logical subproblem is well-defined for integer master assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^I\text{ is accepted}\Longrightarrow x^I\text{ passes the exact logical subproblem check}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits incumbent-triggered checking, but no source supports the callback protocol, and failed checks do not automatically guarantee an available globally valid violated cut without an additional cut-generation assumption.

children.title: Lazy Cut Injection at Incumbents
children.top_down_role: Insertion of master-valid cuts through incumbent callbacks.

knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Cut Injection at Incumbents
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Callback insertion of globally valid LBBD cuts violated by incumbent candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an integer candidate \((x^I,\theta^I)\), solve the exact logical subproblem. If it yields a feasibility or optimality explanation, transform that explanation into a cut \(c(x,\theta)\leq0\) that is valid for every feasible epigraph point and satisfies \(c(x^I,\theta^I)>0\). Submit \(c\) as a lazy constraint and reject the candidate. If no violated valid cut exists and the subproblem check succeeds, permit acceptance. A cut valid only within a branch must not be installed globally unless the branch conditions are included in its activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A failed incumbent check injects a globally valid, currently violated lazy constraint and rejects that candidate.
assumptions_latex: The solver supports correctness-preserving lazy-constraint callbacks.
Every submitted cut is valid over its declared activation scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(x^I,\theta^I)>0\) and \(E(x,\theta)\Rightarrow c(x,\theta)\leq0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm correctly separates global and branch-local validity, but lazy-constraint callback semantics and the LBBD transformation claim require an authoritative source.

children.title: Incumbent Rejection Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Subproblem outcomes that justify rejecting a candidate incumbent.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Rejection Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical and validity limits on rejecting an integer master candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An integer candidate \((x^I,\theta^I)\) may be rejected by the LBBD callback when the fixed-master subproblem is infeasible, or when its certified value \(Q(x^I)\) satisfies \(Q(x^I)>\theta^I+\varepsilon\). Rejection must be accompanied by a cut or certificate valid under the callback's declared scope. If the subproblem is feasible and \(Q(x^I)\leq\theta^I+\varepsilon\), the logical check alone provides no basis for rejection. Likewise, an incomplete search, heuristic failure, or cut valid only outside the incumbent's active scope is not a sound rejection certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reject an incumbent only for certified subproblem infeasibility or a certified recourse-bound violation, supported by a valid cut or certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x^I)\) is exact or certified to the required tolerance.
\(\varepsilon\geq0\) is the declared acceptance tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{sound rejection}\Longrightarrow Q(x^I)=+\infty\text{ or }Q(x^I)>\theta^I+\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Exact recourse value at the incumbent candidate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits and the tolerance condition is plausible, but the claimed exhaustive boundary for sound logical rejection requires a source specifying exact-or-certified subproblem evaluation and callback behavior.

children.title: Node-Triggered Subproblem Checks
children.top_down_role: Subproblem invocation at selected branch-search nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Triggered Subproblem Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical subproblem evaluation at selected branch-and-bound nodes, possibly before integrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a node-selection predicate \(T(N,x^N)\). Whenever branch-and-bound solves node \(N\) with relaxation solution \((x^N,\theta^N)\) and \(T(N,x^N)\) holds, invoke a subproblem oracle defined at \(x^N\). If the oracle derives an inequality \(c(x,\theta)\leq 0\) that is violated by \((x^N,\theta^N)\) and valid for every original-model feasible epigraph point compatible with node \(N\), add it with node-local scope; if it is valid for every original-model feasible epigraph point, it may instead be added globally. Reoptimize after adding the cut; otherwise continue the search. An integer-only oracle may be invoked only when \(x^N\) belongs to its domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected branch-and-bound nodes trigger compatible subproblem checks, and any resulting violated cut is enforced only over the feasible solutions covered by its certified local or global scope.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a specified deterministic or solver-controlled trigger.
The invoked oracle is defined at the current node solution.
The solver supports the declared local or global enforcement scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(N,x^N)\Longrightarrow\) invoke the compatible oracle, and add a returned violated cut only over its certified validity scope.

notation.meaning: Master component of the current node-relaxation solution.
Recourse-bound component of the current node-relaxation solution.
Cut returned by the subproblem oracle.

children.title: Fractional-Node Cut Injection
children.top_down_role: Insertion of valid cuts at nodes with fractional master solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional-Node Cut Injection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity requirement for injecting LBBD-derived cuts at fractional node relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^N,\theta^N)\) be a fractional solution of the relaxation at node \(N\), let \(Z_N\) be the set of original-model feasible epigraph points compatible with that node, and let \(Z\) be the global feasible epigraph set. An inequality \(c(x,\theta)\leq0\) violated by \((x^N,\theta^N)\) may be enforced locally at node \(N\) only if it is valid for every point of \(Z_N\); it may be enforced globally only if it is valid for every point of \(Z\). The inequality need not be valid for every fractional point of the current relaxation, because removing such points is the purpose of a cutting plane. Its submission must nevertheless use a solver mechanism that preserves its certified activation scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut injected at a fractional node must preserve every original-model feasible solution in its local or global activation scope, but it may cut off fractional relaxation points.
assumptions_latex: \((x^N,\theta^N)\) is a fractional node-relaxation solution.
\(Z_N\subseteq Z\) contains the original-model feasible epigraph points compatible with node \(N\).
The solver supports the cut's certified activation scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(x^N,\theta^N)>0\), together with either \(\forall(x,\theta)\in Z_N,\ c(x,\theta)\leq0\) for local enforcement or \(\forall(x,\theta)\in Z,\ c(x,\theta)\leq0\) for global enforcement.

notation.meaning: Original-model feasible epigraph points compatible with node N.

children.title: Node Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Policies determining which search nodes receive subproblem checks.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trigger conditions for exact LBBD subproblem checks during branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the active master node be \(v\), with relaxation solution \((x^v,\theta^v)\), depth \(d(v)\), and integrality indicator \(I(v)\). A node-selection regime is a predicate \(T(v,x^v,\theta^v)\in\{0,1\}\). Standard regimes include incumbent-only, \(T=I(v)\); depth-limited, \(T=\mathbf 1\{d(v)\le D\}\); periodic, \(T=\mathbf 1\{k(v)\equiv0\pmod q\}\); and bound-sensitive, \(T=\mathbf 1\{L(v)<U\}\). Whenever \(T=1\), the subproblem is checked and every resulting cut must be globally valid or explicitly restricted to the subtree rooted at \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node regime specifies exactly which search nodes trigger subproblem solution and requires each generated cut to have the appropriate global or local validity.
assumptions_latex: \(v\) is an active node of an exact branch-and-bound search.
\(D\ge0\) and \(q\ge1\) are fixed integers.
\(L(v)\) and \(U\) are valid node and incumbent bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(v,x^v,\theta^v)=1\) triggers an exact subproblem check at \(v\).

notation.meaning: indicator that the master solution at node v is integral
node lower bound and incumbent upper bound

review_flags: Exact LBBD-specific source locator is unavailable.
standard_field_rationale: callback trigger predicates are standard branch-and-check abstractions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, and the trigger-predicate formulation is coherent, but no inspectable source supports these particular regimes or the asserted global/local cut rule in branch-check LBBD.

children.title: Mixed Trigger Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies combining multiple subproblem-invocation events.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Trigger Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A combined incumbent, node, and progress-based subproblem-check policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an active node \(v\), relaxation solution \((x^v,\theta^v)\), incumbent event \(E_I(v)\), node event \(E_N(v)\), and progress score \(g(v)\), choose thresholds \(\tau\) and \(D\). Set \(T(v)=E_I(v)\lor(E_N(v)\land d(v)\le D)\lor(g(v)\ge\tau)\). If \(T(v)=0\), continue master search. If \(T(v)=1\), solve the induced subproblem, reject an infeasible incumbent, update its objective value when feasible, and inject every valid feasibility or optimality cut. Duplicate checks may be suppressed by caching the master assignment and the cut-generation state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed policy checks subproblems on incumbent, selected-node, or progress events, then rejects, updates, or cuts according to the exact subproblem result.
assumptions_latex: Each triggered subproblem is solved to the accuracy required by the cut oracle.
Every injected cut is valid in its declared callback scope.
Cached results are reused only for equivalent subproblem-defining assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(v)=1\) implies execution of the subproblem oracle and its valid search response.
review_flags: A source specifying mixed-trigger LBBD callback semantics is required.
standard_field_rationale: disjunctive event triggers and cached oracle calls are standard implementation abstractions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Mixed Trigger Policies, but the progress trigger, incumbent response, cut injection, and caching semantics are implementation-dependent and lack an authoritative locator.

children.title: Incumbent–Node Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of checks performed at incumbents with checks performed elsewhere in the tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent–Node Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordination rules preventing inconsistent processing of node and incumbent callbacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a cache \(C\) indexed by the subproblem-defining master assignment \(a(x)\). At a node callback, record valid cuts and bounds obtained for \(a(x^v)\), but accept no fractional solution as an incumbent. At an incumbent callback with candidate \(\bar x\), reuse a cached exact result only if its key equals \(a(\bar x)\); otherwise solve the subproblem. Accept \(\bar x\) only when the subproblem is feasible and its verified recourse value is represented in the incumbent objective. Cuts discovered by either callback are deduplicated and submitted only in a callback context permitting their validity scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Node checks may supply cuts and bounds, while only an exact matching subproblem result may validate and price an incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The cache key uniquely determines the induced subproblem.
Incumbent acceptance is controlled by a callback capable of rejection or lazy-constraint submission.
Concurrent cache and cut-pool updates are atomic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An incumbent \(\bar x\) is accepted only after an exact result for \(a(\bar x)\) verifies feasibility and recourse cost.

notation.meaning: subproblem-defining projection of a master solution
cache of exact subproblem results and generated cuts

review_flags: Solver-independent formalization needs an LBBD callback source.
standard_field_rationale: exact-key caching and incumbent validation preserve oracle consistency.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and exact-key cache discipline fit the container, but incumbent acceptance, node-bound reuse, callback permissions, and concurrency requirements need solver-independent LBBD or solver-API support.

children.title: Hybrid Callback Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Solver-interface limits affecting mixed callback strategies.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Callback Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundaries for cuts and incumbent decisions across callback types.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(v)\) be the master relaxation at node \(v\), and let \(X_v\) be the subtree domain. A cut \(c(x,\theta)\le0\) may be submitted globally only if it holds for every feasible master-recourse pair. It may be submitted locally at \(v\) only if it holds throughout \(X_v\). An incumbent callback may reject a candidate only from an exact infeasibility certificate or a valid violated lazy constraint. A fractional-node callback may strengthen \(R(v)\), but must not certify integer feasibility or replace the incumbent objective using an unverified subproblem value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global cuts must hold everywhere, local cuts throughout their subtree, and fractional callbacks cannot validate incumbents or unverified objective values.
assumptions_latex: The solver distinguishes global cuts, local cuts, and incumbent-rejection callbacks.
The subproblem oracle identifies the validity domain of each returned cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Callback actions are correct only when their solver scope contains the complete validity domain required by the action.

notation.meaning: master assignments in the subtree rooted at v

review_flags: Precise callback permissions depend on the solver API and need authoritative sourcing.
standard_field_rationale: cut validity domains determine admissible global and local submission contexts.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf and the validity-domain distinction is mathematically reasonable, but callback submission and rejection permissions vary by solver and have no authoritative source here.

children.title: Feasibility Preservation
children.top_down_role: Correctness considerations concerning preservation of feasible master solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility correctness of exact branch-check search with valid cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite-domain master set \(X\) and induced subproblem feasibility predicate \(F(x)\). Suppose every accepted incumbent \(x\) is checked exactly, every candidate with \(F(x)=0\) is rejected, and each added cut is satisfied by every \(x\in X\) with \(F(x)=1\). Then no feasible solution of the original decomposed problem is removed by cut generation, and every incumbent returned by the algorithm satisfies \(F(x)=1\). Consequently, if the search reports a feasible solution together with its verified subproblem solution, that pair is feasible for the undecomposed formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact incumbent checking and cuts valid for all feasible assignments ensure that no feasible solution is lost and no infeasible incumbent is returned.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the master domain and \(F\) is evaluated exactly for accepted incumbents.
All generated cuts are valid for every assignment satisfying \(F(x)=1\).
The branch-and-bound engine enforces every submitted cut in its declared scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned incumbent satisfies \(F(x)=1\), and valid cuts preserve all originally feasible assignments.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly establishes branch-check feasibility preservation.
standard_field_rationale: the conclusion follows from exact validation and validity-preserving cuts.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits Feasibility Preservation and its hypotheses support the stated feasibility conclusion, but no cited theorem or section establishes this branch-check LBBD result.

children.title: Optimality Preservation
children.top_down_role: Correctness considerations concerning preservation of globally optimal solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global optimality correctness for exact branch-check LBBD.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original objective be \(c(x)+Q(x)\) over \(x\in X\) with feasible subproblem, where master variable \(\theta\) underestimates \(Q(x)\). Suppose all cuts preserve every feasible pair \((x,Q(x))\), each accepted incumbent uses the exact value \(Q(x)\), and the branch-and-bound lower bounds remain valid after every callback. If exhaustive search terminates with incumbent \(x^*\) and global lower bound \(L\) satisfying \(c(x^*)+Q(x^*)\le L+\varepsilon\), then \(x^*\) is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal for the original problem; for \(\varepsilon=0\), it is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid cuts, exact incumbent recourse values, and valid global bounds make the terminating incumbent epsilon-optimal for the original problem.
assumptions_latex: Every feasibility and optimality cut preserves all original feasible solutions and objective epigraph points.
Accepted incumbent recourse values are exact.
The terminating global lower bound is valid for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(x^*)+Q(x^*)-z^*\le\varepsilon\), where \(z^*\) is the original optimal value.

notation.meaning: valid global lower bound at termination

review_flags: No supplied source directly states this branch-check LBBD optimality theorem.
standard_field_rationale: exact upper bounds and valid exhaustive lower bounds imply the stated gap guarantee.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits Optimality Preservation and the terminal valid-bound argument is coherent, but the LBBD-specific preservation hypotheses and conclusion lack a supporting source locator.

children.title: Termination Conditions
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions supporting finite completion of the search.

knowledge_statements.title: Termination Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination conditions for exact branch-check LBBD.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the master domain \(X\) is finite, each triggered subproblem and cut-separation call terminates, and every rejected complete assignment either is permanently excluded or receives a cut preventing repetition of the same deficient master state. Assume further that node processing is fair and the branch-and-bound engine terminates after finitely many nodes whenever only finitely many distinct cuts can be added. Then branch-check LBBD terminates after finitely many master-node and subproblem evaluations, returning infeasibility or an incumbent with the prescribed optimality gap. Without finite-state exclusion, finite cut generation, or a convergent tolerance rule, termination is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite master states, terminating oracles, fair node processing, and permanent progress at rejected states yield finite branch-check termination.
assumptions_latex: The master domain and set of distinguishable cut states are finite.
Every oracle call terminates and rejected complete states cannot recur indefinitely.
The branch-and-bound node policy is fair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm performs finitely many node and subproblem evaluations before satisfying its infeasibility or optimality-gap stopping rule.

notation.meaning: finite set of complete master assignments

review_flags: A dedicated finite-convergence result for branch-check LBBD is needed.
standard_field_rationale: finiteness plus permanent state exclusion prevents infinite repetition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Finite-state progress plausibly gives finite termination, but the stronger promise of returning an incumbent with the prescribed optimality gap also requires valid bounding, exhaustive pruning, and incumbent-evaluation assumptions not stated here. A dedicated convergence source is needed before fixing the theorem's exact version.

knowledge_statements.title: Logic Cuts for Linear Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual certificates converted into logic-valid cuts for binary master decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) define the linear subproblem \(Ay\ge b-Bx\). For a checked assignment \(\bar x\), an extreme ray \(\lambda\ge0\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\) and \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}(b-B\bar x)>0\) certifies infeasibility. The inequality \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}(b-Bx)\le0\) is therefore a valid feasibility cut whenever the displayed linear dependence on \(x\) represents the induced subproblem exactly. More generally, a logic explanation identifying literals sufficient for the certified contradiction yields the corresponding nogood, which excludes every assignment containing those literals without excluding any feasible induced subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual infeasibility ray yields a linear feasibility cut; a sufficient logical explanation yields a nogood excluding assignments that reproduce the contradiction.
assumptions_latex: The subproblem is a feasible-or-infeasible linear system with continuous variable \(y\).
The dependence \(b-Bx\) exactly represents master-to-subproblem coupling.
Any logical explanation contains only literals sufficient for infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}(b-Bx)\le0\) is valid for every master assignment inducing a feasible linear subproblem.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

review_flags: The locator provisionally supports Benders feasibility cuts; its coverage of logic explanations remains to be checked.

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Farkas-ray feasibility cut is mathematically correct for the displayed system and the certificate role fits the leaf. The cited Benders section is provisionally relevant, but its full text is pending and it does not presently establish the additional logic-explanation/nogood claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Big-M Avoidance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact implication enforcement without artificial large coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a binary master assignment \(x\) induces a subproblem and an infeasibility certificate identifies a sufficient literal set \(S^+\subseteq\{i:x_i=1\}\) and \(S^-\subseteq\{i:x_i=0\}\). The nogood \(\sum_{i\in S^+}(1-x_i)+\sum_{i\in S^-}x_i\ge1\) excludes precisely assignments satisfying all certified literals and requires no big-\(M\) coefficient. Likewise, a valid value-function cut may be imposed directly on \((x,\theta)\) when its derivation supplies finite exact coefficients. Such cuts avoid correctness and numerical conditioning dependence on an externally chosen upper bound \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified nogoods and direct value-function cuts encode subproblem consequences without artificial large constants or dependence on a chosen big-M bound.
assumptions_latex: The literal set is sufficient to reproduce the certified infeasibility.
Any direct value-function cut is globally valid on the master domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed nogood excludes the certified conflict without introducing a big-\(M\) parameter.

notation.meaning: positive and negative literals sufficient for the conflict

review_flags: The supplied sources do not directly document big-M-free LBBD logic cuts.
standard_field_rationale: a literal nogood is an exact Boolean clause and contains no scaling constant.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits Big-M Avoidance and the displayed nogood is a correct big-M-free conflict clause, but no source supports the broader LBBD claim about direct value-function cuts and numerical/correctness independence from an external M.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Support Nogoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion-minimal literal explanations of subproblem infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), let \(\bar x\) induce an infeasible subproblem. A support \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is an infeasibility support if every assignment \(x\) satisfying \(x_i=\bar x_i\) for all \(i\in S\) also induces infeasibility. Its nogood is \(\sum_{i\in S:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)+\sum_{i\in S:\bar x_i=0}x_i\ge1\). The support is minimal when no proper subset of \(S\) is an infeasibility support. Minimality is inclusion-based and does not necessarily imply minimum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal-support nogood uses an inclusion-minimal set of fixed literals sufficient to make the induced subproblem infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is binary and induces an infeasible subproblem.
Subproblem feasibility is determined by the master assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is minimal exactly when it is sufficient for infeasibility and every \(S'\subsetneq S\) is insufficient.
review_flags: A source for minimal conflict or minimal nogood terminology in LBBD is required.
standard_field_rationale: inclusion-minimality is the standard irreducibility predicate for conflict supports.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, the nogood formula is correct, and inclusion-minimality is properly distinguished from minimum cardinality. An authoritative locator for this terminology and its LBBD use is still absent.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Subproblem Processing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous parallel evaluation of separable LBBD subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a master assignment \(x^k\) induces independent subproblems \(P_j(x^k)\) for \(j\in J\). Dispatch all \(P_j(x^k)\) concurrently, solve each to the required certification accuracy, and collect feasibility certificates, values \(Q_j(x^k)\), and valid cuts. If any component is infeasible, add its feasibility cuts and reject an incumbent assignment. Otherwise set the verified recourse value to \(Q(x^k)=\sum_{j\in J}Q_j(x^k)\) and add component or aggregated optimality cuts. Advance the synchronized master iteration only after all results used in its bound or incumbent decision have returned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent subproblems are solved concurrently; their certificates and values are synchronized before the master accepts an incumbent or updates a bound.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(x^k\), the subproblem feasible sets are independent across \(j\in J\).
The total recourse objective is additive across components.
Every worker returns a valid certificate or certified value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x^k)=\sum_{j\in J}Q_j(x^k)\) when all components are feasible; any infeasible component certifies global infeasibility of \(x^k\).

notation.meaning: component subproblem j induced by x

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports parallel LBBD processing.
standard_field_rationale: conditional separability permits independent concurrent solution and additive value aggregation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Parallel Subproblem Processing, and the conclusion follows under conditional independence and additive recourse, but synchronous aggregation and certification behavior lack a supporting LBBD source.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Logic-Based Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive LBBD across a finite hierarchy of master and subproblem levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let levels \(\ell=0,\ldots,L\) form a finite hierarchy in which a decision \(x_\ell\) induces the optimization problem at level \(\ell+1\). At level \(L\), solve the terminal problem exactly. For \(\ell=L-1,\ldots,0\), treat the complete certified result from level \(\ell+1\) as the subproblem oracle: return a feasibility explanation or value cut valid for level \(\ell\), add it to that level's master, and repeat until its stopping test holds. Propagate an incumbent value upward only after every descendant value used in it is certified; the root solution is the algorithm output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested LBBD recursively solves child decompositions and propagates only certified feasibility explanations, value cuts, and incumbent values to parent levels.
assumptions_latex: The decomposition hierarchy has finite depth \(L\).
Every child-level cut returned to its parent is valid for the parent's domain.
Each level terminates under its own exactness or tolerance rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A certified root incumbent incorporates valid, certified results from every descendant level used in its objective and feasibility decision.

notation.meaning: decision vector at hierarchy level ell

review_flags: A dedicated source for recursive or nested LBBD is unavailable in the supplied inventory.
standard_field_rationale: recursive oracle certification is the natural multilevel extension of exact decomposition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Nested Logic-Based Decomposition, but the recursive oracle protocol, upward certification rule, and root-level correctness claim require a dedicated multilevel or nested LBBD source.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Logic-Based Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested LBBD for a finite deterministic stage hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let stages be indexed by \(t=1,\ldots,T\). At stage \(t\), a master selects \(y_t\in Y_t(y_{1:t-1})\) and carries an underestimate \(\theta_{t+1}\) of the downstream value \(Q_{t+1}(y_{1:t})\). Initialize every stage with no cuts. Given a trial history \(\bar y_{1:t}\), recursively solve stage \(t+1\); if it is feasible, return its value and add a valid cut \(\theta_{t+1}\geq \beta_{t,k}(y_{1:t})\), where \(\beta_{t,k}\leq Q_{t+1}\) on the stage-history domain. If it is infeasible, add a valid history-elimination cut. Reoptimize affected ancestor masters. Stop when every selected history is feasible and every active estimate equals its recursively evaluated downstream value; output \(y_{1:T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively solve downstream stages, propagate valid value or infeasibility cuts to their parent masters, and stop when all selected histories are feasible and exactly valued.
assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\), and every stage problem is solved exactly.
Every returned cut is globally valid on its stated stage-history domain.
Each stage master has a finite attainable assignment set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon termination, the returned history \(y_{1:T}\) is globally optimal for the finite multistage model.
review_flags: Exact finite multistage LBBD formulation and convergence source required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the multistage-decomposition container, but no citation supports the recursive convergence claim. A source must also clarify that the stated stopping test constitutes a valid root-level optimality certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Logic-Based Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asynchronous LBBD with globally valid cuts and delayed oracle responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c(y)+Q(y):y\in Y\}\), maintain a master containing \(\theta\geq\beta_k(y)\), a queue of unevaluated assignments, and an incumbent upper bound \(U\). Repeatedly solve the current master, dispatch any new assignment \(\bar y\) to an exact subproblem worker, and continue without waiting. When a response arrives, add either a globally valid value cut \(\theta\geq\beta_{\bar y}(y)\) with \(\beta_{\bar y}\leq Q\), or a globally valid feasibility cut excluding no feasible assignment; update \(U\) from feasible responses. Stop only when the master lower bound \(L\) satisfies \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\) and every outstanding assignment with possible bound below \(U-\varepsilon\) has been resolved or dominated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Master iterations continue while exact subproblems run independently; delayed cuts remain safe if globally valid, and termination waits for every potentially improving response.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is finite, and master and subproblem solves are exact.
Every dispatched task eventually returns unless its assignment is already validly dominated.
Cuts remain valid independently of the master state at which they arrive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned incumbent has objective value at most \(\varepsilon\) above the global optimum.

notation.meaning: current global lower and incumbent upper bounds

review_flags: Asynchronous LBBD termination and delayed-cut validity source required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and topic fit, but the delayed-response termination rule and the meaning of an outstanding assignment having a possible bound below the incumbent require a precise asynchronous-decomposition source.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Loop Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical solve-check-cut LBBD integration outside solver callbacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite master domain \(Y\), initialize a master \(\min\{c(y)+\theta:y\in Y,\ \theta\geq\ell\}\), an incumbent bound \(U=+\infty\), and no Benders cuts. At iteration \(k\), solve the master to obtain \((y^k,\theta^k)\) and lower bound \(L_k\). Solve the exact logical subproblem at \(y^k\). If infeasible, add a valid cut excluding \(y^k\) but no feasible master assignment. If feasible with value \(Q(y^k)\), update \(U\) and, when \(\theta^k<Q(y^k)\), add a valid inequality \(\theta\geq\beta_k(y)\) satisfying \(\beta_k(y)\leq Q(y)\) for all \(y\in Y\). Stop when \(U-L_k\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternately solve the master and exact logical subproblem, add feasibility or value cuts, and terminate when the incumbent and master bounds meet within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is finite and \(\ell\leq Q(y)\) for every feasible \(y\).
Master and subproblem solves are exact.
Every generated cut is valid on \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent returned at termination is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal; with \(\varepsilon=0\), it is globally optimal.

notation.meaning: master estimate of the subproblem value
master lower and incumbent upper bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Lazy-Constraint Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent-triggered enforcement of omitted LBBD constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the master solver minimize \(c(y)+\theta\) over an initial relaxation. Whenever it produces an integer incumbent candidate \((\bar y,\bar\theta)\), solve the exact logical subproblem. If \(\bar y\) is infeasible, submit through the lazy-constraint interface a globally valid feasibility inequality violated by \(\bar y\). If it is feasible with value \(Q(\bar y)\) and \(\bar\theta<Q(\bar y)\), submit a globally valid value inequality \(\theta\geq\beta_{\bar y}(y)\), where \(\beta_{\bar y}(y)\leq Q(y)\) for every feasible integer \(y\) and \(\beta_{\bar y}(\bar y)=Q(\bar y)\). Accept an incumbent only when neither test yields a violated inequality; return the solver-certified optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each integer incumbent, solve the logical subproblem and lazily reject the candidate with a valid feasibility or underestimated-value constraint when necessary.
assumptions_latex: The solver invokes the callback for every incumbent candidate requiring omitted-constraint validation.
Submitted lazy constraints are valid for every feasible integer solution.
The subproblem oracle is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any accepted incumbent satisfies the omitted logical requirements, and solver-certified termination yields a global optimum.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incumbent-validation algorithm fits the lazy-constraint container, but its global-optimality conclusion depends on solver callback guarantees that are not cited.

children.title: User-Cut Callback Integration
children.top_down_role: Solver integration through callbacks accepting globally valid user cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: User-Cut Callback Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fractional-node strengthening using globally valid inequalities that preserve all intended feasible integer solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be the current global master relaxation and let \(F_I\subseteq R\) be the intended feasible integer set. At a fractional relaxation solution \((\bar y,\bar\theta)\in R\), call a separation oracle for an inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}y+d\theta\geq b\) that is valid for every point of \(F_I\). If \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar y+d\bar\theta<b-\tau\) and the solver permits the inequality as a user cut, submit it; otherwise submit nothing. Enforce omitted logical requirements that must be checked at integer incumbents through a lazy-constraint or equivalent incumbent-validation mechanism. Submit an inequality valid only within one branch-and-bound subtree solely through an interface that preserves its node-local scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At fractional nodes, submit user cuts that may remove relaxation points but preserve every intended feasible integer solution. Use incumbent validation for omitted logical requirements and keep subtree-valid deductions local.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau\geq0\) is the separation tolerance.
The separation oracle certifies validity for every point of \(F_I\).
The solver interface distinguishes global user cuts, incumbent enforcement, and node-local constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every submitted global user cut preserves \(F_I\) while potentially strengthening \(R\).
review_flags: An authoritative branch-and-cut callback source is required.

children.title: Node-Callback Integration
children.top_down_role: Solver integration through callbacks tied to branch-search nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Callback Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-level orchestration of relaxation separation, incumbent validation, and subtree-local deductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\) be a branch-and-bound node, let \(R_v\) be its relaxation, let \(F_I\) be the intended global feasible integer set, and let \(F_{I,v}\subseteq F_I\) be the feasible integer solutions compatible with the branching decisions at \(v\). When the solver exposes a fractional solution in \(R_v\), submit a global user cut only if it is valid for every point of \(F_I\); submit a node-local cut only if it is valid for every point of \(F_{I,v}\) and the interface enforces it solely in that subtree. When the solver exposes an integer incumbent candidate, solve the exact logical subproblem and reject the candidate through an incumbent-capable interface whenever it violates a globally valid feasibility or value constraint. Accept the candidate only after exact validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a node, global cuts must preserve every globally feasible integer solution, local cuts must preserve feasible solutions in that subtree, and integer incumbents require exact logical-subproblem validation.
assumptions_latex: The solver identifies the callback context and node scope correctly.
The logical subproblem oracle is exact for integer incumbent candidates.
Each submitted inequality is installed only with a scope on which its validity has been certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The integration preserves every point of \(F_I\) and accepts no incumbent that violates the exact logical subproblem.

notation.meaning: feasible integer set within the subtree rooted at v

review_flags: Solver-specific callback-context and scope guarantees require an authoritative source.

children.title: Callback Eligibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Restrictions governing which decomposition information may enter each callback class.

knowledge_statements.title: Callback Eligibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and enforcement boundaries among global user cuts, lazy constraints, and node-local deductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be the global master relaxation, let \(F_I\subseteq R\) be the intended feasible integer set, and let \(F_{I,v}\subseteq F_I\) be the feasible integer solutions in the subtree rooted at node \(v\). A global user cut may be violated by points of \(R\), but it must hold for every point of \(F_I\) and must satisfy the solver's requirements for relaxation strengthening. A lazy constraint must likewise preserve \(F_I\), but it is used to enforce an omitted model requirement through an incumbent-capable interface. An inequality certified only for \(F_{I,v}\) is eligible solely for node-local enforcement in that subtree. Installing a subtree-valid inequality globally can delete feasible integer solutions outside the subtree, while relying on a user-cut interface to enforce an essential omitted constraint can permit an invalid incumbent if that interface does not guarantee incumbent enforcement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global user cuts may remove fractional relaxation points but must preserve all intended feasible integer solutions. Lazy constraints enforce omitted requirements at incumbents, while subtree-valid deductions must remain local.
assumptions_latex: \(F_I\subseteq R\) and \(F_{I,v}\subseteq F_I\).
The solver may assign different enforcement guarantees to user-cut, lazy-constraint, and local-constraint interfaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A callback submission is sound only if the inequality preserves every feasible integer solution in its enforced scope and the selected interface supplies the required enforcement behavior.

notation.meaning: feasible integer set in the subtree rooted at node v

review_flags: Authoritative documentation is required for the callback-role and enforcement distinctions.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid MIP–CP Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MIP master with an exact constraint-programming subproblem oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition decisions into master variables \(y\in Y\) handled by MIP and subproblem variables \(x\in X(y)\) handled by CP. The MIP master minimizes \(c(y)+\theta\). For each integer trial \(\bar y\), solve the CP model exactly. If it is infeasible, extract an explanation \(E\) and add a MIP-representable inequality excluding every assignment satisfying \(E\) while excluding no extendable assignment. If it is feasible with optimum \(Q(\bar y)\), update the incumbent and add a MIP-representable lower estimator \(\theta\geq\beta_E(y)\) that is valid for all \(y\in Y\) and tight at \(\bar y\). Iterate until the MIP lower bound meets the incumbent bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A MIP master proposes linking decisions; an exact CP oracle returns infeasibility explanations or valid value cuts until global lower and upper bounds coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is finite and the CP oracle solves each fixed-master subproblem exactly.
Every CP explanation is translated into a globally valid MIP inequality.
Every value estimator satisfies \(\beta_E(y)\leq Q(y)\) on \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At bound convergence, the returned MIP–CP solution is globally optimal.
review_flags: Hybrid MIP–CP LBBD cut-translation source required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits hybrid MIP–CP integration, but the explanation-to-MIP translation, globally valid value estimator, and convergence claim require a direct LBBD or hybrid-optimization source.
