knowledge_statements.title: Exact Decision-Diagram Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact layered decision diagram representing every feasible subproblem assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed master assignment \(y\), let \(S(y)\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\) be the subproblem feasible set. A layered acyclic diagram \(G_y=(V,A)\), with one source and one sink, is exact when the labels of its source-to-sink paths are in bijection with \(S(y)\). If each arc at layer \(i\) carries the contribution of its label to an additively separable objective \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\), then feasibility is equivalent to existence of a source-to-sink path and \(Q(y)=\min_{P}\sum_{a\in P}w_a\). Consequently, an exact reachability or shortest-path computation is an exact LBBD subproblem oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact layered diagram has precisely the feasible assignments as source-to-sink paths; reachability decides feasibility and shortest path returns the exact subproblem value.
assumptions_latex: Every path selects exactly one label from each domain \(D_i\).
Arc weights reproduce the stated additive objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The diagram oracle returns the exact feasibility status and, when feasible, the exact value \(Q(y)\).

notation.meaning: feasible subproblem assignments for master decision y

review_flags: Exact decision-diagram oracle representation source required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-diagram representation and shortest-path interpretation are coherent and fit the container, but no source supports the exactness convention or its use as an LBBD oracle.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Decision-Diagram Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Superset diagram yielding safe minimization lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(y\), let \(S(y)\) be the feasible assignments of a minimization subproblem and let \(G_y^R\) be a layered diagram whose represented path-label set \(S^R(y)\) satisfies \(S(y)\subseteq S^R(y)\). Give every represented assignment its original objective value \(f(x)\), and define \(L^R(y)=\min\{f(x):x\in S^R(y)\}\). Then \(L^R(y)\leq Q(y)=\min\{f(x):x\in S(y)\}\). Absence of a source-to-sink path certifies infeasibility of the original subproblem; existence of a path does not certify feasibility unless its labels are checked against the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed diagram represents a superset of feasible assignments, so its shortest path is a safe lower bound; only path absence certifies infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The original subproblem is a minimization problem.
\(S(y)\subseteq S^R(y)\), and diagram weights reproduce \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L^R(y)\leq Q(y)\), and \(S^R(y)=\varnothing\) implies \(S(y)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: assignments represented by the relaxed diagram

review_flags: Relaxed decision-diagram bound and certification source required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimization lower-bound and one-sided infeasibility statements are mathematically consistent and the representation kind fits, but they lack a cited decision-diagram source.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Decision-Diagram Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subset diagram yielding feasible solutions and minimization upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(y\), let \(S(y)\) be the feasible assignments of a minimization subproblem and let \(G_y^D\) be a layered diagram representing \(S^D(y)\subseteq S(y)\). With original objective weights, define \(U^D(y)=\min\{f(x):x\in S^D(y)\}\) when \(S^D(y)\neq\varnothing\), and \(U^D(y)=+\infty\) otherwise. Every source-to-sink path supplies a feasible subproblem assignment, and \(Q(y)\leq U^D(y)\). However, an empty restricted diagram does not certify that \(S(y)=\varnothing\), because feasible assignments may have been discarded during restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted diagram retains only feasible assignments, so every path is feasible and its best value is an upper bound; emptiness does not prove infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The original subproblem is a minimization problem.
\(S^D(y)\subseteq S(y)\), and diagram weights reproduce \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(S^D(y)\neq\varnothing\), then \(Q(y)\leq U^D(y)\); if it is empty, no exact feasibility conclusion follows.

notation.meaning: assignments retained by the restricted diagram

review_flags: Restricted decision-diagram bound and certification source required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subset representation, minimization upper bound, and warning about empty restricted diagrams are coherent and fit the container, but no supporting source is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted-Diagram Value Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic-programming evaluation of a weighted acyclic decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite acyclic decision diagram with source \(r\), sink \(t\), and arc weights \(w:A\to\mathbb R\). Initialize \(d(r)=0\) and \(d(v)=+\infty\) for \(v\neq r\). Process vertices in topological order and apply \(d(v)\leftarrow\min\{d(v),d(u)+w(u,v)\}\) for every arc \((u,v)\in A\). If \(d(t)<+\infty\), return \(d(t)\) and predecessor labels defining a minimum-weight assignment; otherwise return infeasible. When the diagram is exact and path weights equal subproblem objective values, the returned number equals \(Q(y)\). Relaxed or restricted diagrams instead return the corresponding lower or upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Topological shortest-path dynamic programming evaluates a weighted diagram, returning an exact value for exact diagrams and the appropriate bound for relaxed or restricted diagrams.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acyclic.
Each source-to-sink path weight equals the represented assignment's objective value.
The diagram's exact, relaxed, or restricted status is known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle runs in \(O(|V|+|A|)\) time and returns the minimum represented path value or infeasibility of the represented set.

notation.meaning: exact subproblem value for fixed master decision y

review_flags: Weighted decision-diagram oracle and complexity source required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The topological shortest-path algorithm fits a weighted-diagram value oracle, and its linear-time claim is standard for finite DAGs, but the record supplies no citation for either the oracle interpretation or complexity bound.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Equivalence Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact merging condition for nodes in a layered decision diagram representing a finite subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_i\) be the histories reaching layer \(i\). For \(h,h'\in H_i\), define \(h\sim_i h'\) precisely when they admit the same feasible suffix-label sequences and every common suffix has the same remaining objective contribution after removing history-dependent constants. A node aggregation \(\mu_i:H_i\to V_i\) is state-exact when \[\mu_i(h)=\mu_i(h')\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h\sim_i h'.\] Thus a diagram node contains exactly one behavioral equivalence class and retains all information needed to determine feasible continuations and their costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagram state is exact precisely when it merges histories if and only if they have identical feasible continuations and identical remaining objective contributions.
assumptions_latex: H_i is the finite set of histories reaching layer i.
The subproblem objective admits a history contribution plus a suffix contribution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu_i(h)=\mu_i(h')\iff h\sim_i h'

notation.meaning: Behavioral state-equivalence relation at layer i
Map assigning histories to diagram nodes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the decision-diagram-specific equivalence condition. A source must also confirm whether exactness requires nodes to coincide exactly with behavioral equivalence classes, rather than merely forbidding behaviorally inequivalent merges.

children.title: Transition Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness considerations for represented state transitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Transition Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence between diagram arcs and feasible one-step extensions of represented histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_i\) represent exact state classes and let \(T_i\subseteq V_i\times A_i\times V_{i+1}\) be the labeled diagram transitions. Transition exactness holds when, for every \(u\in V_i\), label \(a\in A_i\), and \(v\in V_{i+1}\), \[(u,a,v)\in T_i\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{some history in }u\text{ has a feasible }a\text{-extension whose resulting history lies in }v.\] If state classes are behaviorally equivalent, “some history” may equivalently be replaced by “every history for which the layer is reached.”
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arc exists exactly when its label is a feasible one-step extension from the source state class to the indicated successor class.
assumptions_latex: V_i consists of behaviorally exact state classes.
Each decision label determines a unique successor class whenever it is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (u,a,v)\in T_i\iff a\text{ is a feasible extension from }u\text{ into }v

notation.meaning: Decision labels available at layer i
Labeled transitions from layer i to layer i+1

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local transition characterization is plausible and fits the condition container, but no inspectable source supports the existential-to-universal claim or the stated exactness convention.

children.title: Path Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness considerations for represented source-to-terminal paths.

knowledge_statements.title: Path Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Language-level exactness for complete root-to-terminal paths of a layered decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a layered diagram \(D\), let \(\mathcal L(D)\) be the set of label sequences on its root-to-terminal paths, and let \(X\subseteq A_1\times\cdots\times A_n\) be the feasible subproblem decisions. The diagram is path-exact precisely when \[\mathcal L(D)=X.\] Equivalently, every feasible decision sequence has a root-to-terminal realization in \(D\), and every root-to-terminal path labels a feasible decision sequence; multiplicity of paths with the same label sequence is immaterial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagram is path-exact when its complete path labels are exactly the feasible decision sequences, with neither missing nor spurious sequences.
assumptions_latex: D is a finite n-layer rooted diagram.
X\subseteq A_1\times\cdots\times A_n is the subproblem feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal L(D)=X

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The language-equality formulation is mathematically precise and appropriately classified as a condition, but it has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Transition-to-Path Consistency
children.top_down_role: Structural consistency linking local transition fidelity to complete-path fidelity.

knowledge_statements.title: Transition-to-Path Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition property linking exact local transitions to exact complete paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the root represents the empty history, terminal nodes represent precisely completed feasible histories, states are behaviorally exact, and every layer satisfies transition exactness. Repeated transition composition then induces a label-preserving bijection between feasible decision sequences and equivalence classes of root-to-terminal paths: \[x\in X\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{there exists a root-to-terminal path labeled }x.\] Consequently, local transition exactness implies path exactness. Conversely, path exactness alone need not identify correct intermediate state classes or exclude locally invalid arcs that lie on no complete path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact states and exact layer transitions compose into exact complete paths; path exactness alone does not necessarily certify local transitions.
assumptions_latex: The root and terminals represent exactly the empty and completed feasible histories.
State-equivalence and transition exactness hold at every layer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal L(D)=X

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the local-to-global implication or its converse boundary. The claimed bijection also invokes equivalence classes of paths without defining the path-equivalence relation.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery of the subproblem objective from additive arc values on complete paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be path-exact for feasible set \(X\), and assign each arc \(e\) a value \(w_e\). The diagram is objective-exact for \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) when every root-to-terminal path \(p\) labeled by \(x\in X\) satisfies \[\sum_{e\in p}w_e=f(x).\] Therefore, for minimization, \[\min_{p\in\mathcal P(D)}\sum_{e\in p}w_e=\min_{x\in X}f(x),\] with the analogous equality for maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective exactness requires every complete path’s arc-value sum to equal the objective of its represented feasible decision sequence.
assumptions_latex: D is path-exact for X.
Every complete path has a finite additive arc value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{opt}_{p\in\mathcal P(D)}\sum_{e\in p}w_e=\operatorname{opt}_{x\in X}f(x)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive path-value condition and optimization equality are coherent and fit the condition container, but no decision-diagram source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Width Sufficiency for Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Layerwise width threshold sufficient to preserve every behavioral state class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each layer \(i\), let \(m_i\) be the number of reachable behavioral state-equivalence classes of the exact finite dynamic program. If a decision-diagram compilation permits width \(W_i\ge m_i\) at every layer and merges only histories from the same equivalence class, then no information-losing merge is required. With exact transitions, terminals, and arc values, the resulting diagram is state-exact, path-exact, and objective-exact. In particular, the uniform width \(W\ge\max_i m_i\) is sufficient, though it need not be necessary for representing only the optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Width at least the number of reachable behavioral classes in every layer suffices to construct an exact decision diagram.
assumptions_latex: The exact dynamic program has finitely many reachable state classes per layer.
Compilation merges histories only within behavioral equivalence classes.
Transitions, terminals, and arc values are represented exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_i\ge m_i\ \forall i\implies D\text{ is state-, path-, and objective-exact}

notation.meaning: Number of reachable exact state classes at layer i
Permitted diagram width at layer i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is correctly presented as a theorem, but its width-sufficiency and resulting-diagram claims require an authoritative decision-diagram source specifying the compilation assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed-Path Containment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-side validity condition for a relaxed decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq A_1\times\cdots\times A_n\) be the feasible decision sequences and let \(D^R\) be a relaxed layered diagram. Relaxed-path containment is the condition \[X\subseteq\mathcal L(D^R).\] Hence every feasible sequence has at least one root-to-terminal path in \(D^R\), while sequences in \(\mathcal L(D^R)\setminus X\) may be spurious. Containment is necessary for obtaining a universally valid minimization lower bound merely by minimizing compatible path values over the enlarged path language.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed diagram must contain a complete path for every feasible sequence, although it may also contain spurious paths.
assumptions_latex: X is the original feasible set.
D^R is a rooted layered diagram over the same decision labels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\subseteq\mathcal L(D^R)

notation.meaning: Complete path-label language of the relaxed diagram

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The containment condition is precise and correctly distinguishes missing from spurious paths, but no cited source supports the relaxed-decision-diagram interpretation or necessity claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Compatible Arc Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arc-value condition ensuring that relaxed shortest paths furnish minimization lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization subproblem with objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), arc values \(w_e^R\) on a relaxed diagram \(D^R\) are objective-compatible when every feasible \(x\in X\) has a representing path \(p_x\) satisfying \[\sum_{e\in p_x}w_e^R\le f(x).\] If \(X\subseteq\mathcal L(D^R)\), then \[L:=\min_{p\in\mathcal P(D^R)}\sum_{e\in p}w_e^R\le\min_{x\in X}f(x).\] Equality on every feasible representing path is a sufficient special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxed arc values are compatible when each feasible solution has a representing path whose value does not exceed its true minimization objective.
assumptions_latex: The subproblem is a minimization problem.
Every feasible sequence has a path in D^R.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\le\min_{x\in X}f(x)

notation.meaning: Relaxed value assigned to arc e
A relaxed-diagram path representing feasible sequence x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-bound implication is mathematically plausible and fits the condition container, but the decision-diagram arc-value criterion lacks an inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Spurious-Path Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating harmless feasibility relaxation from invalid objective bounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Spurious paths do not invalidate a minimization lower bound when the relaxed language contains all feasible paths and feasible representing paths have nonoverestimating values: extra paths can only decrease the relaxed minimum. Containment alone, however, is insufficient. Consider \(X=\{1\}\), \(f(1)=0\), and a relaxed diagram containing the path labeled \(1\) but assigning it value \(1\). Its minimum is \(1>0\), so it is not a lower bound. Thus objective compatibility, not merely permission of spurious paths, is the validity boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spurious paths can only improve a relaxed minimization bound, but path containment without compatible arc values can produce an invalid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Bounds are interpreted as lower bounds for minimization.
Path values are sums of arc values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\subseteq\mathcal L(D^R)\not\implies\min_{p\in\mathcal P(D^R)}w(p)\le\min_{x\in X}f(x)

notation.meaning: Sum of arc values along path p

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample supports the stated failure boundary, but no source is cited. The plain statement should also retain the LaTeX statement's qualification that harmless spurious paths require containment and nonoverestimating feasible-path values.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram-Bound Transfer to the Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity certificate for importing a relaxed diagram bound into a minimization master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\in Y\) be a master assignment, let \(Q(y)\) be the associated minimization-subproblem value, and let \(L(y)\) be the minimum objective-compatible path value in a relaxed diagram conditioned on \(y\). If \(L(y)\le Q(y)\) for every \(y\in Y\), then the master constraint \[\theta\ge L(y)\] is valid for any epigraph variable required ultimately to satisfy \(\theta\ge Q(y)\). The pointwise inequality is the certificate: the transferred constraint cannot exclude any pair \((y,\theta)\) in the true epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed diagram bound transfers validly when it underestimates every conditioned subproblem value; then requiring the master epigraph variable to exceed it is safe.
assumptions_latex: Q(y) is the value of a minimization subproblem for every y\in Y.
L(y) is finite and satisfies L(y)\le Q(y) pointwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{(y,\theta):\theta\ge Q(y)\}\subseteq\{(y,\theta):\theta\ge L(y)\}

notation.meaning: True subproblem value at master assignment y
Master epigraph variable for the subproblem value

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The epigraph inclusion is correct pointwise, and certificate is an appropriate content kind. A logic-based Benders source must establish how the functional constraint involving L(y) is represented or generated in the master.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Width Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity of minimization bounds for a nested family of width-limited relaxed diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_W^R\) be relaxed diagrams for a minimization subproblem, with objective-compatible path values inherited consistently across widths. If increasing width produces nested path languages \[\mathcal L(D_{W_2}^R)\subseteq\mathcal L(D_{W_1}^R)\quad\text{whenever }W_1\le W_2,\] then their lower bounds satisfy \[L_{W_1}\le L_{W_2}\le Q^*,\qquad L_W:=\min_{p\in\mathcal P(D_W^R)}w(p).\] Thus greater width weakly strengthens the bound under nesting; width alone gives no such guarantee without the inclusion relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When wider relaxed diagrams have nested, smaller path languages and consistent values, their minimization lower bounds can only improve.
assumptions_latex: Each D_W^R contains every feasible path.
Path values are objective-compatible and consistent across widths.
Path languages are nested in decreasing order as width grows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_1\le W_2\implies L_{W_1}\le L_{W_2}\le Q^*

notation.meaning: Relaxed diagram compiled with width W

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the container, but label-language nesting alone does not compare path values. The meaning of values being inherited consistently requires a sourced, formal path- or label-level condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Refinement-Order Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound monotonicity under language refinement, independently of numerical diagram width.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For relaxed diagrams \(D_1^R\) and \(D_2^R\), write \(D_1^R\preceq D_2^R\) when every complete path of \(D_2^R\) maps label- and value-preservingly to a complete path of \(D_1^R\); equivalently, the second diagram removes possibilities without altering retained path values. For minimization, \[D_1^R\preceq D_2^R\quad\Longrightarrow\quad L(D_1^R)\le L(D_2^R).\] If both diagrams retain all feasible paths and have objective-compatible values, both quantities remain lower bounds on the true optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed diagram that removes paths while preserving retained path values gives a weakly stronger minimization lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Both diagrams represent the same minimization subproblem.
Refinement preserves labels and values of retained paths.
Both diagrams contain every feasible path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_1^R\preceq D_2^R\implies L(D_1^R)\le L(D_2^R)\le Q^*

notation.meaning: Minimum complete-path value in diagram D

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The value-preserving path-map condition suffices for the stated minimization monotonicity and fits the property container, but neither the refinement order nor its lower-bound interpretation has an inspectable citation.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is the exact feasible label set.
\(R_1,R_2\supseteq F\) are path-label sets of relaxed layered decision diagrams.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_1\nsubseteq R_2\land R_2\nsubseteq R_1\), so neither width nor feasibility relaxation alone orders the induced bounds.

notation.meaning: minimum objective value over a set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for comparing relaxed diagrams that are not nested by path-set inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, let \(F=\{00\}\), \(R_1=\{00,01\}\), and \(R_2=\{00,10\}\). Both \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) relax \(F\), but they are non-nested. If \(c(00)=1\), \(c(01)=0\), and \(c(10)=2\), then \(b_c(R_1)=0<b_c(R_2)=1\). Exchanging the costs of \(01\) and \(10\) reverses this inequality. Consequently, without path-set inclusion, increasing compilation width or applying unrelated merges does not by itself imply monotone bound improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two relaxed diagrams can both contain every feasible solution yet contain different spurious paths; then their minimization bounds can occur in either order.
knowledge_statements.title: Non-Nested Compilation Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly shows that two non-nested relaxed path sets can yield bounds in either order, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. However, no inspectable decision-diagram source is cited, and the final claim about increasing compilation width is broader than the example unless width-indexed diagrams are explicitly linked to these non-nested path sets.

assumptions_latex: \(D^k\) is a layered relaxed decision diagram with layer states partitioning exact histories.
A chosen merged state contains histories with distinct exact continuation behavior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_i^{k+1}\prec\mathcal P_i^k\) and the refined diagram removes only transitions invalid for the new state blocks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition-based splitting of merged states in a relaxed layered decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(D^k\), a layer \(i\), and a predicate \(q\) separating histories in one block \(B\in\mathcal P_i^k\). Replace \(B\) by the nonempty blocks \(B_0=\{h\in B:q(h)=0\}\) and \(B_1=\{h\in B:q(h)=1\}\). Redirect each incoming arc according to its history, duplicate or redirect outgoing arcs according to valid continuations, and delete arcs lacking a compatible history. Propagate splitting forward when transition consistency requires it. Output \(D^{k+1}\); stop when the required bound or exactness test succeeds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split a merged state using a distinguishing predicate, redirect compatible arcs, propagate consistency, and repeat until the desired exactness or bound test passes.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Splitting Refinement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits State-Splitting Refinement, and the variables are introduced consistently. The rules for redirecting arcs, propagating splits, preserving relaxation validity, and stopping are specialized algorithmic claims with no cited source or precise invariant establishing them.

assumptions_latex: \(D^k\) is a relaxed diagram whose paths include every exact feasible solution.
An exact checker returns a spurious path or certifies that none exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Paths}(D^{k+1})\subsetneq\operatorname{Paths}(D^k)\) whenever the returned counterexample is eliminated.

notation.meaning: selected path in the relaxed diagram

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample-guided elimination of spurious relaxed-diagram paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a relaxed diagram \(D^0\). At iteration \(k\), select a path \(p^k\) relevant to the current optimization bound and submit its label sequence to the exact checker. If \(p^k\in F\), retain it and apply the prescribed optimality test. Otherwise obtain a layer and distinguishing history predicate witnessing infeasibility, split the implicated merged state, and rebuild affected transitions while preserving all paths in \(F\). Stop when the checker finds no bound-relevant spurious path; output the resulting diagram and its certified bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check a bound-relevant relaxed path; when it is spurious, use the checker’s witness to split states and eliminate that path without losing feasible ones.
knowledge_statements.title: Counterexample-Guided Refinement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the terminal container. No source supports the assumed checker interface, the existence of a distinguishing predicate from every spurious path, or the assertion that absence of a bound-relevant spurious path certifies the reported bound; these details determine whether the algorithm is mathematically valid.

assumptions_latex: Each layer \(i\) has a finite exact state set \(S_i\).
Every unsuccessful iteration strictly splits a current block and never merges distinct exact states.
The stopping test accepts exactly when all relevant blocks are behaviorally exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\leq\sum_i\bigl(|S_i|-|\mathcal P_i^0|\bigr)\) strict refinement iterations suffice for exact recovery.

notation.meaning: finite exact state set at layer i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite recovery under strict partition refinement of finite exact state spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every layer \(i\), a partition can undergo at most \(|S_i|-|\mathcal P_i^0|\) strict block-splitting steps before reaching the singleton partition. Because each unsuccessful iteration strictly increases the number of blocks in at least one layer and no iteration reverses a split, the process terminates after at most \(\sum_i(|S_i|-|\mathcal P_i^0|)\) such iterations. Under the exact stopping-test assumption, the terminal diagram represents precisely the relevant exact continuations and therefore recovers the exact subproblem value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finite exact state sets and irreversible strict splits, refinement reaches an exact diagram after at most the total number of missing partition blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Exact-Recovery Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind is appropriate, and the partition-count bound is plausible under the stated irreversible strict-splitting assumptions. An authoritative source is still required for the decision-diagram exactness implication and for the precise meaning of behaviorally exact relevant blocks and the exact stopping test.

assumptions_latex: \(D^k\) contains a bound-relevant spurious path \(p\notin F\).
Every admissible refinement leaves the state partition traversed by \(p\) unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in\operatorname{Paths}(D^{k+1})\) and the refinement process need not improve its bound or terminate exactly.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by a refinement language unable to separate a persistent spurious path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(p\) is spurious because two exact histories require different continuation states, but the permitted predicates assign those histories identically at every implicated layer. Then every admissible state split preserves the merged block and hence preserves \(p\). Repeated checker calls may return the same counterexample, while the relaxed bound remains unchanged. Thus finite exact recovery requires more than finite state spaces: the refinement language and selection rule must eventually separate every behaviorally incompatible pair relevant to a persistent spurious path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refinement can stall when its predicates cannot distinguish histories responsible for a persistent spurious path, even though the exact state space is finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Stalled-Refinement Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the leaf, but unchanged states traversed by p do not alone ensure that p survives: an admissible refinement could alter or remove a transition used by p without splitting those states. The allowable-refinement model and persistence condition require a source and stronger specification.

assumptions_latex: The diagram has \(n\) transition layers, maximum width \(W\), and at most \(d\) labels per state.
Each successor computation and merge-key evaluation costs \(O(1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T=O(nWd)\) and streaming workspace is \(O(Wd+W)\), excluding storage of all completed layers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-sensitive compilation with a fixed maximum layer width and constant-time transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A layerwise compiler expands at most \(W\) states through at most \(d\) labels in each of \(n\) layers, then merges or discards generated states to restore width at most \(W\). Under constant-time successor and merge-key operations, it examines at most \(nWd\) candidate transitions. Hence compilation takes \(O(nWd)\) time. If only the current and next layers are retained, states and candidate arcs require \(O(W+Wd)\) workspace. This bound controls compilation resources but does not imply exactness or a prescribed relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With width capped at W and d labels per state, layerwise compilation uses O(nWd) time and O(Wd+W) streaming memory under constant-time transitions.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Width Compilation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind fits Bounded-Width Compilation. The O(nWd) claim requires more than constant-time successor and merge-key evaluation: restoring width W must also have bounded total processing cost, and generated-state storage or deduplication must follow the stated workspace model. No supporting source is cited.

assumptions_latex: \(D_W\) is a relaxed minimization diagram of width at most \(W\).
\(\operatorname{Paths}(D_{W+1})\subseteq\operatorname{Paths}(D_W)\) and both contain \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_W\leq b_{W+1}\leq z^*\), but no instance-independent convergence rate follows from width alone.

notation.meaning: minimum path cost in the width-W relaxed diagram

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone minimization bounds for nested width-indexed relaxed diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(b_W=\min\{c(p):p\in\operatorname{Paths}(D_W)\}\) and \(z^*=\min\{c(x):x\in F\}\). Path-set nesting gives \(b_W\leq b_{W+1}\), while relaxation validity gives \(b_{W+1}\leq z^*\). Width alone supplies no positive universal improvement rate: a refinement may remove no optimal spurious path, yielding \(b_{W+1}=b_W\), or a single additional state may eliminate the unique cheapest spurious path and close an arbitrarily large objective gap after cost scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested relaxed diagrams give nondecreasing lower bounds as width grows, but width alone guarantees neither strict improvement nor an instance-independent convergence rate.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Quality Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the leaf, and the nested-set inequalities are mathematically consistent for minimization. The stronger assertion that width alone admits no instance-independent improvement rate, including its cost-scaling construction, has no inspectable source or fully specified width-indexed compilation model.

assumptions_latex: The diagram has layer widths \(w_i\leq W\) and at most \(d\) outgoing labels per state.
Transition generation has constant unit cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T=O(nWd)\), \(M_{\mathrm{stored}}=O(nW+nWd)\), and \(M_{\mathrm{stream}}=O(W+Wd)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compilation and storage bounds for explicit bounded-width layered diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Explicit compilation generates at most \(nWd\) arcs and stores at most \((n+1)W\) nodes. Retaining the entire diagram therefore requires \(O(nW+nWd)\) memory and \(O(nWd)\) transition work. A streaming compiler retaining only adjacent layers reduces workspace to \(O(W+Wd)\), but discards direct access to earlier layers unless they are recomputed or externally stored. Increasing \(W\) can strengthen a nested relaxation, while time and explicit memory scale linearly in \(W\) under this cost model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit storage scales with all layers, while streaming stores adjacent layers only; both compilation time and memory grow linearly with the width cap under the stated model.
knowledge_statements.title: Time–Memory–Width Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind fits the resource-tradeoff container. The counts are plausible for an explicit bounded-degree layered diagram, but the record lacks a source and does not fully account for the representation cost of states, arc payloads, merge structures, and externally stored output in its memory bounds.

children.title: State-Space Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity attributable to the number and organization of diagram states.

assumptions_latex: At layer \(i\), \(S_i\) is the set of reachable exact dynamic-programming states.
Each state representation occupies \(\sigma_i\) memory units.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N=\sum_{i=0}^{n}|S_i|\) and \(M=\Theta\!\left(\sum_{i=0}^{n}|S_i|\sigma_i\right)\) for explicit state storage.

notation.meaning: reachable exact states at layer i
storage size of one layer-i state

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit node complexity induced by reachable exact dynamic-programming states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Canonical exact compilation creates one node for each reachable state at each layer, after identifying histories with the same sufficient state. Consequently, the node count is \(N=\sum_{i=0}^{n}|S_i|\), the maximum layer width is \(\max_i|S_i|\), and explicit state storage is \(\Theta(\sum_i|S_i|\sigma_i)\). If states have constant-size representations, storage is \(\Theta(N)\); if \(|S_i|\) grows exponentially with \(i\), exact diagram size can be exponential even when each transition is inexpensive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact state-based diagram has one node per reachable state per layer, so its size is the sum of layer state counts and may be exponential.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Space Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind fits State-Space Complexity. One node per reachable state per layer holds only for the specified canonical state-based compilation and sufficient-state equivalence; no decision-diagram source is cited for that representation contract or the resulting exact node count.

children.title: Transition-Relation Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity attributable to the number and organization of diagram transitions.

assumptions_latex: \(T_i\subseteq S_{i-1}\times A_i\times S_i\) is the reachable transition relation at layer \(i\).
Testing or generating one transition costs \(\tau_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E=\sum_{i=1}^{n}|T_i|\) and explicit transition processing costs \(\Theta\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}|T_i|\tau_i\right)\).

notation.meaning: reachable transition relation at layer i
cost per generated transition at layer i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-sensitive complexity of explicitly generating reachable decision-diagram transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An explicit layered diagram contains exactly one arc for each represented reachable transition, so its arc count is \(E=\sum_i|T_i|\). Enumerating and recording those arcs requires \(\Theta(\sum_i|T_i|\tau_i)\) work in an output-sensitive model. If every state has at most \(d_i\) candidate labels, then \(|T_i|\leq |S_{i-1}|d_i\); equality need not hold because labels may be infeasible or distinct labels may be represented implicitly. Transition complexity can therefore dominate node complexity when branching is large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit arc count equals the number of represented reachable transitions; generation time is output-sensitive and may dominate node complexity when branching is large.
knowledge_statements.title: Transition-Relation Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind fits Transition-Relation Complexity. The arc-count identity is definitional for an explicit representation, but the Theta processing bound depends on whether tau_i includes enumeration, testing, deduplication, and recording costs. No source establishes the stated output-sensitive model.

children.title: State–Transition Scaling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes distinguished by how state growth interacts with transition growth.

assumptions_latex: \(s_i=|S_i|\), \(t_i=|T_i|\), and every transition has unit processing cost.
The diagram is compiled explicitly by layers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T=\Theta(\sum_i t_i)\), with \(t_i\leq s_{i-1}s_i\) and, under label branching \(d_i\), \(t_i\leq s_{i-1}d_i\).

notation.meaning: reachable state count at layer i
reachable transition count at layer i
candidate label count at layer i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse, label-bounded, and dense transition regimes for explicit compilation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a sparse regime with \(t_i=\Theta(s_i+s_{i-1})\), transition work is linear in adjacent state counts. In a label-bounded regime, \(t_i\leq s_{i-1}d_i\), giving \(O(\sum_i s_{i-1}d_i)\) work. In a dense bipartite regime, \(t_i=\Theta(s_{i-1}s_i)\), so arc processing can be quadratic in layer width. Thus identical state-space sizes can yield different compilation costs; the governing quantity is the represented transition relation, not state count alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compilation is linear in state counts for sparse transitions, label-bounded under limited branching, and potentially quadratic in layer width for dense adjacent-layer transitions.
knowledge_statements.title: State–Transition Scaling Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind fits the scaling-regime leaf. The bound t_i <= s_{i-1}s_i is not valid for labeled multigraphs unless at most one represented arc is allowed for each ordered state pair; that assumption is absent and may conflict with the separate label-branching model. A source and a precise arc model are required.

assumptions_latex: The layered diagram has widths \(w_0,\ldots,w_n\) and maximum width \(W\).
Each node has at most \(d\\) outgoing arcs and arc processing has unit cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|V|=\sum_{i=0}^{n}w_i\leq(n+1)W\) and \(|A|\leq d\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}w_i\leq nWd\).

notation.meaning: number of nodes in layer i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node, arc, and path-optimization complexity parameterized by maximum layer width.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A layered diagram with \(n+1\) layers contains \(\sum_i w_i\) nodes, hence at most \((n+1)W\) nodes. With at most \(d\) outgoing arcs per nonterminal node, it contains at most \(d\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}w_i\leq nWd\) arcs. Once compiled, a forward dynamic-programming pass for a shortest or longest root-to-terminal path takes \(O(|V|+|A|)=O(nWd+nW)\) time and \(O(W)\) value workspace when layers are streamed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximum layer width W bounds nodes by (n+1)W and arcs by nWd, yielding linear-time layered path optimization in the explicit diagram size.
knowledge_statements.title: Layer-Width Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind fits Layer-Width Complexity, and statement_latex itself uses explicit math delimiters. However, the assumption contains malformed notation \(d\\\), no source supports the cost and streaming-workspace model, and O(W) value workspace presumes layerwise access to arcs without counting their storage.

children.title: Diagram-Reduction Complexity
children.top_down_role: Computational costs associated with eliminating redundant diagram structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram-Reduction Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity of bottom-up reduction for a finite layered ordered decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite layered decision diagram whose arcs carry labels and point only to the next layer. Process layers from the terminal layer upward, assign each node the signature consisting of its ordered labeled-successor list, and merge nodes having equal signatures. With comparison sorting of signatures, reduction uses \(O(|A|+|V|\log |V|)\) signature comparisons and \(O(|A|+|V|)\) storage, assuming constant-time comparison of labels and previously assigned child identifiers. With collision-resolving hashing, the expected running time is \(O(|A|+|V|)\). The resulting diagram has at most \(|V|\) nodes and \(|A|\) arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bottom-up merging of equivalent diagram nodes is near-linear deterministically and expected linear with hashing, while never increasing diagram size.
assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is finite, layered, and ordered.
Arc labels and child identifiers admit constant-time comparison.
Each node signature occupies space proportional to its outdegree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{sort}}=O(|A|+|V|\log |V|)\), \(T_{\mathrm{hash}}=O(|A|+|V|)\) in expectation, and \(S=O(|A|+|V|)\).

notation.meaning: Input decision diagram with node set V and arc set A.

review_flags: Decision-diagram-specific complexity source and computational model are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound role fits the leaf, but no decision-diagram source is cited. Constant-time comparison of labels and child identifiers does not make comparison of variable-length successor-list signatures constant time, so the stated deterministic bound requires a more precise representation or analysis.

children.title: Canonicalization Complexity
children.top_down_role: Computational costs associated with constructing canonical diagram representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonicalization Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonicalization of an ordered decision diagram by normalized bottom-up node signatures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite layered ordered diagram \(D=(V,A)\) with fixed variable order and a total order on arc labels. First normalize terminal identifiers. Then, from the last nonterminal layer upward, sort each node's outgoing arcs by label, replace every child by its canonical identifier, and form the signature \(\sigma(v)=((\ell_1,c_1),\ldots,(\ell_k,c_k))\). Assign one identifier to every distinct signature and redirect incoming arcs to its representative. Output the representatives in increasing layer and signature order. Comparison-based dictionaries produce a deterministic canonical encoding in \(O(|A|\log |A|+|V|\log |V|)\) time and \(O(|A|+|V|)\) space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicalization normalizes terminals, sorts labeled successors, merges identical signatures, and emits representatives in a fixed order with polynomial overhead.
assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is finite and respects a fixed variable order.
Arc labels have a fixed total order.
Terminal semantics have a fixed canonical encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a deterministic reduced encoding using \(O(|A|\log |A|+|V|\log |V|)\) time and \(O(|A|+|V|)\) space.

notation.meaning: Canonical labeled-successor signature of node v.
Canonical identifier of the ith child.
Label of the ith outgoing arc.

review_flags: Canonical encoding conventions and a supporting complexity reference are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits canonicalization, but canonicality depends on the exact diagram family, terminal encoding, redundancy rules, and identifier convention. No cited source supports either those conventions or the stated time bound.

children.title: Reduced-Form Uniqueness Costs
children.top_down_role: Resource costs associated with obtaining or maintaining unique reduced forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Form Uniqueness Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost of obtaining the unique reduced form under a fixed ordering and reduction convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite ordered decision diagram representing a fixed function under a fixed variable order, suppose reduction merges nodes with identical labeled-successor functions and removes every node declared redundant by the chosen diagram convention. Once canonical child identifiers are available, testing reduced-form equality requires comparing canonical root identifiers and therefore costs \(O(1)\). Constructing those identifiers from two unreduced diagrams \(D_i=(V_i,A_i)\) costs \(O(M\log N)\) time and \(O(M+N)\) space with comparison-based signature dictionaries, where \(M=|A_1|+|A_2|\) and \(N=|V_1|+|V_2|\). Uniqueness holds only relative to the fixed order and reduction convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After canonical reduction, equality is a root-identifier comparison; obtaining that form costs near-linearithmic time and linear space.
assumptions_latex: Both diagrams use the same variable order and arc-label semantics.
Reduction rules determine a unique representative of every semantic node class.
Canonical identifiers are assigned deterministically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equality query costs \(O(1)\) after preprocessing; preprocessing costs \(O(M\log N)\) time and \(O(M+N)\) space.

notation.meaning: Total number of arcs in the two input diagrams.
Total number of nodes in the two input diagrams.

review_flags: The exact decision-diagram family and redundancy rule must be sourced.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound role fits the leaf. However, constant-time equality by root identifiers requires identifiers produced in a shared canonical namespace or comparison of canonical encodings; separately assigned deterministic identifiers need not be comparable. The applicable uniqueness theorem and preprocessing bound require a diagram-specific source.

children.title: Static Variable Ordering
children.top_down_role: Variable orders fixed independently of evolving diagram structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Static Variable Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed variable order used throughout compilation and subsequent diagram operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\) be the variables of a subproblem. A static variable ordering is a permutation \(\pi:[n]\to[n]\) selected before diagram compilation. Every root-to-terminal path tests or assigns variables in the sequence \(x_{\pi(1)},\ldots,x_{\pi(n)}\), possibly skipping variables permitted by the diagram convention, and \(\pi\) remains unchanged during compilation, reduction, and search. The width at layer \(i\) is the number of distinct residual states after assignments to the first \(i\) ordered variables; hence the size of the compiled diagram is measured relative to \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A static ordering fixes one variable permutation before compilation and retains it throughout reduction and search.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\) is finite.
The diagram has layers compatible with variable assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\) is fixed before compilation and governs every variable layer of the diagram.

notation.meaning: Permutation defining the static variable order.

review_flags: A decision-diagram reference is needed for the locally intended ordering convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits static variable ordering, and the core definition is standard. The assertion that layer width equals the number of distinct residual states is convention-dependent and generally requires a reduced exact diagram; it is not established for arbitrary compatible diagrams. A diagram-specific source is required.

children.title: Structure-Aware Variable Ordering
children.top_down_role: Variable orders selected using structural features of the modeled problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Aware Variable Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static ordering obtained from a structural interaction graph or hypergraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a finite variable set \(X\) and an interaction hypergraph \(H=(X,\mathcal E)\), where each hyperedge contains variables appearing jointly in a constraint or state transition. Initialize \(U=X\). For \(i=1,
\ldots,|X|\), choose \(x\in U\) minimizing a prescribed elimination score such as the number of fill edges created by eliminating \(x\); set \(\pi(i)=x\), add the required fill edges among its remaining neighbors, and replace \(U\) by \(U\setminus\{x\}\). Compile the diagram using \(\pi\), without later reordering. Ties are resolved by a fixed rule, so the output ordering is deterministic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a static order by repeatedly eliminating the variable with the best structural score, updating fill and resolving ties deterministically.
assumptions_latex: \(H=(X,\mathcal E)\) is a finite interaction hypergraph.
The elimination score and tie-breaking rule are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a deterministic structure-guided permutation \(\pi\) of \(X\).
review_flags: The intended structural score and its diagram-width guarantee require a source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but the elimination score is left open and fill-edge updates are not defined for the stated hypergraph representation. A specific structure-aware ordering method and a supporting decision-diagram reference are needed.

children.title: Ordering Robustness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes distinguished by sensitivity of diagram size to ordering choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordering Robustness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative condition under which diagram size is insensitive to admissible static orderings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Pi_n\) be a nonempty class of admissible static orders for instances of size \(n\), and let \(S(I,\pi)\) denote the number of nodes in the reduced diagram for instance \(I\) under order \(\pi\). A family \(\mathcal I_n\) is \(g(n)\)-ordering-robust over \(\Pi_n\) when
\[
\sup_{I\in\mathcal I_n}\frac{\max_{\pi\in\Pi_n}S(I,\pi)}{\min_{\pi\in\Pi_n}S(I,\pi)}\le g(n).
\]
The regime is constant-robust if \(g(n)=O(1)\), polynomially robust if \(g(n)\) is polynomial, and ordering-fragile if this ratio is superpolynomial for infinitely many \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordering robustness bounds the worst-to-best reduced diagram-size ratio over an admissible class of static orders.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi_n\ne\varnothing\).
\(S(I,\pi)\) is finite and positive for every admissible pair \((I,\pi)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robustness is classified by the asymptotic growth of \(\max_{\pi}S(I,\pi)/\min_{\pi}S(I,\pi)\).

notation.meaning: Reduced diagram node count for instance I under order pi.
Admissible static orders at size n.

review_flags: This quantitative regime definition needs alignment with a published ordering-sensitivity convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role is appropriate and the ratio is mathematically well formed under the stated positivity assumption. The robustness terminology and thresholds appear to be a proposed convention rather than an established diagram-ordering classification, so they require a supporting source or explicit standard-field rationale.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Reordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantics-preserving variable-order changes performed while constructing or searching a decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a decision diagram \(D\), its current order \(\pi\), and a trigger threshold \(W\). Whenever the current node count or layer width exceeds \(W\), generate a finite set \(N(\pi)\) of candidate orders, transform \(D\) semantics-preservingly to each candidate, reduce each transformed diagram, and select an order \(\pi'\) minimizing a fixed size score. Accept \(\pi'\) only if its transformation cost plus predicted continuation cost is smaller than retaining \(\pi\); otherwise keep \(\pi\). Continue compilation or search and output the final reduced diagram and order. Every accepted transformation must preserve the represented feasible assignments and path values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic reordering changes the variable order when width grows, accepting only semantics-preserving transformations that improve a fixed cost criterion.
assumptions_latex: Candidate neighborhoods \(N(\pi)\) are finite.
Every reorder transformation preserves represented assignments and path values.
The trigger, score, and tie rule are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output diagram is semantically equivalent to the input representation under the final order.
review_flags: A specific dynamic-reordering method and transformation-cost model must be sourced.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits dynamic reordering, but this is a generic framework rather than a fully specified method: candidate transformations, predicted continuation cost, and the acceptance computation are undefined. A concrete semantics-preserving reordering method and cost model must be sourced.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordering-Induced Size Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic separation between reduced diagram sizes produced by different variable orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an instance family \((I_n)_{n\ge1}\) and two admissible order sequences \((\pi_n)\) and \((\rho_n)\), an ordering-induced exponential size separation occurs when constants \(c>1\) and \(k\ge0\) exist such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
S(I_n,\pi_n)\le n^k
\quad\text{and}\quad
S(I_n,\rho_n)\ge c^n.
\]
Thus polynomial compilation under one order does not imply polynomial compilation under another. Any ordering policy whose admissible outputs include \(\rho_n\) lacks an order-independent polynomial-size guarantee on this family unless additional structural restrictions exclude the separating orders or instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family is order-fragile when one admissible order yields polynomial diagrams while another yields exponentially large diagrams.
assumptions_latex: Both \(\pi_n\) and \(\rho_n\) are admissible for \(I_n\).

\(S(I,
\pi)\) counts nodes after applying the same reduction convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S(I_n,\rho_n)/S(I_n,\pi_n)\ge c^n/n^k\), so no order-independent polynomial bound holds.

notation.meaning: Reduced diagram size under order pi.

review_flags: A concrete separating family for the intended diagram class is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role correctly captures an ordering-induced size separation, and the asymptotic implication follows from the displayed conditions. No concrete instance family, decision-diagram class, or published separation result is cited, so applicability to this container remains unsupported.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Discrete Optimization with Decision Diagrams
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Relaxed diagrams for bounds and branching; restricted diagrams for primal solutions
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Discrete Optimization with Decision Diagrams

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed-Diagram Dual Bounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper bounding for maximization by a decision diagram containing all exact subproblem paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a maximization subproblem with feasible assignments \(F\) and objective \(f:F\to\mathbb R\). Let a relaxed decision diagram \(D^R\) represent a set of root-to-terminal paths \(P^R\), with decoded assignments \(R\supseteq F\), and let every path value equal the objective of its decoded assignment under an extension \(\bar f:R\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(\bar f(x)=f(x)\) for \(x\in F\). Then the longest-path value
\[
U(D^R)=\max_{x\in R}\bar f(x)
\]
is a valid dual bound: \(U(D^R)\ge z^*=\max_{x\in F}f(x)\). Infeasibility cannot be concluded from a nonempty relaxed diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For maximization, a relaxed diagram containing every feasible assignment gives an upper bound through its longest path.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\).
\(\bar f(x)=f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\).
The longest-path value of \(D^R\) equals \(\max_{x\in R}\bar f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Assignments represented by relaxed root-to-terminal paths.

review_flags: A diagram-specific source is needed for relaxation semantics and bound orientation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits relaxed-diagram dual bounding, and the upper-bound orientation is correct for maximization under the explicit containment and value-preservation assumptions. A decision-diagram source is still required for the intended relaxation semantics; the local inventory contains no supporting diagram-specific citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Diagram Primal Bounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounding for maximization by a decision diagram containing only feasible subproblem paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a maximization subproblem with nonempty feasible set \(F\) and objective \(f:F\to\mathbb R\). Let a restricted decision diagram \(D^S\) retain a nonempty subset \(S\subseteq F\) of feasible assignments, with one root-to-terminal path of value \(f(x)\) for every retained assignment \(x\in S\). Its longest-path value
\[
L(D^S)=\max_{x\in S}f(x)
\]
is a valid primal bound satisfying \(L(D^S)\le z^*=\max_{x\in F}f(x)\). A maximizing path in \(D^S\) decodes to an incumbent feasible solution attaining \(L(D^S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For maximization, a restricted diagram containing only feasible assignments supplies a feasible incumbent and a lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\varnothing\ne S\subseteq F\).
Every retained path decodes to its stated feasible assignment and objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(D^S)\le z^*\), and a maximizing retained path certifies feasibility at value \(L(D^S)\).
review_flags: The supplied primal-bounds locator does not establish restricted-diagram semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits restricted-diagram primal bounding, and the lower-bound statement is correct for maximization when retained paths are feasible. The listed general primal-bounds source does not establish restricted-decision-diagram semantics, and the record itself cites no source.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram-Frontier Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branching on an exact cutset or frontier of a relaxed decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a relaxed diagram \(D^R\) for a maximization node and select a frontier \(C\) intersecting every root-to-terminal path exactly once. For each frontier element \(c\in C\), create a child search subproblem whose prefix set is precisely the set of root-to-\(c\) histories assigned to \(c\), together with the original constraints on all completions. If a frontier node aggregates incompatible histories, partition those histories into disjoint nonempty classes before creating children. Construct a relaxed diagram and upper bound for each child, discard children whose bound does not exceed the incumbent, and continue until the active set is empty or the global gap tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on a path frontier, partition merged histories into disjoint children, bound each child, and prune those unable to improve the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible root-to-terminal path meets the chosen frontier exactly once.
The history classes assigned to children are disjoint and exhaustive.
Each child relaxation contains all feasible completions of its assigned histories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The children partition the parent feasible set, and pruning a child with \(U_c\le L\) preserves an optimal incumbent.

notation.meaning: Valid upper bound for child c.

review_flags: A source is required for the precise frontier and merged-state branching construction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the branching container. The stated assumptions support exhaustive branching and safe upper-bound pruning, but the construction for partitioning histories represented by merged frontier nodes is not operationally specified and requires a diagram-search source.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram Search Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite certificate of optimality or prescribed absolute accuracy for diagram branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a maximization problem, let \(L=f(\hat x)\) be the value of a recorded feasible incumbent \(\hat x\). Let \(\mathcal Q\) be the active search nodes, each equipped with a relaxed-diagram bound \(U_q\) valid for every feasible completion in that node, and assume fathomed or branched nodes are accompanied by verifiable pruning or partition records. Define \(U=\max(\{L\}\cup\{U_q:q\in\mathcal Q\})\). The collection of the incumbent path, relaxed diagrams, frontier partitions, and pruning records certifies \(L\le z^*\le U\). It certifies optimality when \(U=L\), and absolute \(\varepsilon\)-optimality when \(U-L\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incumbent plus valid diagram bounds, exhaustive branch partitions, and pruning records certifies the global gap and optimality when that gap closes.
assumptions_latex: \(\hat x\) is feasible and \(L=f(\hat x)\).
Every active-node value satisfies \(z_q^*\le U_q\).
Branch partitions are exhaustive, and every pruned node has a valid fathoming record.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le z^*\le U\); if \(U-L\le\varepsilon\), then \(\hat x\) is absolutely \(\varepsilon\)-optimal.

notation.meaning: Global upper bound from active relaxed diagrams.

review_flags: A decision-diagram branch-and-bound certification source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role exactly fits the leaf, and the global-gap conclusion is correct provided all active bounds, partitions, and fathoming records are valid and exhaustive. No source establishes the decision-diagram-specific certificate objects or their verification requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram-Based Subproblem Solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact path-based solution of a fixed-master LBBD subproblem using a layered decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a master assignment \(\bar x\), construct a finite layered acyclic diagram \(D(\bar x)=(V,A)\) whose source-to-terminal paths are in bijection with feasible subproblem decisions \(y\in Y(\bar x)\). Assign arc weights \(w_a(\bar x)\) so that each corresponding path \(P_y\) has length \(\sum_{a\in P_y}w_a(\bar x)=q(\bar x,y)\). If no source-to-terminal path exists, return subproblem infeasibility. Otherwise compute a shortest path \(P^*\), return its encoded decision \(y^*\), and report \(Q(\bar x)=\sum_{a\in P^*}w_a(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build the exact diagram for the fixed master assignment. Absence of a complete path proves infeasibility; otherwise a shortest path supplies an optimal subproblem decision and value.
assumptions_latex: \(D(\bar x)\) is finite and acyclic.
The path encoding represents exactly \(Y(\bar x)\).
Path weights reproduce the subproblem objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^*\) encodes an optimizer and \(Q(\bar x)=q(\bar x,y^*)\), or path absence certifies \(Y(\bar x)=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Subproblem feasible set under the fixed master assignment.
Layered decision diagram representing the subproblem.

review_flags: Decision-diagram-specific LBBD formulation requires a direct authoritative source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and its exact path-encoding assumptions fit the leaf, but no inspectable source supports this decision-diagram LBBD interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram-Derived Master Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds obtained from relaxed decision diagrams for minimization subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a master assignment \(x\). Let \(D_R(x)\) be a finite relaxed diagram such that every path representing a feasible subproblem decision in \(Y(x)\) is also a source-to-terminal path of \(D_R(x)\), with the same path cost. Additional paths may be present. Defining \(L_D(x)\) as the minimum source-to-terminal path cost in \(D_R(x)\), with \(L_D(x)=+\infty\) when no such path exists, gives \(L_D(x)\le Q(x)\). Consequently, any master constraint \(\theta\ge L_D(x)\) expressed by a valid global representation of \(L_D\) is a relaxation-valid subproblem bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed diagram may add paths but retains every feasible subproblem path. Its shortest-path value therefore lower-bounds the true minimization value and can strengthen the master.
assumptions_latex: The subproblem is a minimization problem.
Every exact feasible path occurs in \(D_R(x)\) with unchanged cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_D(x)\le Q(x)\) for every represented master assignment \(x\).

notation.meaning: Relaxed decision diagram at master assignment x.
Shortest-path value of the relaxed diagram.

review_flags: A direct source connecting relaxed decision diagrams to LBBD master bounds is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-bound direction is mathematically plausible for a minimization problem, but the diagram relaxation and its global master representation require direct source support.

children.title: Diagram-Derived Explanations
children.top_down_role: Master-relevant explanations extracted from decision-diagram structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram-Derived Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagram witnesses identifying master literals sufficient for infeasibility or a subproblem lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a set of master literals satisfied by an incumbent \(\bar x\), and let \(X_E\) be the assignments satisfying every literal in \(E\). A diagram-derived infeasibility explanation is certified when diagram reduction under \(E\) leaves no source-to-terminal path for every \(x\in X_E\). A diagram-derived bound explanation with value \(\beta\) is certified when every source-to-terminal path remaining under \(E\) has cost at least \(\beta\) for every \(x\in X_E\). The respective conclusions are \(Y(x)=\varnothing\) and \(Q(x)\ge\beta\) throughout \(X_E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set of incumbent literals is an explanation if the restricted diagram verifiably has no complete path or has every complete path costing at least a stated bound.
assumptions_latex: The diagram restriction under master literals is sound for every assignment satisfying those literals.
Diagram path costs are valid subproblem costs or lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in X_E\) implies either \(Y(x)=\varnothing\) or \(Q(x)\ge\beta\), according to the certificate type.

notation.meaning: Master assignments satisfying all explaining literals.

review_flags: The exact diagram explanation semantics require decision-diagram and LBBD source support.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the leaf, but the restriction semantics and their uniform validity over all assignments satisfying the explanation are unsupported.

children.title: Diagram-Derived Cuts
children.top_down_role: Master cuts obtained from decision-diagram information.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram-Derived Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master cuts obtained from globally valid diagram bounds or infeasibility certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the master domain and \(Q(x)\) the minimization-subproblem value, extended by \(+\infty\) when the subproblem is infeasible. If a diagram computation produces a function \(L_D:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) satisfying \(L_D(x)\le Q(x)\) for every feasible master assignment, then the epigraph constraint \(\theta\ge L_D(x)\) is a valid optimality cut. If it produces a set \(E\) of literals such that every \(x\in X_E\) has an infeasible subproblem, then the logical constraint \(x\notin X_E\) is a valid feasibility cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally valid diagram lower bound yields an epigraph cut. A diagram-certified region containing only infeasible subproblems yields a logical exclusion cut.
assumptions_latex: The diagram bound or infeasibility explanation is valid over its stated master domain.
\(\theta\) represents a lower approximation of subproblem cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting cut removes no point \((x,\theta)\) satisfying \(x\in X\), \(Y(x)\ne\varnothing\), and \(\theta\ge Q(x)\).
review_flags: Diagram-to-LBBD cut construction needs direct source support.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasibility and optimality cut implications are plausible, but no source supports their claimed diagram-derived LBBD interpretation.

children.title: Explanation-to-Cut Translation
children.top_down_role: Interfaces converting diagram explanations into master-compatible cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation-to-Cut Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation of binary-literal explanations into feasibility or conditional optimality cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For binary master variables, encode each explaining literal by its incumbent value \(\bar x_i\), and define the mismatch count \(d_E(x)=\sum_{i\in E:\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i\in E:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)\). If \(E\) certifies infeasibility whenever \(d_E(x)=0\), add the nogood cut \(d_E(x)\ge1\). If \(E\) certifies \(Q(x)\ge\beta\) whenever \(d_E(x)=0\), choose \(M\ge\beta-L\), where \(L\le Q(x)\) globally, and add \(\theta\ge\beta-Md_E(x)\). Return the constructed constraint to the master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Count violations of the explaining binary literals. An infeasibility explanation becomes a nogood; a bound explanation becomes a big-M conditional lower-bound cut.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) for every explained index \(i\).
The explanation is sound on all assignments with \(d_E(x)=0\).
A finite global lower bound \(L\) is available for the optimality form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated feasibility or optimality constraint is valid for every feasible master-subproblem solution.

notation.meaning: Number of explaining literals violated by x.
Lower bound certified by the explanation.

review_flags: The algebra is standard, but a source explicitly treating explanation-to-cut translation in LBBD is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary nogood and conditional big-M translations are algebraically coherent, but the record lacks a source for this explanation-to-LBBD-cut interface.

children.title: Persistent Diagram Refinement Across LBBD Iterations

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Diagram Refinement Across LBBD Iterations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone reuse and tightening of relaxed diagrams throughout the LBBD solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a relaxed diagram \(D^0\) containing every path that can represent a feasible subproblem decision for any admissible master assignment. At iteration \(k\), restrict \(D^k\) using the incumbent \(x^k\), compute its bound or explanation, and refine only by deleting spurious paths or splitting states while preserving every exact feasible path. Store the result as \(D^{k+1}\). For minimization, require the corresponding shortest-path bounds to satisfy \(L_{D^k}(x)\le L_{D^{k+1}}(x)\le Q(x)\) wherever both diagrams apply. Stop diagram refinement when the required oracle certificate is obtained, while retaining \(D^{k+1}\) for later iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse the relaxed diagram, removing spurious paths or splitting states without losing exact paths. Bounds tighten monotonically while remaining valid across later LBBD iterations.
assumptions_latex: Each refinement preserves all exact feasible paths and their costs.
The subproblem is a minimization problem.
Stored diagram state remains semantically valid under later master assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The persistent sequence yields nondecreasing valid lower bounds and preserves exact subproblem solutions.

notation.meaning: Persistent relaxed diagram after iteration k.
Lower bound obtained from the kth diagram.

review_flags: Persistence across changing LBBD assignments needs precise interface assumptions and a direct source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Persistence across changing master assignments requires a precise shared-diagram semantics and direct support; the stated assumptions alone do not establish the intended implementation interface.
