knowledge_statements.title: Inference-Soundness Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity certification by derivation in a sound inference system for the subproblem theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T(x,y)\) denote the combined master-subproblem theory and let \(C(x,\theta)\) be a proposed logic-based Benders cut. A derivation \(\pi\) certifies the cut by the inference-soundness route if every premise of \(\pi\) is valid for \(T\), every inference rule preserves semantic entailment, and the final formula is \(C\). Under these conditions, \(T(x,y)\land \theta\ge q(x,y)\models C(x,\theta)\). Thus adding \(C\) to the master cannot exclude the projection of any feasible combined solution with a valid objective surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is certified when it is derived from the combined model using only semantically sound inference rules; the derived cut is then entailed by every feasible combined solution.
assumptions_latex: All derivation premises are valid consequences of the combined model.
Every rule used in \(\pi\) preserves semantic entailment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(x,y)\land\theta\ge q(x,y)\models C(x,\theta)\).
review_flags: A logic-based Benders source specifying the accepted inference calculus is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits, but the admissible premises and inference calculus for LBBD cuts are not sourced or specified sufficiently for reliable review.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Relaxation Preservation Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut validity certified by preservation of the master as a relaxation of the full formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\times Y\times\mathbb R\) be the feasible epigraph set of the full problem and let \(R\subseteq X\times\mathbb R\) be the current master relaxation, with \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,\theta}(F)\subseteq R\). For a proposed cut region \(H_C=\{(x,\theta):C(x,\theta)\}\), the master-relaxation preservation route certifies validity by establishing \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,\theta}(F)\subseteq H_C\). The updated master \(R'=R\cap H_C\) then still contains \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,\theta}(F)\), so the cut cannot remove any feasible full-problem epigraph point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Show that every projected feasible full-problem point satisfies the proposed cut. Intersecting the master with that cut then preserves its relaxation property.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,\theta}(F)\subseteq R\).
\(\operatorname{proj}_{x,\theta}(F)\subseteq H_C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,\theta}(F)\subseteq R\cap H_C\).

children.title: Projected-Cut Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity issues specific to cuts expressed in the projected master space.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Cut Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of an inequality stated directly in the projected master space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) be the full feasible set and \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(F)=\{x:\exists y,\ (x,y)\in F\}\). An inequality \(a^\top x\ge b\) is a valid projected cut precisely when it holds for every \(x\in P\). Equivalently, \(a^\top x\ge b\) must hold for every \((x,y)\in F\). Therefore intersecting any master relaxation containing \(P\) with this inequality preserves all master assignments extendable to a feasible full solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected inequality is valid exactly when every full feasible point has a master component satisfying it. Adding it preserves every extendable master assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) is the full feasible set.
\(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(F)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^\top x\ge b\) is valid for \(P\) if and only if it is valid for the \(x\)-components of all \((x,y)\in F\).

notation.meaning: Full feasible set in original and auxiliary variables.
Projection of the full feasible set onto master variables.

children.title: Lifted-Cut Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity issues specific to cuts represented in an extended space.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Cut Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of an extended-space inequality before elimination of auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) be an extended feasible set. A lifted inequality \(a^\top x+c^\top y\ge b\) is valid when it holds for every \((x,y)\in F\). If auxiliary variables are retained in an extended master relaxation, the inequality may be added directly without excluding any point of \(F\). If the master contains only \(x\), eliminating \(y\) from the lifted inequality together with a valid description of the fibers of \(F\) is required; simply dropping the term \(c^\top y\) need not yield a valid projected cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted cut must hold throughout the extended feasible set. It is directly usable with retained auxiliaries; otherwise valid elimination is required before use in the projected master.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) is the relevant extended feasible set.
The retained extended master is a relaxation containing \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq\{(x,y):a^\top x+c^\top y\ge b\}\), while projected validity requires sound elimination of \(y\).

children.title: Projection–Lifting Validity Transfer
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing validity preservation between projected cuts plus lifted representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection–Lifting Validity Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fiberwise transfer of an extended-space inequality to the projected master space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\), let \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(F)\), and let \(F_x=\{y:(x,y)\in F\}\). Suppose \(F_x\ne\varnothing\) for every \(x\in P\), and define \(\phi(x)=\inf_{y\in F_x}c^\top y\). Then the lifted inequality \(a^\top x+c^\top y\ge b\) is valid for \(F\) if and only if the projected inequality \(a^\top x+\phi(x)\ge b\) is valid for \(P\). Hence exact fiber minimization transfers validity between the lifted and projected descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the auxiliary-variable term over each projection fiber. The resulting master-space inequality is valid exactly when the original lifted inequality is valid on the extended set.
assumptions_latex: \(F_x\ne\varnothing\) for every \(x\in P\).
\(\phi(x)=\inf_{y\in F_x}c^\top y\) is well-defined in \(\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^\top x+c^\top y\ge b\) is valid for \(F\) if and only if \(a^\top x+\phi(x)\ge b\) is valid for \(P\).

notation.meaning: Fiber of the extended feasible set over x.
Infimum of the lifted-variable term over the fiber.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination of exact LBBD over a finite master domain when every oracle evaluation permanently resolves its master assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite master domain and consider minimization of \(f(x)+Q(x)\), where \(Q(x)=+\infty\) when the subproblem at \(x\) is infeasible. Suppose the initial master is a valid relaxation with surrogate \(\theta\), every master problem and subproblem oracle is solved exactly, and every generated cut is globally valid. Require that evaluating an unresolved incumbent \(x^k\) either excludes \(x^k\) when \(Q(x^k)=+\infty\), or ensures \(\theta\ge Q(x^k)\) whenever that same assignment is subsequently selected. If the algorithm retains the best feasible incumbent and terminates when the exact master lower bound meets its objective value, then LBBD terminates after resolving at most \(|X|\) distinct master assignments and returns a global optimum or certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite master domain, exact evaluation must permanently resolve each selected assignment by excluding it if infeasible or correcting its master value to the exact subproblem value. With valid cuts and exact bound comparison, LBBD then terminates after at most one unresolved evaluation per master assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(|X|<\infty\).
The initial master is a valid relaxation, and every master solve, subproblem evaluation, and generated cut is exact or globally valid as applicable.
Each unresolved evaluated assignment is permanently excluded if infeasible or permanently assigned a master surrogate value of at least its exact subproblem value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: LBBD resolves at most \(|X|\) distinct master assignments before returning a global optimum or an infeasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: Exact subproblem value, extended by positive infinity for infeasibility.
Master surrogate for the subproblem value.

children.title: Nonrepetition Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Structures preventing repeated master assignments or equivalent search states.

assumptions_latex: The master domain \(Y\) is finite.
Every evaluated \(y^k\in Y\) yields a valid logic-based Benders cut excluding \(y^k\) whenever it is not certified optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No nonoptimal master assignment is evaluated twice, so at most \(|Y|\) distinct nonoptimal assignments are processed before termination or an optimality certificate is obtained.

notation.meaning: master assignment evaluated at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain exclusion by valid no-good or stronger Benders cuts.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be finite and let \(y^k\in Y\) be evaluated at iteration \(k\). If the subproblem oracle does not certify \(y^k\) as optimal, add a valid cut \(C_k\) such that \(y^k\notin C_k\) while every globally optimal master assignment remains in \(C_k\). Since subsequent master iterates belong to \(Y\cap\bigcap_{i\le k}C_i\), no rejected assignment can recur. Consequently, the algorithm performs at most \(|Y|\) distinct rejected evaluations before either exhausting \(Y\) or producing an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid cut removes each rejected finite-domain master assignment without removing any optimum, preventing repetition and forcing finite progress.

children.title: Progress Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Structures certifying meaningful advancement across decomposition iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Progress Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone-bound or feasible-region progress in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(L_k\) be the exact master optimum and \(U_k\) the value of the best certified feasible incumbent after iteration \(k\). Accumulating globally valid relaxation cuts gives \(L_{k+1}\ge L_k\), while retaining the best incumbent gives \(U_{k+1}\le U_k\). If the current master solution \(y^k\) is not termination-certified, require either a better incumbent, \(U_{k+1}<U_k\), or a valid cut violated by \(y^k\), so that \(y^k\) is absent from the next master feasible set. Exclusion is strict feasible-set progress even when \(L_{k+1}=L_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each nonterminal iteration must improve the incumbent or strictly strengthen the master feasible set by excluding its current uncertified solution; exclusion need not strictly increase the numerical lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Each added cut is globally valid and violated by the current uncertified master solution.
The master problem is solved exactly after each cut addition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Until termination, either the incumbent upper bound strictly decreases or the current uncertified master solution is excluded; the master lower bound remains nondecreasing but need not strictly increase.

notation.meaning: master lower bound at iteration k
incumbent upper bound at iteration k

children.title: Stagnation Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where repetition control or progress certification becomes ineffective.

assumptions_latex: The master solver may return a previously evaluated assignment.
Generated cuts may be nonviolated at the current assignment and bounds may remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stopping gap can remain positive forever; validity of cuts alone does not guarantee convergence without strict progress, nonrepetition, or a terminating refinement rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when valid iterations need not make strict progress.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an iteration at \(\bar y\) returns only cuts satisfied by \(\bar y\), produces no improved feasible incumbent, and permits the master solver to select \(\bar y\) again. Then the state can repeat with \(L_{k+1}=L_k\), \(U_{k+1}=U_k\), and \(U_k-L_k>0\). Thus global validity of all accumulated cuts is insufficient for convergence unless an additional rule enforces strict bound improvement, exclusion of uncertified repeated assignments, or finite oracle refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid but nonseparating cuts can allow the same master state and positive gap to recur indefinitely.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Oracle Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-master-domain convergence with exact master and subproblem oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be finite and consider \(v^*=\min_{y\in Y}\{c(y)+Q(y)\}\), where \(c:Y\to\mathbb R\) and \(Q:Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), with \(Q(y)=+\infty\) denoting the absence of a feasible completion. At each iteration, solve a globally valid accumulated-cut master exactly, evaluate its selected assignment with an exact oracle, retain every certified feasible completion as a possible incumbent, and, unless optimality is certified, add a valid cut that excludes the evaluated assignment while retaining every globally optimal assignment. Then no rejected assignment recurs. Because \(Y\) is finite, the method terminates after finitely many evaluations with a certified global optimum or, if every assignment is certified infeasible, a certificate that the original problem is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite master domain, exact master solves, exact subproblem certificates, and optimum-preserving exclusion of every rejected assignment imply finite global convergence or certified infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The master domain \(Y\) is finite, and every accumulated-cut master is solved exactly.
The subproblem oracle returns exact feasible values or exact infeasibility certificates.
Every nonterminal evaluated assignment is excluded by a globally valid cut that retains every globally optimal assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates after finitely many master evaluations with either a certified globally optimal feasible solution or a certificate that every assignment in \(Y\) is infeasible.

notation.meaning: exact recourse value, with positive infinity denoting infeasibility

children.title: Inexact-Oracle Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence regimes permitting controlled oracle inaccuracy.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), the oracle supplies certified bounds \(\underline Q_k(y^k)\le Q(y^k)\le\overline Q_k(y^k)\).
All master cuts use certified lower information and every incumbent uses a certified feasible upper value.
The oracle errors satisfy \(\overline Q_k(y^k)-\underline Q_k(y^k)\to0\) along every infinitely revisited assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accumulation point passing the vanishing-error gap test is globally optimal; on a finite master domain, fair revisitation and vanishing errors yield finite \(\varepsilon\)-termination for every \(\varepsilon>0\).

notation.meaning: certified oracle lower and upper values

review_flags: exact adaptive-oracle theorem source not supplied
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified two-sided inexact oracle with vanishing local error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be the true recourse function. At iteration \(k\), require certified values \(\underline Q_k(y^k)\le Q(y^k)\le\overline Q_k(y^k)\); construct cuts only from lower-valid information and incumbents only from feasible upper information. If every assignment revisited infinitely often satisfies \(\overline Q_k(y)-\underline Q_k(y)\to0\), then the maintained bounds remain valid. On finite \(Y\), fair selection implies that for every \(\varepsilon>0\), some finite iteration satisfies \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\), unless infeasibility is certified earlier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified lower and upper oracle answers preserve bounds; vanishing errors and fair finite-domain revisitation yield any prescribed gap tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Oracle Convergence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this specialized adaptive-oracle theorem. Fair selection, cut updating, and the connection between assignment-level interval convergence and the global gap require a precise sourced theorem before reliability can be assessed.

children.title: Oracle-Refinement Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence regimes driven by progressively improved oracle information.

assumptions_latex: Oracle levels form nested certified intervals containing the true recourse value.
Whenever the global gap test fails at a selected assignment, its oracle level is strictly refined.
Each assignment admits only finitely many refinements before its interval width is at most the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For finite \(Y\), the decomposition terminates after finitely many refinements with a valid \(\varepsilon\)-optimality or infeasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: certified oracle interval at refinement level r

review_flags: exact refinement theorem source not supplied
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain convergence under nested, finitely terminating oracle refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(y\in Y\), let \(I_r(y)=[\ell_r(y),u_r(y)]\) satisfy \(Q(y)\in I_r(y)\) and \(I_{r+1}(y)\subseteq I_r(y)\). If a nonterminal selection of \(y\) strictly increases its refinement level and, for every \(y\), finitely many refinements ensure \(u_r(y)-\ell_r(y)\le\varepsilon\), then finite \(Y\) admits only finitely many unresolved assignment-level pairs. Therefore the algorithm finitely returns a certified incumbent with global gap at most \(\varepsilon\), or certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested certified intervals, mandatory refinement, and finite refinement depth imply finite tolerance convergence on a finite master domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Refinement Convergence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for the claimed refinement theorem. Assignment-level interval widths alone do not establish the stated global-gap certificate without explicit master-bound construction and selection hypotheses.

children.title: Refinement Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits beyond which oracle refinement cannot recover convergence guarantees.

assumptions_latex: An assignment \(\bar y\) can be selected infinitely often.
Its certified oracle interval widths are bounded below by some \(\delta>0\).
The unresolved oracle uncertainty prevents both exclusion and the global stopping test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every tolerance \(\varepsilon<\delta\), finite \(\varepsilon\)-convergence is not guaranteed.

notation.meaning: certified lower and upper oracle values

review_flags: exact adaptive-oracle failure-boundary source not supplied
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent oracle uncertainty blocks convergence below its residual width.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\bar y\) is selected infinitely often and its certified intervals satisfy \(u_k(\bar y)-\ell_k(\bar y)\ge\delta>0\) on those iterations. If this uncertainty prevents a valid exclusion cut and prevents certification of \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\), then for every \(\varepsilon<\delta\) the same unresolved state may recur indefinitely. Thus finite convergence below \(\delta\) requires vanishing error, finite exactification, or another rule that removes \(\bar y\) without sacrificing validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If refinement leaves persistent uncertainty at a recurring assignment, no convergence guarantee exists below that uncertainty level.
knowledge_statements.title: Refinement Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional failure mechanism is plausible, but no inspectable source supports the adaptive-oracle formulation or its precise tolerance boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bound certificate for minimization from a valid, certifiably solved master relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original minimization problem have feasible set \(F\subseteq X\times Y\), objective \(f(x,y)\), and optimal value \(v^*\). Let \(M_k\subseteq Y\times\mathbb R\) be an accumulated-cut master feasible set with objective \(c(y)+\theta\). Suppose that for every \((x,y)\in F\), there exists \((y,\theta)\in M_k\) satisfying \(c(y)+\theta\le f(x,y)\). If a checkable master-solver certificate establishes \(L_k=\min\{c(y)+\theta:(y,\theta)\in M_k\}\), then \(L_k\le v^*\). The master instance, retained valid cuts, and master optimality certificate together form a checkable global lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid master relaxation together with a checkable certificate of its global optimum certifies that optimum as a lower bound on the original minimum.
assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem with feasible set \(F\) and optimal value \(v^*\).
Every original feasible solution is represented in the master relaxation at a master objective value no greater than its original objective.
A checkable master-solver certificate establishes the global optimum \(L_k\) of the current master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certified master optimum satisfies \(L_k\le v^*\) and is a verifiable global lower bound on the original optimal value.

Direct verification of membership in \(F\) certifies primal feasibility. A certified feasible incumbent supplies an upper bound \(v^*\le U\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(U-L\le\varepsilon\), the incumbent is globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal; equality \(U=L\) certifies exact optimality.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given certified bounds \(L\le v^*\le U\) for a minimization problem, the incumbent's suboptimality satisfies \(0\le U-v^*\le U-L\). Hence the tuple consisting of the master lower-bound certificate, the incumbent feasibility certificate, and the inequality \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) certifies global \(\varepsilon\)-optimality. When \(U=L\), both bounds equal \(v^*\), yielding an exact global optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching certified lower and upper bounds within tolerance proves the incumbent globally optimal to that absolute tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Exhaustion Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain certificate based on complete certified coverage relative to a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be a finite master domain, and let \((\hat x,\hat y)\) be a certified feasible incumbent of value \(U\). For each \(y\in Y\), an exhaustion record must certify either that \(y\) has no feasible completion or that every feasible completion associated with \(y\) has objective value at least \(U\). Let \(E\subseteq Y\) be the set covered by such records. If \(Y\setminus E\subseteq\{\hat y\}\), then no assignment can yield a value below \(U\), so the incumbent is globally optimal. If every \(y\in Y\) is covered by an infeasibility certificate, then the original problem is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete finite-domain coverage by infeasibility or incumbent-dominance certificates proves the incumbent globally optimal; coverage solely by infeasibility certificates proves infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The master search domain \(Y\) is finite.
A certified feasible incumbent \((\hat x,\hat y)\) with objective value \(U\) is supplied for the optimality case.
Every covered assignment has a checkable certificate of infeasibility or of a lower bound at least \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(Y\setminus E\subseteq\{\hat y\}\), the incumbent is globally optimal; if every assignment is covered solely by an infeasibility certificate, the original problem is infeasible.

notation.meaning: assignments covered by certified infeasibility or incumbent-dominance records

children.title: Cut Selection Policies
children.top_down_role: Criteria for choosing cuts from the available pool.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Selection Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Score-based cut dispatch with a budget large enough to include all mandatory correctness and progress cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite valid-cut pool \(P_k\), a current master candidate \(z^k\), an integer budget \(b_k\), scores \(s_k(c)\), and a mandatory set \(M_k\subseteq P_k\), with \(b_k\ge |M_k|\). Initialize \(S_k=M_k\). Add cuts from \(P_k\setminus M_k\) in nonincreasing score order until \(|S_k|=b_k\) or the pool is exhausted, resolving ties by a fixed rule. Dispatch \(S_k\) to the master and retain undispatched cuts. If exclusion progress is required at iteration \(k\), require at least one cut \(c\in M_k\) to be violated by \(z^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dispatch every mandatory cut, then fill the remaining budget by score; requiring a mandatory cut violated by the current candidate guarantees its exclusion.
assumptions_latex: The cut pool \(P_k\) is finite and every pooled cut is globally valid.
The mandatory set satisfies \(M_k\subseteq P_k\), and the integer budget satisfies \(b_k\ge |M_k|\).
A current master candidate \(z^k\) and a real-valued score \(s_k(c)\) for each pooled cut are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected set \(S_k\) contains every mandatory cut and satisfies \(|S_k|\le b_k\); if some mandatory cut is violated by \(z^k\), dispatching \(S_k\) excludes \(z^k\) from the next master feasible set.

notation.meaning: finite valid-cut pool at iteration k
selected dispatch set at iteration k
mandatory cut set at iteration k

children.title: Cut Scheduling Policies
children.top_down_role: Timing regimes for introducing selected cuts into the master process.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Scheduling Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A capacity-constrained dispatch rule for valid cuts awaiting activation in a logic-based Benders master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), let \(E_t\) be the eligible cut set, \(b_t\in\mathbb N\) the dispatch capacity, and \(p_t:E_t\to\mathbb R\) a priority score. Schedule \(S_t\subseteq E_t\) by ordering eligible cuts in nonincreasing \(p_t\), breaking ties deterministically, and taking the first \(\min\{b_t,|E_t|\}\) cuts. Add \(S_t\) to the active master and retain \(E_t\setminus S_t\) in the pool. If every persistently eligible cut is eventually scheduled, delayed dispatch does not invalidate convergence arguments based on eventual separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank eligible cuts, dispatch at most the iteration capacity, retain the remainder, and require eventual service of every persistently eligible cut.
assumptions_latex: \(E_t\) contains only cuts valid for the current master formulation.
Persistent eligibility implies eventual dispatch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_t\subseteq E_t\), \(|S_t|\le b_t\), and every persistently eligible cut is eventually activated.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the scheduling-policy leaf, but the specific priority, capacity, tie-breaking, and fairness rule is one possible policy rather than a canonical definition. A direct source is needed for this version and for the conditional convergence statement.

children.title: Selection–Schedule Coordination
children.top_down_role: Interactions between cut priority choices plus activation timing.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection–Schedule Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinates eligibility selection with capacity-limited dispatch while preserving validity and fairness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), a selector maps the cut pool \(P_t\) to an eligible set \(E_t=\sigma_t(P_t)\subseteq P_t\). A scheduler then returns \(S_t=\tau_t(E_t,b_t)\subseteq E_t\) with \(|S_t|\le b_t\). Update the active set by \(A_{t+1}=A_t\cup S_t\) and retain unscheduled cuts in \(P_t\setminus S_t\). Coordination is fair when every cut that remains selected from some iteration onward is scheduled after finitely many iterations; selection must never expose an invalid cut to the scheduler.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selection determines eligibility; scheduling dispatches only eligible cuts within capacity, with persistent selections eventually activated.
assumptions_latex: \(P_t\) contains certified cuts and possibly quarantined cuts excluded by \(\sigma_t\).
\(\tau_t(E_t,b_t)\subseteq E_t\).
Persistent selection is served in finite time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_t\subseteq E_t\subseteq P_t\), \(|S_t|\le b_t\), and coordinated dispatch preserves cut validity and fairness.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local placement fit, but the selector–scheduler interface and finite-service fairness condition are an uncited policy formulation. Source uncertainty affects which coordination guarantees should be stated.

children.title: Duplicate-Cut Detection
children.top_down_role: Recognition of cuts already represented in the active or retained pool.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Cut Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact duplicate detection for affine master inequalities, modulo positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a nontrivial affine cut as \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\), where \((a,b)\ne 0\), and define its positive-scale normalization by \(N(a,b)=(a,b)/\|(a,b)\|_2\). Two cuts \((a,b)\) and \((c,d)\) are duplicates precisely when \(N(a,b)=N(c,d)\); equivalently, there exists \(\lambda>0\) such that \((c,d)=\lambda(a,b)\). Under exact arithmetic either duplicate may be removed without changing the master feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two affine cuts are duplicates when their coefficient and right-hand-side vectors differ only by a positive scalar.
assumptions_latex: Both inequalities use the same orientation \(\le\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N(a,b)=N(c,d)\Longrightarrow\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\}=\{x:c^{\mathsf T}x\le d\}\).

children.title: Dominance Screening
children.top_down_role: Screening based on relative cut strength or redundancy.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-relative logical dominance between valid master cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the master domain before imposing either candidate cut, and let \(C_i=\{x:g_i(x)\le0\}\) for \(i\in\{1,2\}\). Cut \(C_1\) dominates \(C_2\) on \(X\) when \(X\cap C_1\subseteq X\cap C_2\). If both cuts are valid for the original problem, retaining \(C_1\) and discarding \(C_2\) leaves the relaxation \(X\cap C_1\cap C_2\) unchanged. For parallel affine cuts \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\), dominance holds whenever \(b_1\le b_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut dominates another when satisfying the first over the master domain always implies satisfying the second.
assumptions_latex: \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are valid cuts for the original feasible set.
Dominance is tested relative to the same master domain \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\cap C_1\subseteq X\cap C_2\Longrightarrow X\cap C_1\cap C_2=X\cap C_1\).

notation.meaning: current master domain without the compared cuts
feasible halfspace or region induced by cut i

children.title: Equivalence-Class Filtering
children.top_down_role: Treatment of syntactically distinct cuts with equivalent master-space effects.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence-Class Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partitions cuts by equality of their induced feasible regions on the master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For cuts \(C\) and \(D\) and a fixed master domain \(X\), define \(C\sim_XD\) if \(X\cap C=X\cap D\). Equivalently, both inclusions \(X\cap C\subseteq X\cap D\) and \(X\cap D\subseteq X\cap C\) hold. The relation \(\sim_X\) is an equivalence relation. Replacing every equivalence class of valid cuts by one representative preserves the intersection of the cut pool with \(X\), although equivalence may change if the reference domain changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cuts are equivalent when they induce the same feasible subset of the fixed master domain; one representative per class suffices.
assumptions_latex: All compared cuts use one fixed reference domain \(X\).
Every retained representative is valid for the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\sim_XD\Longrightarrow X\cap C\cap D=X\cap C=X\cap D\).

notation.meaning: cut equivalence relative to domain X

children.title: Cut-Aging Policies
children.top_down_role: Measures used to track declining cut relevance over time.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Aging Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic inactivity counter for prioritizing stale cuts without altering their validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each pooled cut \(c\) an age \(a_t(c)\in\mathbb N_0\). Given a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) and current master solution \(x^t\), set \(a_{t+1}(c)=0\) when \(c\) is newly generated, used in a certificate, or has slack at most \(\varepsilon\); otherwise set \(a_{t+1}(c)=a_t(c)+1\). Age may control scheduling or deletion eligibility, but it is not evidence that a cut has become invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reset a cut's age when it is new, useful, or nearly binding; otherwise increment its inactivity counter.
assumptions_latex: Every cut has a computable slack at \(x^t\).
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_{t+1}(c)\in\{0,a_t(c)+1\}\), and aging alone makes no assertion about validity.

notation.meaning: age of cut c at iteration t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the aging-policy leaf, but its reset events and tolerance-based activity rule are implementation choices rather than a unique mathematical convention. A direct source is required for this particular policy.

children.title: Cut-Deletion Criteria
children.top_down_role: Criteria governing removal of inactive or low-value cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Deletion Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe deletion criteria distinguish removal from the active relaxation from permanent loss of separation capability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An active cut \(c\) is deletion-eligible at iteration \(t\) when \(a_t(c)\ge A\), its slack exceeded \(\varepsilon\) throughout the last \(W\) evaluated master solutions, and it is not protected by a current certificate. Removing \(c\) from the active master is convergence-safe only if \(c\) remains archived and testable, can be regenerated by a complete separator, or is implied by the retained master constraints. Otherwise deletion may enlarge the terminal relaxation and invalidate certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete only old, persistently slack, unprotected cuts, while preserving implication, archival testing, or guaranteed regeneration.
assumptions_latex: \(A,W\in\mathbb N\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
Cut ages and recent slacks are recorded exactly to the chosen tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c\) may be safely deactivated only if archival testing, complete regeneration, or implication by retained constraints preserves eventual enforcement.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf and condition role fit, but merely keeping a cut archived and testable does not by itself preserve eventual enforcement; a guaranteed testing and reactivation rule is also needed. A source is required to establish sufficient deletion hypotheses without inventing a replacement policy.

children.title: Cut-Reactivation Triggers
children.top_down_role: Events that restore previously inactive cuts to operational use.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Reactivation Triggers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Violation- and certificate-based triggers for restoring archived valid cuts to the active master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an archived valid cut be written \(g_c(x)\le0\). At a candidate master solution \(x^t\), reactivate \(c\) whenever \(g_c(x^t)>\varepsilon\), whenever a verification certificate explicitly requires \(c\), or whenever a fairness audit selects \(c\) for retesting after its maximum dormancy period. Reactivation adds \(c\) to the next active master and resets its age. A violation trigger guarantees that the current candidate is excluded at the next exact master solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reactivate an archived cut when it is violated, certificate-required, or due for fairness retesting; then reset its age.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) remains valid for the current instance.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
The next master solve enforces every reactivated cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_c(x^t)>\varepsilon\Longrightarrow c\) is active at iteration \(t+1\) and excludes \(x^t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Violation-based reactivation is mathematically coherent, but certificate, fairness-audit, and maximum-dormancy triggers constitute a particular uncited lifecycle policy. A direct source is needed for the complete trigger set.

children.title: Cut-Pool Initialization
children.top_down_role: Sources plus composition choices for the initial cut pool.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Pool Initialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initializes active, archived, and quarantined cut sets before the first master solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a current instance with feasible set \(F\), partition imported or precomputed cuts into certified cuts \(V_0=\{c:F\subseteq C_c\}\) and unverified cuts \(Q_0\). Choose an initial active set \(A_0\subseteq V_0\), set the certified archive to \(R_0=V_0\setminus A_0\), and quarantine \(Q_0\). Solve the initial master using only \(A_0\) together with its structural constraints. Empty initialization \(A_0=R_0=\varnothing\) is valid when later separation is complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certify imported cuts, activate a chosen subset, archive the remainder, and quarantine every cut whose current-instance validity is unverified.
assumptions_latex: Each certified cut \(c\) has an induced feasible region \(C_c\).
Only cuts proved valid for \(F\) enter \(V_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_0\cap R_0=\varnothing\), \(A_0\cup R_0=V_0\), and no quarantined cut constrains the initial master.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The partitioning algorithm fits cut-pool initialization, but the active/archive/quarantine design and the completeness condition for empty initialization are uncited policy choices whose intended formulation cannot be verified.

children.title: Cross-Instance Cut Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of retained cuts across related instances or repeated solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Instance Cut Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A transferred cut is reusable exactly when its validity extends to the target instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_s\) and \(F_t\) be the source- and target-instance feasible sets in a common master-variable space, and let a source cut induce \(C_c\) with \(F_s\subseteq C_c\). Reuse in the target instance is safe only after establishing \(F_t\subseteq C_c\). A sufficient condition is \(F_t\subseteq F_s\); more generally, validity may be recertified directly from target parameters. Source-instance validity alone does not imply target-instance validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse a source cut only after proving that every target-feasible master point satisfies it; source validity alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(F_s\) and \(F_t\) use a common interpretation of the cut variables.
\(F_s\subseteq C_c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_t\subseteq C_c\) is required for safe target reuse, and \(F_t\subseteq F_s\subseteq C_c\) is sufficient.

children.title: Reuse-Safety Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Validity plus relevance limits affecting transferred cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Reuse-Safety Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete failure showing that source-valid cuts need not remain valid after an instance change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider source and target feasible sets \(F_s=\{x\in\mathbb R:x\ge1\}\) and \(F_t=\{x\in\mathbb R:x\ge0\}\). The cut \(x\ge1\) is valid for \(F_s\) but invalid for \(F_t\). Reusing it in the target problem \(\min\{x:x\in F_t\}\) removes the target optimum \(x=0\) and changes the optimal value from \(0\) to \(1\). Thus reuse crosses its safety boundary when target validity is not recertified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A source-valid cut can exclude the target optimum when the target feasible set expands beyond the cut's valid region.
assumptions_latex: Source and target instances share the scalar master variable \(x\).
The transferred inequality is imposed unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_t\nsubseteq\{x:x\ge1\}\), so unrevalidated reuse changes the target optimum.

children.title: Master-Problem Complexity
children.top_down_role: Computational burden attributable to repeated master optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Problem Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enumeration upper bounds and NP-hardness for exact binary Benders-master optimization as cuts accumulate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the iteration-\(k\) master has \(n\) binary variables, \(r\) continuous variables, and \(m_0+k\) rational linear constraints, with encoding length \(\ell_k\). If fixing a binary assignment yields a linear program solvable in time \(L(r,m_0+k,\ell_k)\), exhaustive enumeration gives an exact-solution running-time upper bound \(O\!\left(2^nL(r,m_0+k,\ell_k)\right)\) for that master solve. Over \(K\) iterations, the corresponding upper bound is \(O\!\left(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}2^nL(r,m_0+k,\ell_k)\right)\). General binary linear optimization is NP-hard; consequently, a polynomial-time exact algorithm for all such masters would imply \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerating all binary assignments gives an exponential exact-solution upper bound. General binary master optimization is NP-hard, so a polynomial-time exact algorithm for every such master would imply P equals NP.
assumptions_latex: \(n,r,m_0,K\in\mathbb N_0\).
At iteration \(k\), the master has rational linear data of encoding length \(\ell_k\).
Fixing all \(n\) binary variables yields a linear program in the remaining \(r\) continuous variables.
One new cut is counted per iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_K=O\!\left(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}2^nL(r,m_0+k,\ell_k)\right)\), and a polynomial-time exact algorithm for all general binary masters would imply \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).

notation.meaning: time required to solve a fixed-assignment linear program with r continuous variables, m constraints, and encoding length ell
encoding length of the iteration-k master

children.title: Subproblem Complexity
children.top_down_role: Computational burden attributable to subproblem or oracle evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work accounting for independent logic-based Benders subproblems in one iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(S_{ki}\) be the time required to solve and certify subproblem \(i\in\{1,\ldots,p_k\}\). Sequential evaluation has subproblem time \(S_k^{\mathrm{seq}}=\sum_{i=1}^{p_k}S_{ki}\). If all subproblems may run concurrently on distinct processors without resource contention, their parallel critical-path time is \(S_k^{\mathrm{par}}=\max_{1\le i\le p_k}S_{ki}+H_k\), where \(H_k\) is scheduling and synchronization overhead. Hence \(S_k^{\mathrm{par}}\le S_k^{\mathrm{seq}}+H_k\), with potential speedup bounded by \(p_k\) when \(H_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent subproblem work adds under sequential execution and follows the slowest subproblem under ideal parallel execution, plus coordination overhead.
assumptions_latex: Subproblems at iteration \(k\) are mutually independent after the master decision is fixed.
Each subproblem solver terminates with a valid certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_k^{\mathrm{seq}}=\sum_i S_{ki}\) and \(S_k^{\mathrm{par}}=\max_i S_{ki}+H_k\).

notation.meaning: time for subproblem i at iteration k
number of subproblems evaluated at iteration k

children.title: Master–Subproblem Complexity Coupling
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs linking master strength to residual subproblem difficulty.

knowledge_statements.title: Master–Subproblem Complexity Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: End-to-end runtime accounting for a terminating logic-based Benders execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a logic-based Benders method terminates after \(K\) iterations. Let \(M_k\), \(S_k\), and \(G_k\) denote respectively the master-solve, subproblem-evaluation, and cut-construction times at iteration \(k\), including only work not charged elsewhere. Its total algorithmic time satisfies \[T_{\mathrm{LBBD}}=T_{\mathrm{init}}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}(M_k+S_k+G_k)+T_{\mathrm{final}}.\] Consequently, bounds \(M_k\le\overline M_k\), \(S_k\le\overline S_k\), and \(G_k\le\overline G_k\) imply the corresponding sum bound. Thus iteration count and per-iteration master and subproblem costs are multiplicatively coupled rather than independently predictive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total runtime is the iteration count coupled with the master, subproblem, and cut costs incurred at every iteration.
assumptions_latex: The execution terminates after finite \(K\).
All runtime components use one consistent computation model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{LBBD}}\le T_{\mathrm{init}}+T_{\mathrm{final}}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}(\overline M_k+\overline S_k+\overline G_k)\).

notation.meaning: master, subproblem, and cut-construction times at iteration k

children.title: Cut-Generation Complexity
children.top_down_role: Computational cost of obtaining candidate logic-based cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Generation Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration cost of converting a subproblem certificate into an encoded master cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iteration \(k\), suppose the subproblem oracle returns a certificate \(z_k\) of encoding length \(L_k\), and the resulting master cut has encoding length \(B_k\). Let certificate extraction, coefficient construction, and cut insertion take at most \(C_k\), \(F(L_k)\), and \(E(B_k)\) time, respectively. If these operations contain all work charged to cut generation, then its actual cost \(G_k\) satisfies \[G_k\le C_k+F(L_k)+E(B_k).\] Over \(K\) iterations, define \(G_{1:K}:=\sum_{k=1}^{K}G_k\). Then \[G_{1:K}\le\sum_{k=1}^{K}\bigl(C_k+F(L_k)+E(B_k)\bigr).\] This accounting excludes optional strengthening and subsequent master reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut-generation time is bounded by the certificate-extraction, coefficient-construction, and cut-insertion bounds; total cut-generation work is bounded by their sum over all iterations.
assumptions_latex: Every generated cut has a finite certificate and finite encoding.
The component bounds use a common computation model.
The listed operations contain all work charged to cut generation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_{1:K}\le\sum_{k=1}^{K}\bigl(C_k+F(L_k)+E(B_k)\bigr)\).

children.title: Cut-Strengthening Complexity
children.top_down_role: Computational cost of improving candidate cut strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Strengthening Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additional work for selecting a dominating cut from a prescribed valid family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_k\) be a valid generated cut and let \(\mathcal D(c_k)\) be an explicitly represented family of valid cuts that dominate \(c_k\) on the master relaxation. A strengthening routine solves \[d_k\in\mathop{\mathrm{argmax}}_{d\in\mathcal D(c_k)}\Phi_k(d),\] where \(\Phi_k\) is a specified strength score. If forming \(\mathcal D(c_k)\), optimizing \(\Phi_k\), and encoding \(d_k\) require times \(A_k\), \(O_k\), and \(E_k\), respectively, then strengthening requires \(H_k\le A_k+O_k+E_k\). The bound is meaningful only after the representation and optimization model for \(\mathcal D(c_k)\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strengthening adds the cost of constructing a dominating-cut family, optimizing a strength criterion, and encoding the selected cut.
assumptions_latex: Every member of \(\mathcal D(c_k)\) is valid and dominates \(c_k\).
The maximum of \(\Phi_k\) over \(\mathcal D(c_k)\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_k\le A_k+O_k+E_k\).

notation.meaning: admissible valid cuts dominating the initial cut

children.title: Generation–Strengthening Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Cost-quality regimes linking initial generation effort to subsequent strengthening.

knowledge_statements.title: Generation–Strengthening Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Runtime criterion for deciding whether optional cut strengthening is computationally beneficial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let policy \(s\) impose per-iteration strengthening cost \(H(s)\), average remaining work \(W(s)=M(s)+S(s)+G(s)\), and iteration bound \(R(s)\). Its runtime bound is \[T(s)\le R(s)\bigl(W(s)+H(s)\bigr).\] Relative to unstrengthened policy \(0\), strengthening is justified by this bound precisely when \[R(s)\bigl(W(s)+H(s)\bigr)<R(0)W(0).\] Thus domination or geometric cut strength alone does not establish computational benefit: the reduction in iterations and later work must exceed the strengthening overhead under the same cost model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stronger cut is worthwhile only when its iteration and downstream-work savings exceed the extra strengthening cost.
assumptions_latex: Both policies solve the same problem to the same stopping tolerance.
All quantities are measured under the same computation model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(s)(W(s)+H(s))<R(0)W(0)\) is the stated sufficient comparison for choosing strengthening.

notation.meaning: iteration bound under strengthening policy s

children.title: Iteration Complexity
children.top_down_role: Growth in the number of decomposition rounds required for resolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Iteration Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-termination bound for exact-cut logic-based Benders over a finite master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite master-decision set. At iteration \(k\), an exact master solution \(x^k\in X\) is checked by the subproblem oracle. Suppose every nonterminating iteration adds a valid cut that excludes \(x^k\) from all later master solutions, while never excluding any globally optimal feasible solution. Then no master assignment can be checked twice, and the algorithm terminates after at most \(|X|\) subproblem-evaluation iterations. This is an enumerative worst-case bound; stronger cuts may exclude multiple unchecked assignments and yield fewer iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each valid cut permanently excludes the current finite-domain master assignment, at most one iteration per assignment is possible.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and every master problem is solved exactly.
Each nonterminating cut excludes the incumbent but preserves every globally optimal feasible assignment.

notation.meaning: master assignment checked at iteration k

children.title: Communication Complexity
children.top_down_role: Volume plus frequency of information exchanged across decomposition components.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit complexity of master-worker exchanges in synchronous distributed decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a synchronous execution with \(K\) iterations and \(p_k\) active workers at iteration \(k\), let \(a_{ki}\) be the bits sent from the master to worker \(i\), and let \(b_{ki}\) be the bits in that worker's returned status, certificate, and cut description. Ignoring fixed protocol headers, total communication is \[B_{\mathrm{comm}}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\sum_{i=1}^{p_k}(a_{ki}+b_{ki}).\] If \(p_k\le p\), \(a_{ki}\le a\), and \(b_{ki}\le b\), then \(B_{\mathrm{comm}}\le Kp(a+b)\), with \(2\sum_k p_k\) directed messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed communication equals the encoded master-to-worker and worker-to-master traffic summed over active workers and iterations.
assumptions_latex: Messages have finite binary encodings.
Each active worker receives one request and returns one response per synchronous iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{\mathrm{comm}}\le Kp(a+b)\) and the directed-message count is at most \(2Kp\).

notation.meaning: request and response lengths in bits
active worker count at iteration k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: encoded message lengths add across transmissions
