children.title: Distributed-Coordination Overhead
children.top_down_role: Synchronization costs arising in parallel or distributed execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed-Coordination Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-path overhead beyond useful master and subproblem computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For synchronous iteration \(k\), let \(S_{ki}\) be worker \(i\)'s useful subproblem time, \(C_k\) communication time, \(Y_k\) synchronization time, and \(Q_k\) scheduling or queueing time. The distributed subproblem phase has critical-path time \[D_k=\max_{1\le i\le p_k}S_{ki}+C_k+Y_k+Q_k.\] Its coordination overhead relative to ideal parallel useful work is therefore \(O_k=D_k-\max_i S_{ki}=C_k+Y_k+Q_k\). Across \(K\) synchronous iterations, total coordination overhead is \(\sum_{k=1}^{K}O_k\), excluding duplicated computation and hardware contention unless charged to \(Q_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordination overhead is communication, synchronization, and scheduling time beyond the slowest useful worker computation on the critical path.
assumptions_latex: Iterations use a synchronous barrier before the next master update.
The listed timing components are disjoint.

notation.meaning: useful computation time of worker i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: disjoint critical-path overhead components add

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and disjoint timing categories alone do not establish that communication, synchronization, and queueing occur serially on the critical path rather than overlap. The displayed equality therefore needs a sourced execution model or stronger hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Size Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding-size accounting for a complete finite logic-based Benders execution certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite execution certificate contains a final master solution encoding of \(A\) bits and, for every iteration \(k\), a subproblem certificate of \(L_k\) bits together with a valid master cut of \(B_k\) bits. Its total payload size is \[L_{\mathrm{cert}}=A+\sum_{k=1}^{K}(L_k+B_k).\] If \(A\le a\), \(L_k\le\ell\), and \(B_k\le b\), then \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}\le a+K(\ell+b)\). Any auxiliary data required by the chosen cut or subproblem verifier must be included in \(L_k\) or \(B_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificate size is the final master encoding plus all subproblem-certificate and cut encodings produced during the run.
assumptions_latex: Every certificate and cut has a finite binary encoding.
The verifier's required auxiliary data are included in the measured payload.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}\le a+K(\ell+b)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed execution-certificate format is model dependent. A source must establish that the listed master encoding, subproblem certificates, cuts, and auxiliary data constitute the relevant complete certificate before its size bound can be accepted.

knowledge_statements.title: Enumerative Nogood Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential iteration behavior when each learned nogood excludes only its incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=\{0,1\}^n\), consider an instance whose subproblem is infeasible for every \(x\in X\setminus\{x^\star\}\) and feasible for the unique assignment \(x^\star\). Suppose the only cut learned at an infeasible incumbent \(\bar x\) is the exact nogood \[\sum_{j:\bar x_j=0}x_j+\sum_{j:\bar x_j=1}(1-x_j)\ge1,\] which excludes \(\bar x\) and no other binary assignment. An admissible master tie-breaking order that places \(x^\star\) last forces \(2^n-1\) infeasible subproblem evaluations before finding \(x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incumbent-only nogoods can force enumeration of every wrong binary assignment, producing exponentially many subproblem evaluations.
assumptions_latex: The master domain is \(\{0,1\}^n\).
Each infeasible iteration adds only the displayed exact nogood.
Master tie-breaking may select \(x^\star\) last.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=2^n\) evaluations, including the final feasible assignment, are possible.

notation.meaning: unique assignment with a feasible subproblem

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact nogood construction and exponential enumeration scenario are internally coherent and fit a failure-boundary container, but this concrete LBBD lower-bound family has no inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Explanation Generalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration lower bound induced by explanations that eliminate few infeasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subseteq X\) be the master assignments whose subproblems are infeasible. For a cut \(c\), define its infeasible coverage by \(E(c)=\{x\in I:c(x)\text{ is violated}\}\). If every explanation cut generated during an execution satisfies \(|E(c)|\le q\), then certifying that all assignments in \(I\) are excluded requires at least \(\lceil |I|/q\rceil\) cuts, even when their covered sets are disjoint. Overlap can only increase this requirement. Thus explanations with constant coverage \(q\) yield an \(\Omega(|I|)\) worst-case iteration requirement when at most one cut is generated per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each explanation excludes at most q infeasible assignments, at least the infeasible-set size divided by q cuts are required.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
Every generated cut is valid and covers at most \(q\ge1\) members of \(I\).
At most one explanation cut is added per iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\ge\lceil |I|/q\rceil\).

notation.meaning: infeasible assignments excluded by cut c

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a covering argument yields the displayed lower bound

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The covering bound applies only when certification actually requires the generated cuts collectively to exclude every assignment in I. Ordinary optimization termination need not require that condition, and the current assumptions do not impose it. A direct source and corrected theorem hypotheses are required.

knowledge_statements.title: Understrengthened Master Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear enumeration caused by master lower bounds that remain indistinguishable on unchecked assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite set of \(N\) master assignments and let every evaluated assignment have true recourse value at least \(1\). Suppose that after any \(k<N\) evaluations, the accumulated cuts leave master lower bound \(0\) at every unchecked assignment and exclude or raise only checked assignments. Then the master cannot certify a global lower bound exceeding \(0\) until all \(N\) assignments have been evaluated. Under an admissible selection rule choosing unchecked zero-bound assignments, the decomposition requires \(N\) subproblem evaluations before it can close a positive optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If cuts improve bounds only at checked assignments, the master may have to evaluate every assignment before closing the optimality gap.
assumptions_latex: \(|X|=N<\infty\) and every true recourse value is at least \(1\).
Unchecked assignments retain master lower bound \(0\).
The stopping test requires matching valid lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=N\) subproblem evaluations may be necessary.

notation.meaning: number of subproblem evaluations before certification

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic Benders citation does not presently support this specific lower-bound construction. The claim also needs an explicit master objective and upper-bound setting to justify the asserted positive optimality gap and certification behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsound or Incomplete Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure predicates for explanations converted into logic-based Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\) be the feasible master assignments and let an explanation procedure return a cut with acceptance set \(H_e\subseteq X\). The explanation is unsound if \(F\nsubseteq H_e\), equivalently if it excludes some feasible assignment. It is incomplete at an infeasible assignment \(\bar x\notin F\) if every explanation obtainable there satisfies \(\bar x\in H_e\). Unsoundness can invalidate the final solution; incompleteness permits the same infeasible assignment to remain admissible and prevents cut-based progress unless another refinement mechanism excludes it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explanation fails if its cut removes a feasible assignment or cannot exclude the infeasible assignment that produced it.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the master-assignment domain.
Each returned explanation is translated into an acceptance set \(H_e\subseteq X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\nsubseteq H_e\) characterizes unsoundness, while \(\bar x\notin F\) and \(\bar x\in\bigcap_e H_e\) characterize local incompleteness.

notation.meaning: Assignments retained by the cut derived from explanation e.

review_flags: Exact logic-based Benders explanation soundness and completeness source is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits, but no source supports the proposed explanation semantics or the strong quantification over every obtainable explanation. The indexing set in the intersection is also unspecified.

knowledge_statements.title: Opaque or Unavailable Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate accessibility required for certified master refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a queried master assignment \(\bar x\), suppose the subproblem oracle reports infeasibility or a bound \(q\) but exposes no verifiable certificate \(w\). If the cut generator requires a map \(G(w)\) whose output is a valid master cut, then the report alone cannot justify adding \(G(w)\). The certification interface fails whenever no independently checkable \(w\) is returned and no alternative procedure constructs a cut valid for every feasible master assignment. The algorithm may retain the report heuristically, but it cannot use it as a proof-producing exclusion or optimality bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An opaque oracle conclusion cannot certify a Benders cut unless a checkable certificate or another validity-preserving derivation is available.
assumptions_latex: The master accepts only cuts whose validity can be checked independently.
The oracle report concerns a queried assignment \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absence of both a verifiable \(w\) and an alternative valid derivation prevents certified refinement of the master.

notation.meaning: Master cut derived from the certificate.

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses certificate opacity or proof-producing oracle interfaces.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits, but the proof-producing interface requirements and consequences of certificate opacity have no cited authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Projection Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss incurred when subproblem certificates are mapped into master space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W(\bar x)\) be the certificates available at a rejected assignment \(\bar x\), and let \(P:W(\bar x)\to\mathcal H\) map certificates to master acceptance sets. Projection loss occurs if every projected cut is tautological at the generating point, \(\bar x\in P(w)\) for all \(w\in W(\bar x)\), although some certificate proves that \(\bar x\) is inadmissible. More generally, a projection is certification-safe only when every feasible assignment belongs to \(P(w)\). A projection violating safety is unsound; a safe but tautological projection preserves correctness while losing the separation needed for progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection fails when a rich certificate becomes an invalid cut or a valid cut that cannot exclude its generating assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(W(\bar x)\) contains independently verifiable certificates.
\(\mathcal H\) is a family of acceptance sets over the master domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Safety requires \(F\subseteq P(w)\); useful separation additionally requires \(\bar x\notin P(w)\) for some \(w\in W(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Projection from certificates to master acceptance sets.
Certificates available at the generating assignment.

review_flags: A source formalizing certificate projection loss in logic-based Benders decomposition is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits, but certificate projection loss is introduced as a specialized formal notion without evidence. A source must support the safety and separation criteria in this logic-based Benders context.

children.title: Oracle Inaccuracy Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by unreliable oracle conclusions or objective assessments.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Inaccuracy Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary for inaccurate feasibility and value oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the true subproblem value be \(Q(x)\), with \(Q(x)=+\infty\) denoting infeasibility, and let an oracle return \(\widehat Q(x)\). A cut \(\theta\ge b(x)\) derived from that response is sound only if \(b(x)\le Q(x)\) for every master assignment where the cut applies. Oracle inaccuracy becomes a correctness failure when it causes \(b(x)>Q(x)\) somewhere, falsely labels a feasible assignment infeasible, or supplies an invalid certificate. Underestimation may preserve lower-cut validity but can weaken convergence; overestimation can remove a feasible optimum or produce a false lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle error is fatal when it creates an invalid cut, false infeasibility decision, or unjustified bound; conservative error may only weaken progress.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is the exact subproblem value function.
The master uses \(\theta\) as an epigraph variable for \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cut is valid exactly when \(b(x)\le Q(x)\) throughout its declared scope.

notation.meaning: Exact subproblem value at master assignment x.
Lower estimator used in the generated cut.

review_flags: No supplied source covers inexact logic-based Benders oracle validity conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits, but no source establishes the inexact-oracle claims. With Q(x)=+infinity for infeasibility, finite epigraph lower cuts do not themselves exclude infeasible assignments, so the relationship among value errors, feasibility reports, and generated cuts requires sourced qualification.

children.title: Oracle Availability Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by inaccessible, interrupted, or unsupported oracle services.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Availability Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progress and termination boundary when the subproblem oracle is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^k\) be a master candidate requiring subproblem evaluation. If the oracle returns neither a certified value nor a certified infeasibility result, and no fallback produces a valid cut or complete direct evaluation, then the algorithm cannot certify rejection, recourse cost, or acceptance of \(x^k\). If such an unresolved candidate can remain master-optimal, the usual termination test is unavailable: the master bound and incumbent cannot be reconciled through that candidate. Discarding it without a valid exclusion risks unsoundness, whereas retaining it may cause repeated queries or stalled search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a necessary oracle call yields no certificate and no valid fallback exists, the candidate cannot be safely accepted, rejected, or bounded.
assumptions_latex: The candidate \(x^k\) requires a subproblem result for certification.
No independent fallback solves or validly bounds that subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An unresolved master-optimal \(x^k\) prevents certified termination unless a valid fallback or exclusion is obtained.

notation.meaning: Master candidate queried at iteration k.

review_flags: An authoritative source for unavailable-oracle failure handling is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits, but the asserted inability to certify termination and the alternatives available after oracle nonresponse depend on the precise algorithm and require an authoritative source.

children.title: Hard Repeated Master or Residual Subproblem

knowledge_statements.title: Hard Repeated Master or Residual Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational boundary when decomposition leaves a repeatedly difficult optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(T_M(k)\) be the work required to reoptimize the accumulated master and \(T_S(k)\) the work required to solve the residual subproblem. For \(K\) iterations, decomposition work is at least \(\sum_{k=1}^{K}(T_M(k)+T_S(k))\). The decomposition has no computational advantage under this accounting when this sum, including interface overhead, is not smaller than the work of a direct formulation. Typical failure mechanisms are a master whose growing cut system remains intrinsically hard, or a residual subproblem retaining the original combinatorial core and being solved repeatedly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decomposition loses its computational rationale when repeated master or residual solves cost at least as much as solving the original formulation directly.
assumptions_latex: All compared runtimes use the same computational model and termination tolerance.
Interface and cut-management costs are included.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=1}^{K}(T_M(k)+T_S(k))+T_I\ge T_D\) is the stated no-advantage boundary.

notation.meaning: Master and residual-subproblem work at iteration k.

review_flags: The supplied generic decomposition locator does not establish this computational failure criterion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits, but the runtime comparison is an uncited accounting criterion rather than an established mathematical boundary. The statement calls the work at least the solve-time sum, while the conclusion separately adds interface cost; the intended cost model needs sourced specification.

knowledge_statements.title: Insufficient Decoupling or Excessive Fragmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural boundary balancing residual coupling against coordination overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the residual model into blocks \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) coupled through an interface \(S\). Insufficient decoupling occurs when conditioning on \(S\) leaves a block containing the dominant combinatorial interaction, so its solution cost remains comparable to the undecomposed residual problem. Excessive fragmentation occurs when block solution is cheap but coordinating, communicating, and aggregating certificates across \(m\) blocks dominates. Under a common work measure, the partition is counterproductive whenever \(T_{m coord}(S,m)+\sum_{i=1}^{m}T(B_i)\ge T_{m direct}\). This boundary concerns computational benefit, not the logical validity of correctly generated cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partition fails computationally when it leaves the hard coupling intact or creates coordination overhead exceeding the savings from smaller blocks.
assumptions_latex: Conditioning on the interface \(S\) defines the residual blocks.
All work terms use a common computational measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\rm coord}(S,m)+\sum_{i=1}^{m}T(B_i)\ge T_{\rm direct}\) marks a counterproductive partition.
review_flags: A source connecting partition structure to this logic-based Benders failure boundary is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits, but the structural diagnoses and aggregate runtime inequality are unsupported and depend on a defined computational model and decomposition architecture.

knowledge_statements.title: Late or Stale Cut Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and progress consequences of delayed or state-dependent cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a cut \(c_t(x)\le0\) is generated from proof state \(s_t\) and inserted at later state \(s_u\). If its validity is global, meaning \(c_t(x)\le0\) for every feasible \(x\), delayed insertion preserves soundness but may waste search performed before insertion. If validity depends on a scope predicate \(D_t(x)\), insertion is sound only when the current search region lies within \(D_t\), or when the cut is enforced conditionally on \(D_t\). Applying a stale state-dependent cut outside that scope can exclude feasible solutions and corrupt the bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A delayed globally valid cut remains sound but may be ineffective; a stale local cut used outside its generating scope can invalidate the search.
assumptions_latex: The generating and insertion states are \(s_t\) and \(s_u\), respectively.
Any state-dependent cut has an explicit validity domain \(D_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unconditional insertion is safe only if \(F\subseteq\{x:c_t(x)\le0\}\); otherwise the cut must remain restricted to \(D_t\).

notation.meaning: Validity domain of the generated cut.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports delayed and state-scoped cut integration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits, but delayed and state-dependent cut semantics are implementation-sensitive and lack a source establishing the stated safety conditions and bound-corruption consequence.

children.title: Callback-Scope Violations
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by using cuts or information outside an eligible callback context.

knowledge_statements.title: Callback-Scope Violations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-callback legality boundary for adding proof-producing cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For callback context \(s\), let \(\mathcal C_s\) denote the cuts permitted by the solver and let \(R_s\) be the relaxation or candidate state exposed to the callback. A scope violation occurs when the callback reads information not valid in \(R_s\), modifies proof state nonatomically, or submits \(c\notin\mathcal C_s\). In particular, a cut valid only for integer candidates cannot be installed as a globally valid relaxation cut unless it is valid for every feasible point admitted there. Such a violation can invalidate bounds, remove feasible solutions, or make the solver’s proof log unverifiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A callback violates scope when it uses unavailable state or adds a cut whose validity class is not permitted in that callback context.
assumptions_latex: Each callback context \(s\) has a declared readable state \(R_s\).
Each context has a declared admissible cut class \(\mathcal C_s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Proof-safe insertion requires \(c\in\mathcal C_s\) and validity of \(c\) over the domain governed by context \(s\).

notation.meaning: State legally visible in callback context s.
Cuts legally admissible in callback context s.

review_flags: Solver-specific callback semantics and an authoritative proof-safety source are needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits, but permitted callback state and cut classes are solver-specific. An authoritative solver or algorithm reference is required before these legality and proof-log claims can be reviewed reliably.

children.title: Proof-State Corruption
children.top_down_role: Loss of valid proof context during callback-driven search.

knowledge_statements.title: Proof-State Corruption
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant violation in the accumulated decomposition proof state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a minimization proof state be \(S=(L,U,\mathcal C)\), where \(L\) is the certified lower bound, \(U\) is the value of a certified feasible incumbent, and \(\mathcal C\) is the committed cut set. The state is consistent only if every \(c\in\mathcal C\) is valid for all feasible solutions and \(L\le z^*\le U\). Proof-state corruption occurs if an invalid or wrongly scoped cut is committed, a bound is updated from uncertified data, or concurrent updates produce a state violating these invariants. A termination claim based on a corrupted state is not a valid optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proof state is corrupted when committed cuts, bounds, or incumbents violate validity or the invariant that the optimum lies between certified bounds.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with optimum \(z^*\).
Committed cuts and bound updates are intended to be certificate-backed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consistency requires \(L\le z^*\le U\) and validity of every \(c\in\mathcal C\); failure of either condition corrupts the proof state.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound and incumbent upper bound.

review_flags: A source formalizing proof-state invariants for callback-driven decomposition is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits, but the proposed proof-state abstraction, concurrency invariants, and certification consequence have no cited source in callback-driven logic-based Benders decomposition.

children.title: Callback–Proof-State Synchronization
children.top_down_role: Consistency risks between callback timing plus the solver proof state.

knowledge_statements.title: Callback–Proof-State Synchronization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Versioned commit condition for asynchronous callback-generated certificates and cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate each callback observation with a proof-state version \(v\). A cut or bound update derived from that observation may be committed to current version \(v'\) only if it is globally valid independently of intervening changes, or if its assumptions and validity scope are revalidated against version \(v'\). The commit must atomically record the certificate, its scope, and the resulting state update. Consequently, every committed item has a traceable certificate valid for the state where it is used, and concurrent callbacks cannot overwrite bounds, duplicate incompatible updates, or attach a certificate to the wrong master state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A callback update is synchronized when it is globally valid or revalidated at commit time, and its certificate, scope, and state change are recorded atomically.
assumptions_latex: Proof states carry monotonically distinguishable versions \(v\).
Each proposed update records its certificate and validity scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Commit at \(v'\) is permitted only under global validity or successful revalidation at \(v'\), followed by an atomic certified update.
review_flags: Authoritative synchronization and callback proof-state semantics are not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind appropriately describes a synchronization requirement, but the versioning, revalidation, atomicity, and concurrency guarantees form an uncited protocol rather than a source-backed standard condition.

children.title: Diagram-Size Explosion
children.top_down_role: Failure regimes caused by excessive decision-diagram growth.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram-Size Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential representation boundary for ordered binary decision diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), define \(|x|=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\) and the hidden weighted-bit function by \(\operatorname{HWB}_n(x)=0\) when \(|x|=0\), and \(\operatorname{HWB}_n(x)=x_{|x|}\) otherwise. Every reduced ordered binary decision diagram representing \(\operatorname{HWB}_n\) has \(2^{\Omega(n)}\) nodes, regardless of the variable ordering. Thus ordering optimization cannot always prevent diagram-size explosion. Any decomposition interface that requires explicitly constructing such an exact diagram inherits exponential space and construction-output cost on this family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Some Boolean functions require exponentially large exact ordered decision diagrams under every variable ordering, so reordering cannot universally control interface size.
assumptions_latex: The representation is an exact reduced ordered binary decision diagram.
Diagram size is measured by the number of nonterminal nodes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{size}(\operatorname{OBDD}(\operatorname{HWB}_n,\pi))=2^{\Omega(n)}\) for every variable ordering \(\pi\).

notation.meaning: Hidden weighted-bit Boolean function on n variables.
Variable ordering of the ordered decision diagram.

review_flags: The exponential OBDD lower bound requires a precise authoritative theorem locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the container and the hidden weighted-bit claim is a theorem-level OBDD lower bound, but no source or precise theorem locator is supplied. The inherited construction-cost conclusion also requires support or explicit qualification.

children.title: Variable-Ordering Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Performance or representation failures attributable to variable ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Ordering Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of an ordered decision diagram’s representation size on its variable order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), and for each permutation \(\pi\) of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(D_\pi(F)\) be the reduced layered binary decision diagram that tests variables in order \(\pi\). Its width and node count, denoted by \(w_\pi(F)\) and \(s_\pi(F)\), are properties of the pair \((F,\pi)\), not of \(F\) alone. Consequently, two orders \(\pi\) and \(\sigma\) may represent the same feasible set exactly while satisfying \(s_\pi(F)\ll s_\sigma(F)\); for suitable families, this separation is exponential in \(n\). Thus a width or memory limit can be harmless under one order and force relaxation or restriction under another.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same feasible set can have a compact exact decision diagram under one variable order and an exponentially larger diagram under another.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is represented by reduced ordered binary decision diagrams.
Every root-to-terminal path assigns variables according to one fixed permutation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_\pi(F)\) and \(w_\pi(F)\) can depend exponentially on the chosen order \(\pi\).

notation.meaning: Reduced decision diagram for feasible set F under order pi.
Maximum number of nodes in any layer.

review_flags: Exact decision-diagram ordering theorem requires an authoritative source and explicit separating family.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf, but the exponential ordering separation is a nontrivial claim requiring an authoritative decision-diagram source and a precise separating family.

children.title: Size–Ordering Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interactions between ordering choices plus attainable diagram compactness.

knowledge_statements.title: Size–Ordering Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interaction between variable ordering, width limits, and diagram approximation quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an order \(\pi\), let \(D_\pi\) be an exact layered decision diagram and let \(W\) be an imposed width limit. If \(w_\pi\leq W\), exact compilation is possible without width reduction. If \(w_\pi>W\), maintaining the limit requires either merging states, producing a relaxed diagram with path set \(P(D_\pi)\subseteq P(D^R_{\pi,W})\), or deleting states, producing a restricted diagram with \(P(D^S_{\pi,W})\subseteq P(D_\pi)\). Because \(w_\pi\) depends on \(\pi\), minimizing exact diagram size need not maximize the bound or incumbent quality obtained after width limiting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order yielding the smallest exact diagram need not yield the strongest width-limited relaxation or the best restricted feasible solution.
assumptions_latex: All diagrams use the same variable domains and objective.
Relaxed merging preserves every exact path, while restriction retains only exact paths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The choice of \(\pi\) jointly controls compilation size and the information lost when enforcing \(W\).

notation.meaning: Set of assignments encoded by root-to-terminal paths of diagram D.
Width of the exact diagram under order pi.

review_flags: Needs a decision-diagram optimization source for the approximation-quality tradeoff.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and path-set inclusions fit, but ordering-dependent approximation quality does not follow from width sensitivity alone and needs direct decision-diagram evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Overmerged Relaxed Diagrams
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of decomposition information caused by excessive state merging in relaxed diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) encode exactly the feasible assignments \(F\), and let \(D^R\) be obtained by merging layer states so that every continuation allowed from either original state is allowed from the merged state. Then \(F=P(D)\subseteq P(D^R)\), so optimization over \(D^R\) remains a valid relaxation. If merging creates a spurious path \(z\in P(D^R)\setminus F\), however, an objective bound attained at \(z\) need not be attainable by the original subproblem. Increasing such merging can therefore preserve bound validity while making the bound, inferred conflicts, or Benders communication arbitrarily uninformative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Excessive merging preserves a valid relaxation but introduces spurious paths that can make bounds and decomposition cuts too weak to guide search.
assumptions_latex: State merging retains all continuations of every merged state.
The original diagram represents \(F\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq P(D^R)\), but strict inclusion permits valid yet arbitrarily weak relaxation information.

notation.meaning: Relaxed diagram formed by state merging.

review_flags: Needs an authoritative relaxed decision-diagram source supporting the merging semantics and weakness claim.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relaxed-diagram inclusion is plausible and the knowledge kind fits, but the claims about arbitrarily weak bounds, conflicts, and Benders communication require authoritative support.

knowledge_statements.title: Overpruned Restricted Diagrams
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certification limits created by deleting too many states or arcs from a restricted diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) encode the feasible set \(F\), and construct \(D^S\) only by deleting nodes or arcs from \(D\). Then \(P(D^S)\subseteq F\), and every surviving root-to-terminal path is a feasible solution, so its objective value is a valid incumbent bound. Nevertheless, \(P(D^S)=\varnothing\) certifies only that the retained subset is empty; it does not imply \(F=\varnothing\). Excessive pruning may remove every optimal path, or every feasible path, and therefore cannot supply a valid global infeasibility certificate or optimality lower bound without an independent relaxation or exact oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heavily pruned restricted diagram yields valid feasible solutions, but emptiness or poor quality in that subset says little about the full problem.
assumptions_latex: The exact diagram represents \(F\).
Restriction is performed solely by deleting exact nodes or arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(D^S)\subseteq F\), while \(P(D^S)=\varnothing\) does not imply \(F=\varnothing\).
review_flags: Needs a restricted decision-diagram source for the certification boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restricted-diagram inclusion and emptiness limitation are mathematically coherent and fit the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the stated certification boundary.

children.title: Decomposition Applicability Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Applicability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient finite-master regime for exact logic-based Benders decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c(x)+Q(x):x\in X\}\), where \(X\) is finite and \(Q(x)\) is the exact value of a subordinate optimization problem, with \(Q(x)=+\infty\) when it is infeasible. Logic-based Benders decomposition is exact in the following applicability regime: for every queried \(\bar x\), the subproblem oracle either returns \(Q(\bar x)\) and a globally valid optimality cut, or proves infeasibility and returns a globally valid feasibility cut; the returned cut excludes the current unsupported master outcome; and the master is solved exactly over accumulated cuts. Under these conditions, no master assignment is queried indefinitely, and termination occurs after finitely many distinct assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite exact decomposition applies when every subproblem call returns an exact result and a globally valid cut that removes the current unsupported master outcome.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and the master is solved exactly.
Every oracle result and generated cut is globally valid.
Each nonterminal cut excludes the current unsupported outcome.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates finitely with an optimal feasible solution or a valid proof of infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Exact subproblem value, extended by positive infinity for infeasibility.

children.title: Failure-Boundary Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Cross-cutting signals that an applicability limit has been reached.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure-Boundary Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic tests distinguishing invalid certificates, weak communication, and incomplete search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite master set \(X\), a subproblem oracle, generated cuts \(C_1,\ldots,C_t\), and a search log, perform: (i) oracle validation by independently checking each reported feasible value or infeasibility certificate; (ii) cut validation by checking that every known feasible pair satisfies each \(C_i\); (iii) separation validation by verifying that the outcome generating \(C_i\) violates it when continuation was required; and (iv) search validation by confirming exact master optimization and a sound stopping bound. Failure of (i) or (ii) identifies unsound certification; failure of (iii) identifies weak communication; failure of (iv) identifies incomplete search. Passing sampled checks is diagnostic evidence, not a universal correctness proof.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check oracle results, global cut validity, incumbent separation, and master stopping conditions to localize decomposition failure without treating sampling as proof.
assumptions_latex: The diagnostic has access to generated cuts and their originating master outcomes.
Independent checking procedures are available for logged oracle claims.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The first failed test classifies the observed defect as certification, communication, or search failure.
review_flags: Diagnostic taxonomy and validation protocol require a dedicated logic-based Benders source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An algorithm is appropriate for this diagnostic leaf, but the proposed validation protocol and three-way failure classification lack a dedicated source. Checking known feasible pairs alone also cannot establish global cut validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Facility Assignment with CP Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logic-based Benders template separating facility assignment from constraint-programming schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) assign job \(i\) to facility \(j\), with \(\sum_j x_{ij}=1\). The master chooses \(x\) and a schedule-cost estimate \(\theta\), subject to assignment and facility constraints. For each facility \(j\), a constraint-programming subproblem schedules \(I_j(x)=\{i:x_{ij}=1\}\) under its temporal and resource constraints. If all subproblems are feasible, update an incumbent and add valid inequalities supporting \(\theta\) at \(x\); if one is infeasible, extract an assignment conflict \(S\subseteq I_j(x)\) and add \(\sum_{i\in S}x_{ij}\leq |S|-1\). Repeat until the master lower bound meets the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master assigns jobs to facilities; CP schedules each facility and returns either schedule-cost cuts or conflict cuts excluding an infeasible assignment core.
assumptions_latex: Each CP subproblem is solved exactly.
Every returned conflict set is infeasible when assigned jointly to its facility.
All optimality cuts are globally valid lower estimators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For finite assignments, the procedure terminates exactly when every nonterminal iteration excludes its current assignment.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logic-based decomposition template for master project decisions and CP scheduling feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let activities \(V\) have precedence arcs \(E\), renewable capacities \(R_k\), and optional master decisions \(x\) selecting modes, activities, or capacity investments. The master chooses \(x\) and a makespan estimate \(\theta\). Fixing \(x=\bar x\), a constraint-programming subproblem selects start times \(s_i\) satisfying \(s_j\geq s_i+p_i(\bar x)\) for \((i,j)\in E\) and \(\sum_{i:s_i\leq t<s_i+p_i(\bar x)}r_{ik}(\bar x)\leq R_k(\bar x)\) for every resource \(k\) and time \(t\). It returns an optimal schedule and valid makespan cut, or an infeasible master-decision core whose simultaneous selection is forbidden.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master chooses project modes or capacities, while a CP subproblem enforces precedence and cumulative-resource scheduling and returns cost or conflict cuts.
assumptions_latex: The activity and master-decision sets are finite.
The CP subproblem solves the fixed-decision scheduling problem exactly.
Every returned core and makespan cut is globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Repeated exact master and subproblem solution yields a finite exact decomposition when each failed outcome is excluded.

notation.meaning: Duration of activity i under master decision x.
Consumption of resource k by activity i.

knowledge_statements.title: Machine-Assignment Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition of machine assignment decisions from machine-specific sequencing subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For jobs \(I\) and eligible machines \(M_i\), let \(x_{ik}\in\{0,1\}\) satisfy \(\sum_{k\in M_i}x_{ik}=1\). The master selects \(x\) and a scheduling-cost estimate \(\theta\). For fixed \(x=\bar x\), each machine subproblem sequences \(I_k(\bar x)=\{i:\bar x_{ik}=1\}\) subject to release dates, deadlines, and nonoverlap constraints. A feasible solution supplies an incumbent and a globally valid lower-bound cut for \(\theta\); an infeasible subproblem supplies a conflict set \(S\subseteq I_k(\bar x)\) and the cut \(\sum_{i\in S}x_{ik}\leq |S|-1\). Iteration stops when the master bound equals the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign jobs in the master, sequence each machine in a subproblem, and return either scheduling bounds or assignment-conflict cuts.
assumptions_latex: Every job has at least one eligible machine.
Machine subproblems are solved exactly.
Returned lower-bound and conflict cuts are globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scheme is finitely exact if every nonterminal iteration excludes its current assignment or strictly strengthens its value estimate.

children.title: Sequence-Dependent Scheduling

knowledge_statements.title: Sequence-Dependent Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjunctive temporal representation with predecessor-dependent setup times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a machine assignment and let \(I_k\) be the jobs assigned to machine \(k\). For distinct \(i,j\in I_k\), introduce \(y_{ijk}\in\{0,1\}\), equal to one when \(i\) precedes \(j\). With start times \(s_i\), processing times \(p_{ik}\), setup times \(q_{ijk}\), and a valid constant \(M\), nonoverlap with sequence-dependent setup is represented by \(y_{ijk}+y_{jik}=1\), \(s_j\geq s_i+p_{ik}+q_{ijk}-M(1-y_{ijk})\), and \(s_i\geq s_j+p_{jk}+q_{jik}-M(1-y_{jik})\). Additional ordering constraints must eliminate directed cycles when pairwise precedences do not already imply a total order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary precedence variables select one order for each job pair, and temporal inequalities apply the setup time associated with the selected predecessor.
assumptions_latex: All jobs in \(I_k\) require exclusive use of machine \(k\).
\(M\) is large enough to deactivate an unselected temporal inequality.
Setup time may depend on both predecessor and successor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed disjunction enforces pairwise nonoverlap and the selected sequence-dependent setup time.

notation.meaning: Indicator that job i precedes job j on machine k.
Setup time from job i to job j on machine k.

children.title: Assignment–Sequencing Coupling

knowledge_statements.title: Assignment–Sequencing Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical consistency conditions linking assignment and same-machine precedence variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{ik}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate assignment of job \(i\) to machine \(k\), and let \(y_{ijk}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that \(i\) precedes \(j\) on \(k\). Exact pairwise activation requires \(y_{ijk}\leq x_{ik}\), \(y_{ijk}\leq x_{jk}\), and \(y_{ijk}+y_{jik}\geq x_{ik}+x_{jk}-1\) for every distinct pair \(i,j\) and machine \(k\). Together with \(y_{ijk}+y_{jik}\leq 1\), these inequalities force exactly one precedence direction when both jobs use \(k\), and force both directions to zero whenever either job is assigned elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A precedence variable can activate only when both jobs share a machine, and exactly one direction must activate when they do.
assumptions_latex: Assignment and precedence variables are binary.
Each job is assigned to exactly one eligible machine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_{ijk}+y_{jik}=1\) holds exactly when \(x_{ik}=x_{jk}=1\), and otherwise both precedence variables are zero.

knowledge_statements.title: Routing with Scheduling or Congestion Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders template separating discrete route selection from operational temporal or congestion checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_a\in\{0,1\}\) select arcs satisfying the master’s routing and connectivity constraints, and let \(\theta\) estimate operational cost. For a fixed route \(\bar x\), solve a scheduling or congestion subproblem over the selected arcs, including time windows, shared-resource capacities, or flow-dependent delay constraints. If feasible, return its exact value, a feasible operational plan, and a globally valid cut lower-bounding \(\theta\). If infeasible, extract a route feature set \(S\) whose simultaneous selection causes the conflict and add a valid cut excluding every master route containing that conflicting combination. Reoptimize until the master lower bound meets the best feasible combined solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master chooses routes; an operational subproblem checks timing or congestion and returns either a value cut or a conflicting-route cut.
assumptions_latex: The master route set is finite.
Each operational subproblem is solved exactly.
Every returned optimality or conflict cut is globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decomposition terminates finitely and exactly when each nonterminal cut removes the current unsupported route outcome.

knowledge_statements.title: Network Design with Operational Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LBBD template separating binary network design from an operational feasibility-and-cost subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\), let \(x\in X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{E}\) select network elements, and let \(c\in\mathbb R^{E}\). For each design \(x\), define the operational value \(Q(x)=\inf\{d(y):y\in Y(x)\}\), with \(Q(x)=+\infty\) when \(Y(x)=\varnothing\). The integrated design problem is
\[\min_{x\in X}\;c^{\mathsf T}x+Q(x).\]
An LBBD master uses a variable \(\theta\) and accumulated valid inequalities \(\theta\ge B_k(x)\), together with feasibility cuts excluding designs certified to have \(Y(x)=\varnothing\). Each iteration solves the master, checks \(Y(\bar x)\), and adds a cut valid for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose network elements in the master, check operational feasibility and cost in a subordinate model, and add valid feasibility or cost cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{E}\) is nonempty.
For every feasible operation, \(d(y)\) is bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+Q(x)\}\) admits a design master with operational checks and valid LBBD cuts.

notation.meaning: operationally feasible decisions under design x
optimal operational value, or positive infinity if infeasible

knowledge_statements.title: Packing with Combinatorial Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Packing decisions form the master; compatibility, placement, or sequencing is checked combinatorially.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be a finite item set, let \(x\in X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{I}\) select items, and let \(p_i\) be item profits. For a selection \(x\), let \(Y(x)\) contain its feasible packings and define \(Q(x)=\inf\{g(y):y\in Y(x)\}\), where \(Q(x)=+\infty\) if no packing exists. The decomposed model is
\[\min_{x\in X}\;-\sum_{i\in I}p_i x_i+Q(x).\]
If \(Y(\bar x)=\varnothing\), any identified conflict \(C\subseteq\{i:\bar x_i=1\}\) satisfying \(Y(\mathbf1_C)=\varnothing\) yields the valid cut \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le |C|-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master selects items; a combinatorial packing model either supplies recourse cost or returns an infeasible item conflict that becomes a cut.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{I}\).
Packing feasibility is downward closed: \(Y(x)\ne\varnothing\) and \(x'\le x\) imply \(Y(x')\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every infeasible conflict \(C\) produces the valid master inequality \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le |C|-1\).

notation.meaning: feasible packings of the selected items
incidence vector of item set C

knowledge_statements.title: Facility Location with Discrete Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facility openings precede discrete assignment, routing, scheduling, or service recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J\) be candidate facilities, let \(x\in X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{J}\) denote openings, and let \(f_j\) be opening costs. For each \(x\), define a discrete recourse set \(Y(x)\subseteq\mathbb Z^m\) and
\[Q(x)=\inf\{q^{\mathsf T}y:y\in Y(x)\},\qquad \min_{x\in X}\left\{\sum_{j\in J}f_jx_j+Q(x)\right\}.\]
An LBBD master replaces \(Q(x)\) by \(\theta\) and valid logical lower bounds. If a recourse explanation identifies a facility set \(S\subseteq J\) whose closure makes service impossible, the master may impose \(\sum_{j\in S}x_j\ge1\); optimality explanations instead impose valid bounds \(\theta\ge B_k(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facility openings are first-stage decisions; a discrete service model evaluates them and returns logical feasibility or recourse-cost cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite and \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{J}\).
Every feasible recourse problem has a finite attained minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}\{f^{\mathsf T}x+Q(x)\}\) is represented by an opening master coupled to discrete recourse evaluations.

notation.meaning: discrete service decisions compatible with openings x

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity Design with Feasibility Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An oracle accepts or rejects each discrete capacity design and returns a valid explanatory cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite design set \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^n\), design cost \(c\), and an oracle \(\mathcal O\). Initialize \(K=\varnothing\). At iteration \(t\), solve \(x^t\in\arg\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X,\ g_k(x)\ge0\ \text{for all }k\in K\}\). Query \(\mathcal O(x^t)\). If it returns feasible, output \(x^t\). Otherwise it returns a predicate \(g_t\) satisfying \(g_t(x)\ge0\) for every operationally feasible \(x\) and \(g_t(x^t)<0\); set \(K\leftarrow K\cup\{t\}\). If the master becomes infeasible, certify that no feasible capacity design exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly optimize capacity cost, query an operational feasibility oracle, and add each oracle-generated valid cut until finding a feasible design or proving none exists.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^n\) is finite.
Every rejected design yields a valid cut that excludes that design.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates after at most \(|X|\) rejected designs with an optimal feasible design or an infeasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: valid feasibility-cut function returned at iteration t

knowledge_statements.title: Configuration with Constraint Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A master selects component configurations; a constraint model checks detailed compatibility and performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) index components, let \(K_i\) be the finite options for component \(i\), and let \(x_{ik}\in\{0,1\}\) satisfy \(\sum_{k\in K_i}x_{ik}=1\). Write \(x\in X\) for all master-level configuration rules. A constraint subproblem has variables \(y\in D\), constraints \(C(x,y)\), and value
\[Q(x)=\inf\{h(y):y\in D,\ C(x,y)\}.\]
The integrated problem is \(\min_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+Q(x)\}\). An infeasible constraint explanation involving selected literals \(L\) yields the no-good cut \(\sum_{(i,k)\in L}x_{ik}\le |L|-1\); stronger explanations may replace \(L\) by a smaller conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master chooses one option per component; a constraint subproblem checks detailed compatibility and converts conflicts into no-good or strengthened cuts.
assumptions_latex: Each option set \(K_i\) is finite.
The constraint solver returns a sound conflict when \(C(\bar x,y)\) is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A sound conflict \(L\) yields the valid cut \(\sum_{(i,k)\in L}x_{ik}\le |L|-1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Decomposed Discrete Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario recourse separates once the common first-stage discrete decision is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be a finite scenario set with probabilities \(p_s>0\) and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\). For \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\), define discrete scenario recourse
\[Q_s(x)=\inf\{q_s(y_s):y_s\in Y_s(x)\},\qquad Q(x)=\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x).\]
With \(Q_s(x)=+\infty\) for infeasible recourse, the two-stage problem is \(\min_{x\in X}\{c(x)+Q(x)\}\). An LBBD master may use variables \(\theta_s\) and independent valid cuts \(\theta_s\ge B_{sk}(x)\); scenario feasibility cuts are imposed directly on the common decision \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing the shared first-stage decision separates discrete recourse by scenario, allowing independent scenario evaluations and cuts in a common master.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite with \(p_s>0\) and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
Each feasible scenario subproblem has a finite attained value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x)=\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x)\), so scenario subproblems and their LBBD cuts separate conditional on \(x\).

notation.meaning: optimal discrete recourse value in scenario s

children.title: Stochastic Planning Templates
children.top_down_role: Templates placing uncertain strategic or tactical planning decisions in the master layer.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Planning Templates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strategic planning decisions are shared across scenarios, while operational plans provide scenario-specific discrete recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) be a planning decision chosen before a finite scenario \(s\in S\) is observed. Let \(p_s\) be its probability and let
\[Q_s(x)=\min\{q_s^{\mathsf T}y_s:y_s\in Y_s(x)\subseteq\mathbb Z^{m_s}\}.\]
The risk-neutral stochastic planning template is
\[\min_{x\in X}\;c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x).\]
The LBBD master contains \(x\) and scenario estimates \(\theta_s\). For each incumbent \(\bar x\), scenario planning subproblems generate valid feasibility cuts on \(x\) or optimality cuts \(\theta_s\ge B_{sk}(x)\), which are accumulated across iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common strategic plan is evaluated by scenario-specific discrete operational plans, whose feasibility and costs generate separate LBBD cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(p_s>0\) with \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
Each feasible \(Y_s(x)\) has an attained finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The expected recourse objective is represented by \(c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x)\) with scenario-indexed LBBD cuts.

master estimate of scenario-s recourse value

children.title: Stochastic Scheduling Templates

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Scheduling Templates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared resource or assignment choices precede scenario-specific scheduling decisions and temporal feasibility checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) encode assignments or resource commitments made before scenario revelation. For each \(s\in S\), let \(Y_s(x)\) be the set of schedules satisfying scenario-dependent durations, precedences, and capacities, and define \(Q_s(x)=\inf\{h_s(y_s):y_s\in Y_s(x)\}\). The stochastic scheduling problem is
\[\min_{x\in X}\;c(x)+\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s(x).\]
When \(Y_s(\bar x)=\varnothing\), a sound temporal or resource conflict yields a feasibility cut on \(x\); otherwise a valid lower-bounding function \(B_{sk}\) yields \(\theta_s\ge B_{sk}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-stage assignments or resources are checked by scenario-specific scheduling models, which return temporal conflicts or schedule-cost cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite with probability vector \(p\).
Each subproblem solver returns sound conflicts and valid cost lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scenario scheduling checks define \(Q_s(x)\) and generate valid scenario-indexed feasibility or optimality cuts.

notation.meaning: feasible schedules in scenario s under master decision x
optimal scheduling cost in scenario s
scenario-s recourse lower bound generated at iteration k

children.title: Scenario-Coupling Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces linking shared decisions to scenario-specific operational evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Coupling Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonanticipativity specifies exactly which decisions must agree across scenarios sharing the same observed history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be a finite scenario set and let \(h_t(s)\) denote the information history observed through stage \(t\) in scenario \(s\). For scenario-indexed decisions \(z_{t,s}\), the scenario-coupling interface is the nonanticipativity condition
\[h_t(s)=h_t(s')\ \Longrightarrow\ z_{t,s}=z_{t,s'}\qquad\text{for all }t\text{ and }s,s'\in S.\]
Equivalently, partition \(S\) into information classes \(\mathcal P_t\); then introduce one master variable \(z_{t,C}\) for each \(C\in\mathcal P_t\) and substitute \(z_{t,s}=z_{t,C}\) whenever \(s\in C\). Conditional on these shared variables, scenario subproblems may be solved independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decisions agree between scenarios until their observed histories diverge; representing each information class by one master variable preserves scenario separability.
assumptions_latex: All scenarios use a common finite stage index set.
The history map \(h_t\) determines the information available when stage-t decisions are made.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonanticipativity holds exactly when \(z_{t,s}\) is constant on every information class \(C\in\mathcal P_t\).

notation.meaning: information history of scenario s through stage t
partition of scenarios by identical stage-t histories
decision shared by scenarios in information class C

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonanticipativity condition is standard, precise, and appropriately classified as a condition. No citation is supplied, however, and the additional claim that conditioning on information-class master variables makes the scenario subproblems independent depends on the rest of the model containing no other cross-scenario coupling. An authoritative multistage stochastic-programming source and support for the LBBD interface claim are required.

children.title: Robust Subproblem Templates
children.top_down_role: Templates using subordinate checks over prescribed uncertainty sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Subproblem Templates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A design is evaluated against its worst admissible uncertainty realization and corresponding operational response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in X\) be a discrete design, let \(U\) be a nonempty uncertainty set, and let \(Y(x,u)\) be the feasible operational responses to realization \(u\). Define
\[Q(x,u)=\inf\{q(x,y,u):y\in Y(x,u)\},\qquad R(x)=\sup_{u\in U}Q(x,u).\]
The robust design problem is \(\min_{x\in X}\{c(x)+R(x)\}\), with \(R(x)=+\infty\) if some \(u\in U\) has no feasible response. A worst-case subproblem at \(\bar x\) returns either such an infeasible realization or a maximizer \(\bar u\); its explanation produces a valid feasibility cut or a lower bound \(\theta\ge B_{ar u}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each design, maximize optimal operating cost over admissible uncertainty; worst-case realizations generate robust feasibility or cost cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is nonempty.
Whenever \(Y(x,u)\ne\varnothing\), the operational infimum is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust recourse is represented by \(R(x)=\sup_{u\in U}Q(x,u)\) and enforced through worst-case subproblem cuts.

notation.meaning: optimal operational value for design x and realization u

children.title: Adversarial Subproblem Templates
children.top_down_role: Templates using subordinate searches for damaging realizations or counterexamples.

knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial Subproblem Templates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An adversarial oracle searches for the uncertainty realization most violating feasibility or the current recourse bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a design set \(X\), uncertainty set \(U\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and operational value \(Q(x,u)\). Initialize \(U_0\subseteq U\). At iteration \(k\), solve a master over \(x\in X\) and \(\theta\) enforcing cuts for realizations in \(U_k\), obtaining \((x^k,\theta^k)\). Solve the adversarial problem \(u^k\in\arg\max_{u\in U}Q(x^k,u)\). If \(Q(x^k,u^k)\le\theta^k+\varepsilon\) and all responses are feasible, output \(x^k\). Otherwise add \(u^k\) and a valid feasibility or optimality explanation to the master, set \(U_{k+1}=U_k\cup\{u^k\}\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate between design optimization and an adversary that finds a worst realization; stop when no realization violates feasibility or the recourse bound beyond tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Each master problem and adversarial maximization is solved globally.
Every returned explanation is valid for all \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(\sup_{u\in U}Q(x^k,u)\le\theta^k+\varepsilon\), with robust feasibility certified separately.

notation.meaning: uncertainty realizations accumulated through iteration k
adversarial realization found at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind, but no source is supplied. The argmax step additionally requires worst-case attainment or an approximate-oracle formulation, and the record gives no finite-scenario or convergence assumptions ensuring that repetition reaches the stated stopping condition. The conditional certificate at actual termination is plausible, but the algorithmic version cannot be accepted without authoritative sourcing and the missing conditions.

children.title: Uncertainty-Set Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural variants induced by finite, budgeted, polyhedral, or combinatorial uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertainty-Set Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite, compact, and decision-dependent uncertainty sets induce distinct worst-case oracle and convergence requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For robust recourse \(R(x)=\sup_{u\in U(x)}Q(x,u)\), distinguish three regimes. The finite regime satisfies \(|U(x)|<\infty\) and permits enumeration or finite scenario generation. The compact continuous regime has nonempty compact \(U(x)\subseteq\mathbb R^d\); a worst-case realization is guaranteed when \(u\mapsto Q(x,u)\) is upper semicontinuous. The decision-dependent regime allows \(U(x)\) to vary with \(x\), so a realization generated at \(\bar x\) yields a globally valid master cut only when its explanation remains valid for every design to which that cut is applied. Empty uncertainty sets require an explicit modeling convention and are excluded here.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite sets support scenario generation; compact continuous sets need attainment conditions; decision-dependent sets require cuts whose validity accounts for the changing uncertainty domain.
assumptions_latex: For every admissible \(x\), \(U(x)\ne\varnothing\).
In the compact regime, \(Q(x,\cdot)\) is upper semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under compactness and upper semicontinuity, \(R(x)=\max_{u\in U(x)}Q(x,u)\); decision dependence additionally requires globally valid cut explanations.

notation.meaning: recourse value under design x and realization u

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite, compact, and decision-dependent distinctions fit the leaf, and compactness plus upper semicontinuity correctly gives worst-case attainment for each fixed x. No sources are supplied for these regimes or for the more specialized global-validity requirement under decision-dependent uncertainty, so authoritative citations with specific locators are required.

knowledge_statements.title: MIP Master with CP Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logic-based Benders template with a mixed-integer master and an exact constraint-programming recourse oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x+Q(x):x\in X\}\), initialize a MIP master with \(x\in X\), a variable \(\eta\), and any valid lower bound on \(Q\). At iteration \(k\), solve the master to obtain \((x^k,\eta^k)\). Fix \(x=x^k\) in the CP subproblem. If it is feasible, compute \(Q(x^k)\) and a MIP-representable logic-based cut \(\eta\ge L_k(x)\) satisfying \(L_k(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(L_k(x^k)=Q(x^k)\). If it is infeasible, add a valid MIP-representable exclusion cut derived from a CP conflict. Stop when the incumbent upper bound equals the master lower bound; return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve a MIP master, evaluate its assignment by constraint programming, and add globally valid optimality or conflict cuts until the master and incumbent bounds coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is MIP-representable and the master is solved globally at every iteration.
The CP oracle decides feasibility and computes \(Q(x^k)\) exactly.
Every returned cut is globally valid and expressible in the MIP master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon finite termination with equal bounds, the returned incumbent \(\bar x\) satisfies \(c^{\mathsf T}\bar x+Q(\bar x)=\min_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+Q(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: Master-feasible set for the complicating variables.
Optimal CP-subproblem value, extended to positive infinity when infeasible.
Master variable underestimating the subproblem value.

knowledge_statements.title: MIP Master with Combinatorial Subproblem

An infeasible response supplies a valid exclusion cut. Terminate when the best feasible objective equals the master bound.

knowledge_statements.title: MIP Master with Decision-Diagram Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logic-based Benders template using an exact decision diagram as the subproblem optimization oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x+Q(x):x\in X\}\). Maintain a MIP master in \((x,\eta)\) with accumulated lower-bounding cuts. After obtaining \(x^k\), restrict an exact decision diagram so its source-to-terminal paths represent precisely the subproblem solutions compatible with \(x^k\). If no such path exists, extract a valid MIP-representable exclusion cut. Otherwise optimize path weight to obtain \(Q(x^k)\) and extract a MIP-representable cut \(\eta\ge L_k(x)\), where \(L_k(x)\le Q(x)\) for all \(x\in X\) and \(L_k(x^k)=Q(x^k)\). Repeat until the incumbent upper bound equals the master lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The MIP master proposes assignments; an exact decision diagram evaluates compatible paths and yields valid exclusion or tight lower-bounding cuts until the bounds coincide.
assumptions_latex: The decision diagram exactly represents all feasible subproblem solutions and their objective values.
\(X\) and every extracted cut are MIP-representable.
Master and decision-diagram optimizations are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At bound equality, the returned incumbent \(\bar x\) attains \(\min_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+Q(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: Optimal compatible source-to-terminal path value, or positive infinity if no path exists.

knowledge_statements.title: Non-MIP Master with Optimization Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized logic-based Benders template allowing a non-MIP master and an arbitrary exact optimization subproblem.

The subproblem oracle computes \(Q(x^k)\) exactly or certifies infeasibility.
All generated cuts are globally valid and representable in the chosen master formalism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the incumbent and master bounds agree, the returned \(\bar x\) solves \(\min_{x\in X}\{f(x)+Q(x)\}\) globally.
